This surah begins the group of the Ha Mim surahs, meaning the surahs that open with the words *Ha Mim*. We say *al-Hawamim* in the plural, though this plural is not the usual rule. The more correct form is *Al Ha Mim*. *Ha Mim* is among the disjointed letters (*al-muqatta'at*) that occur at the openings of surahs. We have discussed them at more than one place before. In truth, we only circle around their meanings, to the extent that we can understand and derive them. In the end, everyone says: Allah knows best what He intends, because their meanings are beyond full comprehension.

We have said that a letter has a name and a referent. We say *alif* for the letter (أ) and *ba'* for the letter (ب). This is the name of the letter. As for the referent, if you say, for example, *kataba* (كتب), I do not pronounce it as *kaf-ta'-ba'*. Rather, I pronounce it *kataba*, and this is the referent. The referent of *kaf* is *ka*, the referent of *ta'* is *ta*, and the referent of *ba'* is *ba*. So in our speech we pronounce the referents of letters.

But in *Ha Mim* we pronounce the names of the letters, so we say *Ha Mim* (ح م). If we pronounced the referents, we would say *hamma*. Here lies the importance of oral transmission (*al-sama'*) in Qur'an recitation. Through transmission, at the beginning of al-Baqarah, (الم) is recited as *alif lam mim*. Yet the same letters are recited in Surat al-Sharh, ﴿Did We not expand for you your breast?﴾ [al-Sharh: 1], and without transmission we would not know this pronunciation.

Some scholars began circling around the meanings of these letters at the openings of surahs. They said: the Qur'an is a miracle for the Arab people. Since the Arabs excelled in eloquence and clarity of expression, the miracle came from the same kind as that in which they excelled, so that the inimitability (*i'jaz*) would be in its proper place. Otherwise, there is no nation among the nations that made the word into markets and fairs as the Arabs did at Ukaz, al-Mirbad, Dhu al-Majaz and others. The Qur'an's challenge to them was itself a testimony to their superiority in this field and that they were a proof in it.

But from where does the inimitability of the Qur'an come? And by what is it distinguished from the speech of the Arabs, when the letters are the letters and the words are the words?

They said: the letters of a language include letters of structure (*huruf mabna*), meaning letters that build a word, and these letters have no meaning in themselves. And there are letters of meaning (*huruf ma'na*), which have a meaning on their own. For example, *kaf* is a letter of structure because it enters into the construction of the word *kataba*. If you took the *kaf* from *kataba*, it would have no meaning on its own. But the *kaf* in *al-jundi ka-al-asad* (the soldier is like the lion) is a letter of meaning, which by itself conveys the meaning of comparison, and it does not enter into the structure of the word *al-asad*. Likewise, *ba'* is a letter of structure in *kataba*, and a letter of meaning in *bi-Allah* (by Allah), because it conveys the meaning of an oath.

From these letters words are formed, from words sentences and phrases are formed, and phrases form style and distinctive, attractive expression that captivates the ear and affects the soul. Here lies the eloquence and clarity of speech when it conforms to the rules of the language. If the Arabic letters and words are the very same in the Qur'an, then by what is it distinguished from the speech of the Arabs? They said: it is distinguished by its special weave, and by the fact that the One who spoke it is Allah, glory be to Him.

We have said before that if we want to test a group of weavers for the quality and fineness of their cloth, it is not right to give one of them wool, another cotton, and another silk, because the raw material differs and we cannot tell which is finest. Rather, the material must be the same so that the distinction can be made.

So the meaning of ﴿Ha Mim. The revelation of the Book is from Allah, the Mighty, the All-Knowing﴾ [Ghafir: 1-2], or ﴿Ha Mim. By the clear Book﴾ [al-Dukhan: 1-2], or ﴿Alif Lam Mim. This is the Book about which there is no doubt...﴾ [al-Baqarah: 1-2], is that from these letters the Qur'an was composed, and this gave it the secret of inimitability and challenge. This is because Allah, the Exalted, is the One who spoke it and conveyed it through His Messenger (ﷺ), who was unlettered (*ummi*) and could neither read nor write.

For this reason, he recited the Qur'an exactly as it was revealed to him and did not change a single letter of it. Therefore unlettered-ness was a defect and a disgrace for others, but for the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) it was an honour and a distinction. It is as if he were saying by his unlettered-ness: I learned nothing from anyone, and all my knowledge is from my Lord.

Likewise, the whole nation was an unlettered, nomadic people, not knowing civilisation and not governed by a general law. If the Arab nation at that time had been a civilised nation, they would have said of Islam that it was a civilisational leap. But Islam came in the Arabian Peninsula, where they were a Bedouin people with no law or constitution to govern them except the law of the tribe and its tribal solidarity (*'asabiyya*). The ruler among them was the tribal sheikh. Their houses were on the backs of their camels. Wherever they found pasture, they alighted and pitched their tents, and wherever they found water, they settled beside it. They were not tied to any homeland or place.

Not to mention the tribal conflicts among them and the wars that broke out over the slightest causes. You know, for example, the War of Dahis and al-Ghabra, which lasted forty years among them. Therefore, when the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) wished the newborn state to have an army, he did not open a school to teach the arts of fighting and war, because they were a nation that mastered these arts perfectly, and the Arab by nature is ready for war whenever he hears a cry for help (*ha'ya*), and rushes to it.

So, how could such a nation, described in this way, lead the whole world and conquer the lands of the earth?

It is as if Allah, the Exalted, wanted to prepare them to travel across the earth, guiding Allah's creation, without being tied to anything. Then He sent among them the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), who made slaves into masters, and shepherds of sheep into leaders and beacons for all nations. So the Arab nation was prepared, in its language, unlettered-ness and Bedouin character, to lead the civilised world, so that everyone would know that what Muhammad brought was not from human beings, but from Allah.

Let us return to the matter of the disjointed letters. These may come as a single letter, such as (ق، ص), as two letters, such as (طس، حم), as three letters, such as (طسم، الم), as four letters, such as (المص، المر), or as five letters, such as (كهيعص). So they do not follow one pattern.

When we reflect on the totality of these letters, we find that they are fourteen, which is half of the twenty-eight letters of the alphabet. The fact that they come in exactly half indicates that this is intended and did not come about by chance. The evidence for these fourteen letters is that they are used in a way that suggests they have a purpose and wisdom, and did not come arbitrarily. Of the twenty-eight letters, nine from the first, from *alif* and *ba'* to the letter *dhal*, were taken in the disjointed letters only two: *alif* and *ha'*. The rest were left out. These are seven letters.

Then consider the last nine letters, and you will find that Allah, glory be to Him, took seven of them and left two, in contrast to the first group. He took from them: *qaf*, *kaf*, *lam*, *mim*, *nun*, *ha'* and *ya'*, and left *fa'* and *waw*. These are eighteen letters in total. There remain the ten letters in the middle, from *ra'* to *ghain*.

We also note that among these letters He took the unpointed letters and left the pointed ones. He took *ra'* and left *zay*, took *sin* and left *shin*, took *sad* and left *dad*, took *ta'* and left *za'*, and took *ayn* and left *ghayn*.

So this system in the disjointed letters shows that they do not follow a single pattern, that they have an intended wisdom, and that they did not come arbitrarily. It is for us to derive these wisdoms and understand these indications, each according to what is made easy for him. We are still (searching) in these letters, hoping that we will reach something.

But your seeking wisdom is a praiseworthy effort. You may also rest your mind and take them from Allah as they are, just as you take a key, for example, from the one who made the lock. It does not matter whether it has one, two, three or four teeth. What matters is that it opens for you, and the secret of the key lies with the one who made it.

But the mind may find comfort in certain things. How?

They said: Allah, the Exalted, wants three things in His religion: beliefs, rulings, and the material that conveys these beliefs and rulings, which is His speech in the Qur'an. Each of these three has an unseen (*ghayb*) aspect and a witnessed (*mashhad*) aspect.

As for beliefs, the first of which is belief in Allah, it is unseen, but you can reach it and infer it from the witnessed things of His creation and the magnificence of His craftsmanship and design in the visible universe. For no one has claimed to have created this marvellous universe, nor attributed it to himself. So it belongs to Allah alone. Thus we affirm this unseen by means of the witnessed. As for the unseen that has no witnessed aspect, such as the attributes of Allah, the Exalted, we take them from what we hear of His speech.

Likewise, the obligations and rulings have a witnessed aspect and an unseen aspect. Prayer, almsgiving, pilgrimage and fasting are all witnessed, and they have an unseen aspect whose wisdom we do not yet know. Prayer is a means of walking the path of servitude, fasting is the continuation of the obligation, almsgiving is for circulating wealth in society, and pilgrimage is for declaring loyalty to the House, which is the House of Allah. These are things you can know by reason. But what is the wisdom, for example, of making the dawn prayer two units, the noon prayer four, the afternoon prayer four, the sunset prayer three, and the night prayer four? We do not know this.

So with every unseen there is a witnessed aspect, and with every witnessed aspect there is an unseen. Likewise, the speech of Allah, the Exalted, has an unseen and a witnessed aspect. The witnessed aspect is the speech that we know, recite, hear, write, and understand its meaning and interpretation. Its unseen aspect is as in (الم، ن، ق، ص).

So every unseen is guarded by a witnessed thing that helps us believe in the unseen, because if all matters were witnessed, there would be no room for faith. Now, you and I are sitting in a session of knowledge in the mosque of Sheikh Sulayman. Is this witnessed scene a place of faith for us? No, it is simply something witnessed. Faith is situated in the unseen. Therefore Allah, the Exalted, said: ﴿who believe in the unseen...﴾ [al-Baqarah: 3].

But this unseen must have evidences from what is witnessed and an introduction that leads to it. Have you considered, for example, the journey of the Night Journey and Ascension (al-Isra' wal-Mi'raj)? This is an unseen matter that no one saw except our master, the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ). The Night Journey was a journey on earth, and the Ascension was a journey in the heavens. People witnessed the landmarks on the earth, but did not witness what is in the heavens.

Therefore, when our master, the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), wanted to give them proof of his truthfulness, he described to them landmarks he had seen on the earth. He described Bayt al-Maqdis to them, and the caravan he had seen travelling, and when it would arrive, and that it had a camel of such and such a description. This was an earthly journey upon which proof could be established.

By his truthfulness (ﷺ) concerning what he reported of earthly witnessed matters, this journey became a witnessed event and a means of affirming witnessed matters that contradict the familiar laws. So if he reports that he ascended to the heavens, then believe him, and take from his truthfulness in what is witnessed a proof of his truthfulness in what is unseen. For every unseen, as we have said, is guarded by a witnessed thing.

Then Allah, glory be to Him, says:

﴿The revelation of the Book is from Allah...﴾.

The root nzl ("to descend") appears in the Qur'an in several forms: anzalna, nazzalna, tanzil, and nazala. All of them carry the sense of height in the thing that is sent down, and the quality of height indicates that what is sent down is not the product of human making. It also indicates the greatness and high station of what is sent down, even if it comes from the earth and not from the sky, as the Exalted said in al-Hadid: ﴿And We sent down iron, wherein is great might and benefits for mankind﴾ [al-Hadid: 25].

It is known that iron is extracted from the earth and does not descend from the sky. So the meaning is: We sent it down as a gift from the High to the low, and the higher must necessarily be greater than the lower. We say the same even in rulings and laws, when we wish to legislate and codify laws.

Do not abandon the laws of the Highest and take up the laws of the lowest, because the Highest Legislator, glory be to Him, is not like a legislator from among humans. However much knowledge and wisdom a human attains, he will not be free of desire, and he will not be exempt from some purpose. If he is wealthy, he legislates for capitalism; if he is poor, he legislates for communism.

For this reason, it is required of one who legislates that he have no desire, that he not benefit from what he legislates, and that he encompass all matters such that nothing is added to him and he does not forget any particular detail of the subject. All of these conditions are found only in the Truth, glory be to Him. Therefore it is not permissible for us to abandon the law of God and His sharia and resort to the law of humans...

As for the word (al-Kitab), that is: the Qur'an. God named it "Kitab" because it is written, and "Qur'an" because it is recited. Or it is "Kitab" as a notification that it is to be written, and "Qur'an" as a notification that it is to be read. Reading is either from the lines (written text) or from the memorizing hearts. He named it "Wahy" (revelation) because it was revealed to His Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace: ﴿It is not but a revelation revealed﴾ [al-Najm: 4]. So every naming has its own point.

When they wished to compile the Qur'an, they stipulated that both hearts and written lines agree on it. They did not write down a single verse unless they found it written on pieces (of leather or bone) and two witnesses testified to its authenticity. May God have mercy on our master Shaykh Muhammad Abdullah Draz, who linked this matter with the Exalted's words: ﴿That if one of them errs, the other will remind her﴾ [al-Baqarah: 282].

Then He, glory be to Him, says: ﴿From God, the Mighty, the Knowing﴾ [Ghafir: 2]. So this Book is sent down from God, who is characterized by absolute perfection, and He has absolute freedom of power, absolute freedom of wisdom, absolute freedom of mercy, and absolute freedom of being the Most Merciful. Since the Book came from One with these attributes, it is impossible for anything to be added to it. And since nothing can be added to it, believe the verse: ﴿Today I have perfected for you your religion, completed My favor upon you, and have approved for you Islam as a religion﴾ [al-Ma'idah: 3].

For this reason we are amazed at those who now call for the "modernization" of Islam, and we say to them: instead of modernizing Islam, make the age religious (dayyinu al-'asr).

As for the attribute (al-'Aziz), that is: the Victorious who cannot be overcome. Since this Book was sent down by the Mighty who is not overcome, this Book must rise, must be spread, and people must hear it; no one can overcome it, because its Sender is Mighty, and because God, exalted is He, would not have sent a Messenger with it and then abandoned or forsaken it. However much they oppose it, however much they become arrogant and deny, this Qur'an will prevail, and it will never be overcome in any field whatsoever.

The Almighty wills that His creation never be separated from Him, no matter how great their sins or how dominant their desires. He wants to draw them back to Himself and gather them in His presence. For this reason He opened the door of repentance and forgiveness for them, and extended the hand of pardon and forbearance. Then He showed them the staff of punishment, so that they would not become deluded. This approach benefits the whole universe and the individual in particular, for if the sinner knew that his sin would never be forgiven, he would persist in it, increase in it, act wantonly in the universe and cause corruption. At that point, society would suffer because of him, especially the people of faith.

For this reason, this verse is among the most hopeful verses in the Noble Qur'an, as He, glorified is He, said at the end of Surat az-Zumar: ﴿Say: "O My servants who have transgressed against themselves, do not despair of the mercy of Allah. Indeed, Allah forgives all sins. Indeed, it is He who is the Forgiving, the Merciful."﴾ [az-Zumar: 53].

We have said that this verse and similar ones do not contradict His saying: ﴿Indeed, Allah does not forgive association with Him, but He forgives what is less than that for whom He wills...﴾ [an-Nisa': 48], because disbelief (kufr) is not a sin. A sin (dhanb) is to oppose a command or prohibition from the Supreme Legislator, glorified is He. As for associating partners with Allah, it is an exit from faith altogether, so the one who does it is not called a sinner.

The Almighty often reminds His servants of His forgiveness and His acceptance of repentance, so that no one despairs of His mercy, exalted is He. His saying: ﴿Say: "O My servants who have transgressed against themselves, do not despair of the mercy of Allah..."﴾ [az-Zumar: 53] was not uttered except where there was someone who had transgressed against himself and despaired of his Lord's mercy, because he had gone to extremes in sins until he thought they would never be forgiven.

Among these was Wahshi, the slayer of our master Hamzah. After he killed him, he felt the weight of his sin and the enormity of his crime, and became certain that he was doomed and that Allah would not forgive him. Therefore some say that he went to the Messenger of Allah to ask him about this matter, and so on and so forth. But the reality is that he was in Makkah, and the verse was revealed in Madinah, yet it was conveyed to him, and when he heard it he believed and embraced Islam.

It is narrated that Wahshi met the Prophet (ﷺ), and the Prophet (ﷺ) said to him: "I did not wish to see you, unless you came seeking protection, and my Lord says: ﴿And if any of the polytheists seeks your protection, then grant him protection until he hears the words of Allah, then convey him to his place of safety...﴾" [at-Tawbah: 6].

He said: "I seek your protection until I hear the words of Allah." So the Messenger of Allah recited to him: ﴿Say: "O My servants who have transgressed against themselves, do not despair of the mercy of Allah. Indeed, Allah forgives all sins. Indeed, it is He who is the Forgiving, the Merciful."﴾ [az-Zumar: 53].

He said: "But Allah says: ﴿except for one who repents, believes, and does righteous deeds...﴾ [al-Furqan: 70], and I cannot guarantee that I will do righteous deeds." So the Messenger of Allah recited to him this verse: ﴿Forgiver of sin, Acceptor of repentance, Severe in punishment, Possessor of bounty...﴾ [Ghafir: 3].

Among those who were struck by despair of Allah's mercy was Ayyash ibn Abi Rabi'ah. It is narrated that when our master Umar (may Allah be pleased with him) wished to emigrate, he agreed with Ayyash and Hisham ibn al-'As ibn Wa'il as-Sahmi that they would emigrate together and gather at the well of Ghifar. If one of them were detained, the others would wait for him. When the appointed time came, Ayyash did not arrive, for his family had detained him from emigrating and then subjected him to trial, and he was tried and did not emigrate with his two companions, so despair of Allah's mercy befell him.

When this verse was revealed: ﴿Say: "O My servants who have transgressed against themselves, do not despair of the mercy of Allah"﴾ [az-Zumar: 53], Umar remembered his companion Ayyash, who had been tried, and remembered that he had met with him on faith one day, and that he had intended to emigrate, but his family tried him. His heart softened for him, and he sent him this verse so that he would be reassured and return to faith.

The saying of the Almighty: ﴿Forgiver of sin﴾ [Ghafir: 3], i.e., of what has passed; ﴿Acceptor of repentance﴾ [Ghafir: 3], i.e., of the sin that one turns to anew; ﴿Severe in punishment﴾ [Ghafir: 3], for wisdom. The Almighty combines forgiveness and punishment so that people do not rely on Him passively and do not become deluded by the mercy of Allah. Religion rests on fear and hope, and they are like the two wings of a bird; both are necessary together. ﴿Possessor of bounty﴾ [Ghafir: 3], as you say, meaning "his hand is long" (iyduh tawilah), he does what He wills. Allah is the Possessor of bounty, i.e., the Lord of grace and favour, who gives and bestows upon whom He wills, and none can repel His giving. Therefore it is related in the supplication: "There is no giver of what You withhold, and no withholder of what You give."

When the Almighty says: ﴿The revelation of the Book is from Allah, the Mighty, the All-Knowing﴾ [Ghafir: 2], we understand from the word "revelation" (tanzil) the loftiness of the One who sends down, the intermediary, the one to whom it is sent down, and the people to whom it is sent down, so that it becomes a method for the movement of their lives. This loftiness arises because the Book is from Allah, the Necessarily Existing, who possesses absolute perfection, in our saying "There is no god but Allah" and "Allah is greater" above everything, which we explained in His saying: ﴿To Him belong the keys of the heavens and the earth﴾ [az-Zumar: 63].

So "There is no god but Allah" is a key (miqlad), "Allah is greatest" is a key, "Glory be to Allah" is a key, "Praise be to Him" is a key, "We seek Allah's forgiveness" is a key, "There is no power nor strength except with Allah" is a key, He is the First, a key; He is the Last, a key; He is the Manifest, a key; He is the Hidden, a key; in His hand is all good, a key; and He is over all things capable, a key. You will not find anything in Allah's dominion that goes beyond these keys, and everything in them is in the hand of Allah, as He, glorified is He, said: ﴿And with Him are the keys of the unseen; none knows them but He﴾ [al-An'am: 59].

After that the Almighty spoke, saying ﴿the Mighty﴾ [Ghafir: 2], i.e., regarding His creation. The Mighty is the One who overcomes and is not overcome. This is an indication that when Allah sends down a Book upon a Messenger, no one will be able to stand against this Book, for He is the Overcomer who is not overcome. His saying ﴿the All-Knowing﴾ [Ghafir: 2], i.e., He places things in their proper places, knowing that they will perform their function with their righteousness.

Then He reassured His creatures who had transgressed against themselves in some matters, mentioning in ﴿Forgiver of sin and Acceptor of repentance﴾ [Ghafir: 3] the clearing (al-takhliyah) of the way, but He, glorified is He, together with His forgiveness of sin and acceptance of repentance, is ﴿Severe in punishment, Possessor of bounty; there is no god but He; to Him is the final return﴾ [Ghafir: 3], so He gathered in this verse all His attributes of majesty and all His attributes of beauty.

From "there is no god but He" we understand that no one may object to anything in His saying ﴿to Him is the final return﴾ [Ghafir: 3]; there is no recourse and no turning back except to Him.

Then Allah, glorified is He, says to His Messenger (ﷺ):

﴿None dispute concerning the signs of Allah except those who disbelieve...﴾.

The Messenger (ﷺ) came as a messenger from God, bringing what would lift the Jahiliyyah (the age of ignorance before Islam) to the station of knowledge of God. Through this, the movement of their life is purified of everything that causes vibration in the universe, or everything that causes conflict in it, until the whole universe becomes mutually supportive and reinforcing, such that one thing does not build while another tears down. Thus the Exalted says: ﴿None dispute concerning the signs of God except those who disbelieved﴾ [Ghafir: 4].

Al-jadal (disputation): to firmly twist a thing so that it becomes truly fixed and can never be undone. This matter is like the process of twisting ropes among us in the villages, where a man takes the fibres of the well-known tīl (fibre plant) and keeps twisting them, until the fibres interlace, hold together and intertwine, and that is why we see the rope strong and sturdy.

Argument between people is called jadal because each of the two parties wants to make his own logic and proof prevail so as to overcome the other. Each one disputes for his own benefit: the one with the truth disputes to display his truth, and the one with falsehood disputes to make his falsehood appear true. That is: he presents it in the form of truth.

But is disputation blameworthy in itself? No, because disputation depends on its aim. For this reason the Exalted says: ﴿And do not dispute with the People of the Book except in a way that is best﴾ [al-'Ankabut: 46]. This shows that in disputation there is what is good and what is better. Good disputation is that which seeks to establish proof that the truth is truth and falsehood is falsehood. If it is the reverse, it is false and blameworthy disputation.

Therefore we understand from His words: ﴿None dispute concerning the signs of God except those who disbelieved﴾ [Ghafir: 4] that this is false disputation, because disputation is conducted "for" them (ʿan-hā), not "in" them (fī-hā). One disputes for them, i.e., defends them in order to establish their truthfulness and make manifest the truth they brought; whereas disputing "in" the signs (yujādilu fī al-āyāt) means trying to cast doubt upon them and deny them.

We have said that the signs of God are of three kinds, and these are the ones in which disputation takes place: the cosmic signs which testify to the existence of the Supreme Creator, Exalted is He; the clear miraculous signs which establish the truthfulness of the Messenger in conveying from his Lord; and the Qur'anic verses which carry the rulings...

But which of these three kinds do the disbelievers dispute? Of course, they do not dispute the cosmic signs nor confront them, because firstly they benefit from them and see in them a precise, firm order that does not deviate or fail; so there is no room for disputation concerning them. Rather, they dispute the other signs: the miracle, and the verses of the Book carrying the rulings, and so they cast doubt upon them...

As for His words: ﴿those who disbelieved﴾, i.e., they concealed the existence of the Supreme Necessary Being who created them and created the whole universe around them, as evidenced by their own acknowledgment of this in the cosmic signs: ﴿And if you asked them, "Who created the heavens and the earth?" they would surely say, "God"﴾ [Luqman: 25]. So although they believe in these cosmic signs, they disbelieved in their Creator, Exalted is He, and concealed the Supreme Necessary Being who organizes the movement of life for all His creation, such that the movement of life is mutually supportive and not conflicting, so that the cultivation of the universe that the Creator, Exalted is He, willed remains intact.

We have previously explained that the word kafarū (they disbelieved) in itself is evidence of faith, because kufr means concealment (sitr), and concealment requires something concealed. So the concealed thing existed first before the concealer. Since they concealed the existence of God by disbelief, the principle is that He exists.

As for His words: ﴿So let not their movement throughout the land deceive you﴾ (lā yaghurrannaka taqallubuhum fī al-bilād), i.e., do not let it deceive you that they have in the lands authority, empowerment, exaltation and awe, such that no one can confront them in their movement from place to place, or in their journeys in the caravans of winter and summer.

If they had known the reality of this station, and who it was that placed them in this position, they would not have taken this stance toward you, O Muhammad. They obtained this awe and attained this station only through their proximity to the House of God, and God is the One who sent you to them, so it was incumbent upon them to believe in you and to confirm you.

The word (taqallub) indicates their movement and transfer from place to place, and indicates the strength of their bodies. For this reason all the tribes of the Arabs stood in awe of them. This standing for Quraysh came from the season of Hajj, when all the tribes of the Arabian Peninsula would come to them and be under the protection of Quraysh during the season; and from here they felt secure in their travels, and it was incumbent upon them to honour this blessing. But they denied it, so the saying of the Exalted applies to them: ﴿Have you not seen those who exchanged the blessing of God for disbelief and caused their people to alight in the abode of ruin?﴾ [Ibrahim: 28]... So His words: ﴿So let not their movement throughout the land deceive you﴾ are because God, Exalted is He, has not neglected them, but only gives them respite.

If you say: what is the wisdom of the respite? That is: since God, Exalted is He, has not neglected them, why did He not seize them from the beginning?

They say: Because God, Exalted is He, sent His Messenger (ﷺ), the seal of the Messengers, and made his religion the seal of religions and a guardian over time and place. There is no prophet after him, and for the Messenger there is a term at the end of which his role in life concludes and he passes to the Highest Companion; then after him the soldiers of truth, whom hardships have tested, will carry his message.

For this reason we have said: the chieftains of disbelief who tortured and persecuted the early Muslims were later among the soldiers of Islam. Why? Because this persecution and torture were what tested the Muslims and removed the weak of resolve and the weak of faith, whom torture had seduced and persecution had terrified, until no one remained in the field of faith except the strong, worthy of bearing this message and its consequences, because it is an eternal message that remains in all time and place.

Thus the Truth, glorified is He, did not neglect the disbelievers but gave them respite for a task: that they would contribute to the education of this generation that would carry God's call: ﴿those who convey the messages of God and fear Him, and fear none but God﴾ [al-Ahzab: 39].

These are the Muhammadan generation that bore the banner of Islam and spread it throughout all regions, not awaiting any advance payment for that, but awaiting their reward from God in the Hereafter.

This is the difference between the call of truth and the call of falsehood: the people of truth do not await an advance wage, whereas the people of falsehood take their wage before beginning the work. For this reason all the messengers of God said this word: ﴿And I do not ask you for any wage for it; my wage is only from the Lord of the worlds﴾ [al-Shu'ara': 109].

Yes, their reward is with God, because it is precious and no one can provide it except God. No one can repay the Messenger for his mission of guiding his people even if he were given all the wealth of this world.

Taqallub in the land means moving from place to place within it, which cannot be accomplished except through several things, the most important of which are: soundness of bodies to bear the hardship of travel; then security from the fear of the road; then the availability of provisions for him in the stopping places he alights at along his way...

The meaning: they are not unprecedented in existence, just as you are not unprecedented among the messengers. Your brethren among the messengers came before you and were denied, just as your people denied you. But what was the outcome of the denial? Did God send a messenger and then abandon him and hand him over? No, by God, rather it is God's way (sunnah) with His messengers that He grants them victory and humiliates the enemies of their call. God the Exalted says: ﴿And已 Our word had already preceded to Our servants, the messengers. Indeed, they would be the ones given victory. And indeed, Our soldiers would be the victorious﴾ [al-Saffat: 171-173].

This is not a theoretical statement with which We console you, O Muhammad. It has a reality and has parallels that confirm it in the procession of the messages, as He, glorified is He, said about the deniers: ﴿So each one We seized for his sin. Among them were those upon whom We sent a storm of stones (hasiban), and among them were those who were seized by the Blast, and among them were those whom We caused the earth to swallow, and among them were those whom We drowned﴾ [al-Ankabut: 40]. That is, a wind that pelts them with heated stones. ﴿And among them were those seized by the Blast﴾ [al-Ankabut: 40], and they were the people of Thamud. ﴿And among them were those whom We caused the earth to swallow﴾ [al-Ankabut: 40], as Qarun was swallowed up. ﴿And among them were those whom We drowned﴾ [al-Ankabut: 40], as was done to the people of Noah and the people of Pharaoh.

So God's way with the messages is that He gives victory to His messengers and defeats their enemy. Therefore we have said: if you see the Muslim community being defeated in a battle, know that the condition of being God's soldiers has been compromised in it. Had it remained upon God's condition of soldiery, it would never have been defeated.

As for His saying, ﴿Before them denied the people of Noah﴾ [Ghafir: 5], that is, before your people who denied you (the people of Noah). This is consolation for the Messenger of God and a lightening of his burden. The denial of messages is nothing new. He chose the people of Noah specifically because the message of Noah, peace be upon him, was the longest message. He remained in the call to his people for a thousand years less fifty years. Throughout this long lifespan they argued with the Messenger of God, Noah, denied him and opposed him. Therefore he despaired of their righteousness and prayed against them: ﴿My Lord, do not leave upon the earth from among the disbelievers an inhabitant. Indeed, if You leave them, they will mislead Your servants and will not beget except wicked disbelievers﴾ [Nuh: 26-27].

As for the few who believed with him, he prayed for them, beginning with himself: ﴿My Lord, forgive me and my parents﴾ [Nuh: 28]. Then ﴿and my parents﴾ [Nuh: 28], because they were the cause of my existence. ﴿And whoever enters my house as a believer﴾ [Nuh: 28], and they had no relationship with him. Then for the general believing men and believing women: ﴿and the believing men and believing women﴾ [Nuh: 28].

So: the denial of the people of Noah was mentioned specifically because it is the foundation of this matter, the clearest and the most violent. The positions to which Noah, peace be upon him, was exposed, of denial by his people, their harming him, and their mocking him while he was building the ark, are not hidden from you.

As for His saying, ﴿and the factions after them﴾ [Ghafir: 5], what is meant is 'Ad, the people of Hud, peace be upon him, and Thamud, the people of Salih, peace be upon him. This is not a theoretical statement; it is a reality that you see, and you pass by these ruined dwellings: ﴿And indeed, you pass by them in the morning, and at night. Will you not reason?﴾ [al-Saffat: 137-138].

They pass by Al-Ahqaf and the cities of Salih during their journeys. And here in Egypt, the monuments of the Pharaohs all bear witness to the truth of God in this message. Here are the most advanced countries of the world now, and a civilization that stands helpless before the civilization of the Pharaohs. How did they reach this level of advancement more than seven thousand years ago? Yet this civilization eluded them, because they did not reach the limit that would preserve it for them.

If you wish, read His saying: ﴿Have you not considered how your Lord dealt with 'Ad, Iram of the pillars, the likes of which had not been created in the lands, and Thamud who carved out the rocks in the valley, and Pharaoh of the stakes? Those who transgressed in the lands and caused much corruption therein. So your Lord poured upon them a scourge of punishment. Indeed, your Lord is ever in observation﴾ [al-Fajr: 6-14].

That is: the matter did not end with 'Ad, Thamud, and the people of Pharaoh. Rather, it is general for every denier: ﴿Indeed, your Lord is ever in observation﴾ [al-Fajr: 14].

The "factions" (al-ahzab) are those who band together and gather upon a single principle. The meaning here is those who form factions against the call and against guidance, and for this reason they are called the party of Satan, and opposed to them is the party of God, who support the messengers and aid the call to truth.

﴿And every community plotted against their messenger to seize him﴾ [Ghafir: 5]: that is, to kill him. This matter came in detail in His saying: ﴿And [remember] when those who disbelieved plotted against you to restrain you, or kill you, or expel you. But they plan, and Allah plans. And Allah is the best of planners﴾ [al-Anfal: 30]. That is, to imprison you or bind you so that you cannot move here or there.

The point here is that they intended this but did not do it and were not able to do it. The word (hammat) means an orientation and a desire toward something that did not actually happen. Among this is His saying regarding the two groups at the Battle of Uhud: ﴿When two parties among you were about to lose heart﴾ [Al 'Imran: 122]. But the failure did not happen. So the (hamm) is the preoccupation of the heart with doing a thing, but the act does not occur. For this reason He, glorified is He, said: ﴿And they intended what they did not attain﴾ [al-Tawbah: 74].

Except for the (hamm) that came from our master Yusuf, peace be upon him, because the matter here concerns the infallibility (ʿiṣmah) of a prophet, as He, the Exalted, said: ﴿And she certainly desired him, and he would have desired her...﴾ [Yusuf: 24]. Some impose on this verse meanings that are not fitting for the infallibility of the prophet of God, Yusuf. They say: how could he desire her while he is a prophet?

We say: desire (hamm) is the attachment of the thought to the act, or the attachment of the body's response to the act. But whether it is acted upon or not, that is what matters. The verse contains two desires: ﴿And she certainly desired him﴾ [Yusuf: 24], then a pause, then ﴿and he would have desired her﴾ [Yusuf: 24]. Note that her desire did not gain anything from him, which is why she said: ﴿And I had certainly sought to seduce him, but he refrained. And if he does not do what I order him, he will surely be imprisoned and will be of the debased﴾ [Yusuf: 32].

This is evidence that her desire did not produce a result. How could her desire produce nothing despite her disobedience, while his desire produces something? So: she desired him and nothing happened, and she was the one willing. Likewise he desired her and nothing happened, because he did not will it.

Consider here the precision of the Qur'anic expression in the use of the heavy emphatic nun in ﴿he will surely be imprisoned﴾ [Yusuf: 32] and the light emphatic nun in ﴿and will be of the debased﴾ [Yusuf: 32]. Because imprisonment is a matter in her hand, and by her command Yusuf would be imprisoned, so the heavy emphatic nun is used, which indicates firm control over the act. As for being of the debased, this is not in her hand. Perhaps she would imprison him and the guards would sympathize with him and honour him. So the light emphatic nun is used here to undermine her control over this act.

The answer by which we settle the matter of desire in this story and clarify the innocence of our master Yusuf from what the slanderers say about him is this: we say, "And she certainly desired him." Yes, did she carry out this desire or not? She did not carry it out, as evidenced by her saying: ﴿And if he does not do what I order him﴾ [Yusuf: 32], and ﴿and he would have desired her﴾ [Yusuf: 24]. Yes, he desired but did not act, by the same evidence as before. So why are you keen to attach the accusation to the prophet of God, when his desire, like hers, produced nothing?

Furthermore, desire in his case here is a natural matter, because it is the readiness of nature to fall into this act. That is, it is a possibility for him, peace be upon him. His nature is suited to act; otherwise we would say he is impotent (haṣūr) and has no capacity for this matter. Rather, he is suited to it and capable of it. So what prevented him? We say: what prevented him is ﴿had he not seen the proof of his Lord﴾ [Yusuf: 24].

That is, regarding the fact that this is forbidden. As you say: "I would visit you, were it not that so-and-so is with you," meaning that I did not visit you. So: ﴿And he desired her, had he not seen the proof of his Lord﴾ [Yusuf: 24]. That is, he desired but did not act. So the ruling here is the innocence of Yusuf, peace be upon him, even from desire.

Returning to His saying: ﴿And every community plotted against their messenger to seize him﴾ [Ghafir: 5]. This occurred, but they did not act and did not seize him. ﴿And they argued with falsehood to refute thereby the truth﴾ [Ghafir: 5]: that is, to remove and defeat the truth with falsehood. So what was the outcome? ﴿Then I seized them﴾ [Ghafir: 5]: that is, I actually destroyed them, not merely with desire as they had done. This is what befits the supreme power. ﴿Then how was My punishment?﴾ [Ghafir: 5]: that is, did we know? Were we able to punish them?

This is like His saying: ﴿Indeed, those who committed crimes used to laugh at those who believed. And when they passed by them, they would exchange winks. And when they returned to their people, they returned jesting. And when they saw them, they said, "Indeed, these are misguided." But they had not been sent as guardians over them. So today, those who believed will laugh at the disbelievers, upon couches, observing. Have the disbelievers been recompensed for what they used to do?﴾ [al-Mutaffifin: 29-36].

That is: were we able to repay them for their deeds and their crimes? It is as if the Exalted wishes to alert the people of faith and reassure them of His justice, glorified is He. These people will not escape punishment. And there is no doubt that the punishment of the people of crime and the people of disbelief brings comfort to the people of faith.

Consider also here the precision of the Qur'anic expression in His saying: ﴿And every community plotted against their messenger to seize him﴾ [Ghafir: 5]. It did not say "their messenger" (rasuluha) in agreement with the fact that "community" (ummah) is a feminine singular noun. Instead it said "their messenger" (rasulihim), attributing the messenger to a masculine plural. This is because the confrontation between Islam and disbelief was carried out by men, and women were not a party to these confrontations. The evidence is that when they plotted against the Messenger of God on the night of the Hijrah, they were all men, and there was not a single woman among them. Likewise the situation with ﴿and they argued with falsehood to refute thereby the truth﴾ [Ghafir: 5]. These are matters in which women have no part.

(حَقَّتْ) means: it became due, was established, and remained firm, and no event came to annul it. Why? Because the One who spoke it knows what will follow it, especially when those who act have a choice in whether they act or not.

God, exalted is He, spoke it and passed judgment upon them while they were in the midst of worldly ease and in a time of choice, and yet they did not oppose it. Here lies the greatness of God's speech: the greatness that I challenge you concerning a matter in which you have choice, and yet you do not go beyond what I have judged against you.

We have said something similar concerning His saying, exalted is He, about Abu Lahab and his wife: ﴿Perish the hands of Abu Lahab, and perish he. His wealth will not avail him, nor what he earned. He will burn in a Fire of blazing flame, and his wife, the carrier of firewood, with a rope of twisted fiber around her neck﴾ [al-Masad: 1-5].

So the Truth, glorified and exalted, judged that both of them were disbelievers and that their destiny is the Fire, even though faith and disbelief are a matter that God has entrusted to the choice of the servant. The proof is that the likes of Abu Lahab among the disbelievers of Makkah became Muslims, such as Khalid ibn al-Walid, 'Amr ibn al-'As, 'Ikrimah and others. And it was possible for Abu Lahab, after this surah was revealed, to testify that there is no god but Allah and that Muhammad is the Messenger of Allah, saying it even if hypocritically, but it did not happen, and the saying of God came true concerning him.

This matter was explained by the Truth, glorified and exalted, in His saying: ﴿And know that Allah intervenes between a man and his heart...﴾ [al-Anfal: 24]. So his heart may tell him of something, but divine greatness turns him away from it.

Therefore, the Exalted said to the mother of Musa: ﴿So when you fear for him, cast him into the river, and do not fear and do not grieve...﴾ [al-Qasas: 7]. Rational analogy does not accept this solution, for what sensible person would say that a woman, when she fears for her infant, throws him into the sea? But here, the mother of Musa did not heed the voice of reason, nor was she moved by her emotional attachment to her child. Rather, she heeded the word of her Lord, and listened to this supreme inspiration which no lowly satanic inspiration could oppose, so she never hesitated to cast her child into the sea, because God, exalted is He, came between her and the feeling of her heart.

The same is the case in the story of our lord Musa with Pharaoh. The soothsayers informed Pharaoh that the end of his kingdom would be at the hand of a boy from the Children of Israel. So what did Pharaoh do? Let you know how the mentality of those who claimed divinity was, and how God intervenes between a person and his heart: what did Pharaoh do? He began searching for infants and killing them, and he did not know that God was preserving for him this boy, who would come to him and knock at his door while he was in his cradle in the form you know. Yet he felt at ease with him and adopted him as a son, and his wife said: ﴿A comfort of the eye for me and for you...﴾ [al-Qasas: 9]. So he took him and raised him in his house. This is the meaning of ﴿And know that Allah intervenes between a man and his heart...﴾ [al-Anfal: 24].

Thus, His saying: ﴿And thus the word of your Lord has been fulfilled against those who disbelieved, that they are the companions of the Fire﴾ [Ghafir: 6]: it did not become due against them by force and compulsion; rather, it became due against them by their own choice. The Truth, glorified and exalted, by His eternal knowledge, knew their choice, and so He judged them by His prior knowledge concerning them. And no event can come that contradicts this judgment, because the One who speaks these words is God.

We had already clarified that the word (kalimah) is applied to a single word, and it is applied to speech. Among its uses is His saying: ﴿By no means! It is only a word he is saying...﴾ [al-Mu'minun: 100], and His saying concerning those who said "Allah has taken a son": ﴿...Allah has taken a son...﴾ [Yunus: 68], He said: ﴿Great is the word that comes out of their mouths; they say nothing but falsehood﴾ [al-Kahf: 5]. And we call a long sermon a kalimah.

So the word that became due, was established and remained firm is not just any word; rather, it is ﴿the word of your Lord﴾ [Ghafir: 6]. The word of God must come to pass and must remain firm, and God, exalted is He, would not say a word and then events would come and contradict it. The word that became due against those who disbelieved is that ﴿they are the companions of the Fire﴾ [Ghafir: 6].

Commentary of al-Sha'rawi (Tafsir al-Sha'rawi, surahs 1-53, fragments of 54-66) on surah 40, verse 7:

These are the angels whom Allah created for His glorification, glory be to Him. They have no task other than glorifying Allah, and they are the bearers of the Throne and those around it. Glorification (tasbih), as we have said, is among the keys (maqalid), and the meaning of ﴿They glorify their Lord with His praise..﴾ [Ghafir: 7] is: they declare Him far above resembling His creation in names, actions and attributes.

Therefore we have said: whenever the Truth, glory be to Him, shares something with His creation, we must take it within the frame of ﴿There is nothing like unto Him..﴾ [Ash-Shura: 11].

Allah has an action and you have an action, but do not measure your action by the action of your Lord, glory be to Him. We clarified this matter in the explanation of the beginning of Surat al-Isra'. Since the event was astonishing, Allah the Exalted began the surah with glorification: ﴿Glory be to He who took His servant by night..﴾ [Al-Isra': 1]. He said it at the outset so that we do not measure Allah's action by the action of humans, nor Allah's power by human power. Allah has an action and you have an action, but the action of Allah is not like your action. So beware of saying "the distance and the time."

The phrase (Subhan Allah) means the declaring of Allah far above everything that resembles human beings. Therefore they said: whatever occurs to your mind, Allah is other than that. This glorification is not something that arose with the existence of those who glorify Allah; rather it is eternal, before Allah created those who glorify Him. He, glory be to Him, is transcendent in His essence before any who glorify Him exist.

Therefore, when the heavens and the earth came into being, He said: ﴿Whatever is in the heavens and the earth glorifies Allah..﴾ [Al-Hadid: 1]. That is: they glorified Allah the moment they were created, saying: Glory be to Allah, the Creator, the Mighty. And they never cease glorifying, as He said: ﴿Whatever is in the heavens and whatever is in the earth glorifies Allah..﴾ [Al-Jumu'ah: 1]. So glorification is continuous and perpetual. If the whole cosmos glorifies Allah and never ceases to do so, and the cosmos was created for you, O human, then you are more entitled to glorification than it. Therefore He said: ﴿Glorify the name of your Lord, the Most High﴾ [Al-A'la: 1].

The glorification of Allah is declaring Him free of resemblance in His actions and in His attributes. When you contemplate, for example, the matter of creation, you find that the human being was created from clay. Can you take a piece of clay, shape it into the form of a human, and then breathe the spirit into it yourself? This process is not within the power of anyone except the Creator, glory be to Him.

Therefore, when Allah willed to make for our master Jesus, peace be upon him, a sign and a miracle in the matter of creation, he said: ﴿Indeed, I create for you from clay [a figure] like the form of a bird, then I breathe into it and it becomes a bird by permission of Allah..﴾ [Ali 'Imran: 49]. He said regarding the breathing of the spirit ﴿by permission of Allah..﴾ [Ali 'Imran: 49], because he by himself could not perform this process. Rather, my fashioning a statue in the form of a human or a bird is an easy matter.

So, O human whom Allah has honored, you should have glorified, because the cosmos and the inanimate things that Allah created for you have glorified and still do.

As for His saying, the Exalted: ﴿Those who bear the Throne..﴾ [Ghafir: 7], they are the angels who bear the Throne. So the Throne is carried, and these angels, even their number contains a miracle. The Truth, glory be to Him, informed that they are eight: ﴿And above them on that Day eight will bear the Throne of your Lord﴾ [Al-Haqqah: 17].

Why did He not make them four, as is customary in any structure that has four corners? And why were they not five, for instance? Therefore, there must be wisdom and a miracle in this particular number.

This numerical miracle is also evident in His saying: ﴿Over it are nineteen﴾ [Al-Muddaththir: 30]. Why nineteen specifically? Why did He not make them twenty, for example? This is evidence that behind this number there is wisdom. Allah the Exalted has informed that this number is a trial: ﴿And We have not made the companions of the Fire except angels, and We have not made their number except as a trial for those who disbelieve..﴾ [Al-Muddaththir: 31].

Faith requires affirming what the Truth, glory be to Him, has informed, and not debating such matters. The important thing is whether He said it or not, whether the event occurred or not. Therefore, when they informed our master Abu Bakr that your companion claims to be a messenger, what did he say? He said: "Did he indeed say it?" They said: "Yes." He said: "Then he has spoken the truth," and he did not investigate the matter. Likewise, in every matter where the intellect stands still, as long as a report has come to us from Allah concerning it, we must accept it and believe in it: ﴿And who is more truthful in statement than Allah?﴾ [An-Nisa': 87].

Whether your mind can comprehend this report or cannot is another subject, because there is a difference between existence and the manner of existence. A thing may exist while you do not know how it came to exist.

Consider the story of the father of the prophets, our master Abraham, peace be upon him, when he said: ﴿My Lord, show me how You give life to the dead. He said: Have you not believed? He said: Yes, but [I ask] that my heart may be assured..﴾ [Al-Baqarah: 260].

You will find that superficial people in understanding Allah accuse the Qur'an of contradiction in this matter. How? They say: the meaning of (Bala, "yes") is "I have believed," and belief requires the heart's assurance in the creed, so why does he say after it: ﴿but that my heart may be assured..﴾ [Al-Baqarah: 260]?

We say to him: you are excused, because you did not understand the meaning of the question. Had you understood its meaning, you would not have accused the Qur'an. Did Abraham say to his Lord: "Can You give life to the dead?" No, he said: ﴿My Lord, show me how You give life..﴾ [Al-Baqarah: 260]. He therefore did not ask about the possibility of the act, nor did he doubt the power of Allah, but he asked about the manner. ﴿My Lord, show me how You give life to the dead..﴾ [Al-Baqarah: 260]. So the giving of life to the dead is a matter already established, and Abraham asked about its manner. If I said to you: "How did you build this house?", this means that the house already stands in fact.

Therefore, his saying (Bala) means: I have believed, O Lord, that You give life to the dead, and his request for assurance afterward concerns the manner. Asking about the manner is necessary in the matter of creation and the manner of bringing into being, because it is a process that cannot be accomplished by speech, since the act of Allah the Exalted is not a treatment like the act of humans.

If I said to you: "How did you build this house?", you would say: I dug the foundation, brought iron and cement, and did such and such; so-and-so designed, so-and-so executed, so-and-so built. And I would give you the manner of the act so that you can apply it if you wish, without finding any discrepancy. But if we wanted to explain the manner of giving life, how would we build it?

It is a matter that cannot be accomplished by speech; the process must be carried out in actuality. Consider that Allah the Exalted willed that Abraham carry it out himself, and not that it be done for him; he practises it with his own self. There is a difference between transferring your power to another so that he acts on your behalf, and transferring your power to another so that he himself performs it. For example, you may be unable to carry something, and I carry it for you; this is a natural matter. But the greatness lies in my making you able, by yourself, to carry it.

This is what the Truth, glory be to Him, did with His prophet Abraham, peace be upon him: ﴿He said: Take four birds and make them incline toward you..﴾ [Al-Baqarah: 260], that is: gather them to you and learn their characteristics. ﴿Then place on every hill a portion of them..﴾ [Al-Baqarah: 260], meaning: slaughter them and scatter their parts over the hills. ﴿Then call them; they will come to you in haste..﴾ [Al-Baqarah: 260].

So He is the one who slaughters, He is the one who cuts the parts, He is the one who scatters them, and He is the one who calls them by Himself, so they gather by the power of Allah and come hastening as they were before. So if He made able what is not able, shall I not be able to do it?

The Throne is the mark of the establishment of kingship, the control of rule and the seizing of it. It is not necessary that he actually sit on the Throne. Therefore, when the hoopoe spoke of the queen of Sheba, he said: ﴿She has been given of all things, and she has a mighty throne﴾ [An-Naml: 23], because a king does not sit upon the throne except when affairs are settled for him and the lands submit to him. If there was an area that opposed or troubled the king, he would devote himself to it until it submitted to him, and then his kingship would be established.

When the Truth, glory be to Him, spoke of His istiwa' over the Throne, He said, glory be to Him: ﴿Say: Do you indeed disbelieve in He who created the earth in two days, and you set up rivals to Him? That is the Lord of the worlds. And He placed within it firm mountains from above it, and blessed it, and measured therein its sustenance in four days, alike for those who ask. Then He turned to the heaven while it was smoke, and said to it and to the earth: Come willingly or unwillingly. They said: We come willingly. So He completed them as seven heavens in two days, and inspired in each heaven its command..﴾ [Fussilat: 9-12].

So His istiwa' over the Throne came after He had finished the creation and every matter of kingship and complete control had been accomplished for Him.

Thus His saying, glory be to Him: ﴿Those who bear the Throne..﴾ [Ghafir: 7] are the eight angels who bear the Throne. ﴿And those around it glorify with the praise of their Lord, and believe in Him, and ask forgiveness for those who believed..﴾ [Ghafir: 7]. These are another kind of angels, namely the cherubim (karubiyyun), who have no task except glorifying Allah, and this whole cosmos is not in their minds, and they know nothing of it; only ﴿they glorify with the praise of their Lord..﴾ [Ghafir: 7].

But these cherubim who surround the Throne and glorify Allah, having no task other than that, do they see Allah, glory be to Him, while He is upon the Throne? Our scholars, may Allah have mercy on them, said: despite their station, they do not see Allah the Exalted. The most manifest of these opinions is the view of Imam al-Razi, may Allah have mercy on him. When he discussed this verse ﴿Those who bear the Throne and those around it glorify with the praise of their Lord and believe in Him..﴾ [Ghafir: 7], he relied on the opinion of the author of al-Kashshaf, who preceded him, and said: the meaning of ﴿and believe in Him..﴾ [Ghafir: 7] is that they do not see Him, because observable things contain no faith; faith is for the unseen. Had they witnessed Allah while He was upon the Throne, He would not have said concerning them ﴿and believe in Him..﴾ [Ghafir: 7]. Then al-Razi said: even if al-Imam, the author of al-Kashshaf, had only this [remark], it would have sufficed him for his whole life, despite the disagreement in opinion between the two imams.

So from the station of these angels and their nearness to the Lord of Majesty, glory be to Him, we should not understand that they see Him. Rather, He, glory be to Him, is for them an unseen reality that they do not see. This is confirmed by His saying, glory be to Him: ﴿and believe in Him..﴾ [Ghafir: 7]. For you, now, in this gathering, do not say, for example: "I believe that Sheikh al-Sha'rawi is sitting and around him are his lovers, speaking about such and such," because what we are in now is a visible scene in which faith has no place. Faith exists only with an unseen matter, and this is the distinctive feature of faith. Therefore His saying, the Exalted, is often repeated: ﴿Those who believe in the unseen..﴾ [Al-Baqarah: 3].

We have previously given an example: suppose I fear thieves, so I take my money that I fear for and go to a distant place in the garden, for example, and place the money and on top of it a heavy stone. When I need this money, I call out to the worker: "O so-and-so, lift this stone." He says: "I cannot alone, it is heavy." I say to him: "Do you know what is under this stone? Under it is the money from which I will give you your wages." Then he approaches the stone and lifts it. So the important thing is not obeying a command whose benefit is known, but obeying a command while it is unseen to you.

The meaning of ﴿they glorify with the praise of their Lord..﴾ [Ghafir: 7] is: glorification joined with praise, because glorification is an extolling of Allah, whereas praise is thanks to Allah for His previous blessings. Among the most exalted of blessings is that nothing resembles Him, for if He had a like, there would have been conflict in the cosmos: ﴿Otherwise each god would have taken away what he created, and some of them would have exalted themselves over others..﴾ [Al-Mu'minun: 91]. So He alone is the one worshipped, and He alone is deserving of praise.

Then: ﴿and they ask forgiveness for those who believe..﴾ [Ghafir: 7], meaning that among these angels' duties is seeking forgiveness for the believers, as the Qur'an relates them saying: ﴿Our Lord, You have encompassed all things in mercy and knowledge, so forgive those who repent and follow Your way, and protect them from the punishment of the Blazing Fire﴾ [Ghafir: 7].

This is the angels' supplication for those who believe. The supplication is customarily with "Rabbana" with the letter of address (ya) of calling omitted, so it is not said "Ya Rabbana," because calling with the particle ya indicates the distance of the one called, and the most distant is called with ay(a), while the near is called with the hamza, as in: "Amuhammad."

As for the Truth, glory be to Him and exalted, He is so near that we do not use in calling Him any particle of address, because He is nearer to His servant than the jugular vein. Therefore we call Him directly, "Rabbana." You may survey the whole Qur'an and you will not find in His calling any particle of address.

Even the disbelievers, when they called upon the Truth, glory be to Him, said: ﴿O Allah, if this is indeed the truth from You, then rain down upon us stones from the sky..﴾ [Al-Anfal: 32]. It is well known that the mim at the end of the word Allah here is a substitute for the particle of address; so they did not say "Ya Allah," but said "Allahumma."

Then the Truth, glory be to Him, continues the mention of the angels' supplication for those who believe, saying:

﴿Our Lord, and admit them into the Gardens of Eternity which You have promised them...﴾.

Meaning of "Gardens of Eternity" (jannāti ʿadn): i.e., permanent abode.

Reflect on the fruit of faith in God, the fruit of "There is no god but God": with faith, no disobedience causes harm. The angels in the highest ʿIlliyyūn remember you and occupy themselves with you, O believer, and pray for you because you have believed in God. This is a consolation for our master, the Messenger of God (ﷺ), and for his community, who bore the hardships of the call, and for those who follow them until the Day of Religion.

So, O Muhammad, if the disbelievers of Makkah have taken this stubbornly opposed stance toward you and your followers, do not grieve. It is enough for you and your community that the angels ask forgiveness for you. And which angels? The bearers of the Throne and those who surround it.

When you read this supplication of the angels, you find in it indications and pauses worthy of reflection. The first is that you, O believer, are mentioned among the bearers of the Throne, and you are the object of their concern, despite the lowliness of your rank and the loftiness of theirs. These angels have no task except to glorify their Lord with His praise and to seek forgiveness for those who believe.

Reflect on their supplication regarding the matter of takhliyah (clearing away) and then tahliyah (adorning): they say, "So forgive those who repent and follow Your way, and protect them from the punishment of the Blazing Fire" [al-Ghafir: 7]. This is takhliyah first, from what is painful; then comes tahliyah with the blessing that gladdens, and that is in "Our Lord, and admit them to Gardens of Eternity which You have promised them..." [al-Ghafir: 8]. This is because clearing away and deliverance from punishment take precedence over enjoyment, and the principle is that averting harm takes precedence over securing benefit. Therefore He, exalted is He, said: "Whoever is drawn away from the Fire and admitted to Paradise has indeed succeeded" [Al ʿImran: 185].

Moreover, their supplication does not single out the believers alone; it includes the entire family: "and whoever of their fathers, their spouses, and their offspring are righteous" [al-Ghafir: 8]. Thus they mention the whole tree, because fathers rejoice in being with their children, so this blessing is not cut off from them...

Then the verse is concluded with His saying, exalted is He: "Indeed You, You are the Mighty, the Wise," and He did not say, for example, "Indeed You, You are the Forgiving, the Merciful," so as to suit the supplication mentioned in the verse.

(وَقِهِمُ) — here it is an imperative, or a supplication, from the verb وَقَى (waqa, "to protect"). That is, "O Lord, keep them away from sins." It is also valid to say: "Protect them from evil deeds." That is: keep them from the punishment of sins, or keep them from the sins themselves. The essence of mercy is that Allah keeps you away from sins and evil deeds, and so He said: ﴿And whoever is protected from evil deeds on that Day, You have certainly had mercy on him..﴾ [Ghafir: 9].

This is like His saying, Exalted is He, concerning the Noble Qur'an: ﴿And We send down of the Qur'an that which is a healing and a mercy for the believers..﴾ [Al-Isra: 82]. Healing is for a disease that already exists in the human soul; the Qur'an treats, for example, the diseases of stinginess, cowardice, lying, etc. As for mercy, it is that the disease never arises in the first place. Without doubt, avoiding the disease at the outset is better than treating it, as they say: prevention is better than cure.

﴿And that is the great achievement﴾ [Ghafir: 9]. Yes, and what achievement is greater than that Allah keeps you away from evil deeds so that you do not fall into them? The word fawz (achievement, "success") means salvation and success. It is described as "great" because in this world you may succeed in wealth, position, or children; this is a success, but the great success is in the Hereafter, because it is lasting and permanent, whereas the success of this world ends in passing away.

Then the Almighty says:

﴿Indeed, those who disbelieved will be called out to: The hatred of Allah is greater...﴾.

Commentary of al-Sha'rawi (Tafsir al-Sha'rawi, surahs 1-53, fragments of 54-66) on surah 40, verse 10:

If we follow this matter from its beginning, we find that the Truth, glory be to Him, called creation through His messengers and His method (manhaj) towards them. Some of them responded and believed, and some of them disbelieved: ﴿when you are called to faith, then you disbelieve﴾ [Ghafir: 10]. Those who did not respond to the caller to the Truth wished not to be bound by God's method of "do" and "do not do," and not to constrict themselves by adherence to the method, and to walk in the world according to their desires. This is what led them to disbelieve.

So when they witness the punishment in the Hereafter, they regret at a time when regret does not benefit, and they hate themselves with the utmost hatred, because it did not follow the method of faith.

This is the meaning of His, glory be to Him, saying: ﴿Indeed, those who disbelieved will be called out to: "The hatred of Allah is greater than your hatred of yourselves, when you were called to faith but you disbelieved."﴾ [Ghafir: 10]. Al-maqt is the most intense hatred. The Truth, glory be to Him, wanted to say to them: If you hated yourselves with the utmost hatred because it did not believe in Muhammad (ﷺ) and in the method of Truth that he brought, then know that God's hatred of you for your disbelief in Him is more severe and greater than your hatred of yourselves. You hated yourselves because it deprived you of good and drew evil upon you when it disbelieved in God.

And the Truth, glory be to Him, hates you because you distanced yourselves from the sphere of His good and exited from His embrace and the circle of His mercy. For He, glory be to Him, becomes most angry when one departs from His presence and deprives oneself of His goodness. This means that your Lord loves you, wills good for you, wants you by His side and in His company, and is jealous over you when you stray or deviate from His method, for you are His servant and His creation.

So His hatred for the disbeliever is, as it were, a mercy towards him and a jealousy over him...

Thus: the Truth, glory be to Him, first established their hatred for themselves, then He showed them that His hatred for the disbeliever is greater than this.

Commentary of al-Sha'rawi (Tafsir al-Sha'rawi, surahs 1–53, fragments of 54–66) on surah 40, verse 11:

To understand the meaning of ﴿You caused us to die twice, and You gave us life twice﴾, we must first know what death is. Death is the removal of life after it has existed. Since death will occur, it is evidence of life before it. Death also means the absence of life entirely, that is, a non-existence that was not preceded by life at all.

For this reason, He, glory be to Him, said: ﴿How can you disbelieve in Allah, when you were dead and He gave you life?﴾ [al-Baqarah: 28]. This is a rhetorical question expressing astonishment, meaning: tell us, how can disbelief come from you? ﴿When you were dead﴾ [al-Baqarah: 28], that is, you were non-existent, and He bestowed life upon you. ﴿Then He causes you to die﴾ [al-Baqarah: 28], that is, He removes the life that exists. ﴿Then He gives you life﴾ [al-Baqarah: 28], that is, in the Hereafter.

So, death occurs twice and life occurs twice as well. The disagreement on this matter is: Must death come after a life, or is it sufficient that it be a non-existence after which life comes? We say: death is absolute non-existence, whether or not it was preceded by life...

Thus, the verse combines both meanings: absolute death, or the non-existence that was not preceded by life, and death in the sense of ending the life that is actually present. So He, glory be to Him, said: ﴿You caused us to die twice, and You gave us life twice﴾.

Some hold that the first death is the removal of life after the term has expired, then one is alive in the grave for questioning, then dies in the grave, then is raised on the Day of Resurrection. The first view that we have chosen is more fitting.

As for His statement, glory be to Him: ﴿So we have acknowledged our sins. Is there any way to get out?﴾, the interrogative in ﴿Is there any way to get out?﴾ is a question expressing wishing, but it is far-fetched. Even if they were returned, they would revert to what they had been, so there is no benefit in repeating this trial. Allah, the Exalted, clarified this matter in His saying: ﴿No! It is merely a word he speaks﴾ [al-Mu'minun: 100].

Even if they were returned, they would revert with the evil natures within them and would disbelieve. "The way out" means the escape from the predicament we are in and from the punishment we are witnessing; ﴿a way﴾ means a path of exit and deliverance.

What we have mentioned concerns the life and death of bodies. As for the life of hearts and spirits, it has another path, which Allah, the Exalted, mentioned in His saying: ﴿O you who have believed, respond to Allah and to the Messenger when He calls you to that which gives you life﴾ [al-Anfal: 24].

There is no doubt that He, glory be to Him, addresses them while they possess material life. Therefore, there is another life to which He calls them: it is the life of the immaterial realities, after which there is no death, and it is the life of Paradise.

So, there is a life of matter by which one lives, moves, eats, drinks and is active, and there is another, immaterial life by which one enters Paradise, where there is bliss without cessation and life without death. Material life has a spirit suited to it, and it is a life that ends in death. As for the life of values and immaterial realities, it necessarily has a lofty spirit that comes through adherence to the method in: "do" and "do not do." Therefore Allah calls it a spirit: ﴿We have revealed to you a spirit of Our command﴾ [al-Shura: 52], and He called the one who bears it a spirit: ﴿The Trustworthy Spirit has brought it down﴾ [al-Shu'ara': 193].

Each of the two lives has what suits it of permanence: the first is limited by a term, while the other is extended and lasting. Therefore we have said that the martyr who gave his soul and ended his life in the cause of his method, Allah rewards him by preserving him from death after that.

Al-Sha'rawi's commentary on Surah 40, verse 12:

When the Truth, glorified and exalted is He, spoke about the creed and confirmed it with miracles, it was necessary for us to receive His rulings in it with contentment and acceptance. He, glory be to Him, did not impose upon us a command of "do" and "do not" except after He had presented the grounds for the supreme faith in the Supreme God, so whoever believed believed and whoever disbelieved disbelieved, despite all our interests in organizing the movement of life by the methodology of God.

So when He issues a ruling against us, it is obligatory that we obey Him. And if something contrary to that has settled in your minds, then your actual situation confirms that you have not believed with your hearts. That is: what happens from you of confronting the call and clashing with it, and your standing in this hostile position, arises from ﴿when God alone is invoked, you disbelieve﴾, meaning: you disbelieved in Him.

And in another place He, glory be to Him, said: ﴿And when God alone is mentioned, the hearts of those who do not believe in the Hereafter shrink; but when those besides Him are mentioned, behold, they rejoice﴾ [al-Zumar: 45].

That is: there appeared upon them displeasure and distress when they heard the word of God. Why? Because they know the meaning of faith and what follows from it of obligation to a methodology: "do such-and-such and do not do such-and-such." They know that this methodology restricts their desires, forbids them from things beloved to them, and calls them to other things heavy upon their souls. Therefore, when you remind them of God and the methodology of faith, they become displeased, whereas when someone other than Him, from among their gods, is mentioned, ﴿they rejoice﴾ [al-Zumar: 45] and are pleased. Why?

Because these gods they have taken besides God have no demand upon them and no obligations of "do" and "do not." So: with this worship you are left to your own whims and to the evils of your souls. This is the meaning of rejoicing, and the meaning of ﴿and if He is associated with, you believe﴾.

But one truth remains that should not be absent from your minds: ﴿So judgment belongs to God, the Most High, the Greatest﴾. So rejoice in your alleged gods as you wish. I will judge you by My decree, against your will: I will make you ill as I please, cause you to die whenever I will, impoverish you and enrich you... and so on. You will never escape anything of My dominion except in what I have granted you choice.

You are free to choose in belief and disbelief: whoever wills, let him believe, and whoever wills, let him disbelieve; whoever wills, let him obey, and whoever wills, let him disobey. Your obedience will not benefit Me, and your disobedience will not harm Me. However much you rebel in matters where you have choice, your return is to Me and your end is with Me.

﴿So judgment belongs to God, the Most High, the Greatest﴾, who can never be rebelled against in His decree by anyone. So if you have become accustomed to rebellion in belief and in obedience, then show me how you rebel against God in what you have no choice about.

The verses (āyāt) are the plural of āyah (sign), and we have said that they are of three kinds: cosmic signs (āyāt kawniyyah) that point to the high power and surpassing wisdom of the true God, Lord of exaltation and majesty; the signs of miracles (āyāt al-mu'jizāt), which He bestows to confirm the messengers and to establish belief in the truth of their message from God; and then the legal rulings (āyāt al-aḥkām), which carry God's rulings.

He, glorified is He, says: ﴿It is He who shows you His signs﴾, that is, the cosmic ones, so that you may believe in the Most High God, and He shows you the miracles at the hands of the messengers. Then He sends down to you the legal verses which protect your religions and your creed, because just as I protected your bodies by what I sent down of rain from the sky and what grows from it of provision by which you feed and live, likewise take from Me the other thing which I made for the sustenance of your religions, namely the rulings which protect your belief in the legislative movement of "do" and "do not."

So His saying, glorified is He, ﴿It is He who shows you His signs and sends down for you provision from the sky﴾ takes both matters into account together, so that neither is neglected at the expense of the other.

﴿And none remembers except one who turns back (to God)﴾, that is, returns to God and casts off from himself the pride of denial of that God, and shakes off from himself the dust of heedlessness, until he returns to the innate faith (fiṭrah) which the Real, glorified is He, intended in His saying: ﴿Am I not your Lord?﴾ [al-A'rāf: 172], and the answer was that all of them said, ﴿Yes (balā)﴾, meaning: You are our true Lord.

Commentary of al-Sha'rawi (Tafsir al-Sha'rawi, surahs 1-53, fragments of 54-66) on surah 40, verse 14:

Du'a' (supplication, calling upon God): it is the manifestation of humility and submission to God Most High. Why? Because among people there are those who rebel against God and are arrogant toward obedience, too proud to show submission to God.
