When such a person sees from you humility and submission to God, and sees sincerity in worship, he knows that this rebellion is not a natural disposition of man, but rather a disposition of his own desire (hawa). The evidence is that among people there are those who humble themselves and submit, and among people there are those who call upon their Lord, devote themselves sincerely to Him, and obey Him.

So: rebellion is not an inherent necessary characteristic of man; it is a characteristic only of the rebellious one. Rather, when man is in his natural state and original disposition (fitrah), he must turn to God and seek His help. Therefore: ﴿So call upon God, making your religion sincere for Him, even though the disbelievers dislike it﴾.

We have said, regarding the virtue of supplication, that it is "the marrow of worship" (mukh al-ibadah). Supplication is nothing but the humility of the worshipper before the might of the One worshipped, the mere manifestation of humility, regardless of what results from the supplication. Otherwise, God, glory be to Him, gave you before you asked Him, and created for you before you existed. Therefore, it is not necessary that God respond to everyone who calls upon Him. It is as if He, glory be to Him, is saying to us: Take note that among you are those who call upon Me and I do not respond to them, and when I do not respond to them, I grant them the highest bounty, because a person may ask for evil while he thinks it is good, and may request a thing without knowing that in it lies his destruction...

Therefore we have said in praising Him, glory be to Him: "Glory be to You, O One who corrects the error of those who call upon You by not answering them, and by this You protect us from harm. How often does a person ask for evil while he thinks it is good!"

And in this verse, ﴿So call upon God, making your religion sincere for Him, even though the disbelievers dislike it﴾, there is an exhortation to us to outwit the disbelievers and enrage them by manifesting humility before God and submission to Him, glory be to Him. This matter vexes them, because it shows them the might of lordship and the greatness of God Most High, whom they disbelieved in, whom they refused to obey, and toward whom they were arrogant, glory be to Him. Therefore, persist in supplication in their presence, and show them from yourselves the utmost humility before God.

Commentary of al-Sha'rawi (Tafsir al-Sha'rawi, surahs 1-53, fragments of 54-66) on surah 40, verse 15:

The word (rafīʿ) is on the pattern (faʿīl) from the verb rafaʿa (to raise). This pattern can carry the meaning of the active participle, as in (raḥīm), an intensive form of rāḥim (merciful), and it can carry the meaning of the passive participle, as in qatīl, meaning maqtūl (killed). Likewise, the word (rafīʿ) may be understood as meaning "one who raises." That is, He, glory be to Him, raises others, just as He, glory be to Him, raises some of creation above others.

It is also valid for (rafīʿ) to mean the passive sense, that is, "elevated in His essence." The one who raises others can only raise them if he is elevated in himself. So (rafīʿ) here means "elevated above everything," just as we say: Allah is greater (Allāhu akbar), and Allah is higher and more majestic.

So God, exalted be He, is elevated in existence, because His existence is eternal, not after non-existence. Our existence, however, is after non-existence. His existence, glory be to Him, endures, while our existence tends toward non-existence. He, glory be to Him, exists in Himself, while our existence is through Him, glory be to Him. Therefore, He, glory be to Him, is the most exalted in existence. Yes.

God, glory be to Him, is elevated in His self-subsistence (qayyūmiyyah). We work, become tired, and sleep in order to rest, but He, glory be to Him, is not overtaken by any labour, nor does He sleep to rest. Therefore He, glory be to Him, said: ﴿Allah – there is no deity except Him, the Ever-Living, the Sustainer of existence. Neither drowsiness overtakes Him nor sleep﴾ [al-Baqarah: 255]. It is as if the Truth, glory be to Him, is saying to us: Sleep, you, with your eyes full, for I am not overtaken by drowsiness or sleep. He wants us to feel secure while we are in His care, glory be to Him.

By this self-subsistence Allah raises whom He wills, and by the absoluteness of His power, glory be to Him, He keeps whom He wills in elevation and brings down whom He wills to lowliness. ﴿Say: O Allah, Owner of sovereignty, You give sovereignty to whom You will, and You take sovereignty from whom You will. You honour whom You will, and You humble whom You will﴾ [Āl ʿImrān: 26].

As for His saying: ﴿rafīʿ al-darajāt﴾ (Exalted in degrees), because raising implies a higher station than another station, and these are the "darajāt" (degrees), that is, what lies between each station and another. Degrees exist only in ascent, whereas descent to a lower place is called its stages, "darakāt" (descending ranks).

The Truth, glory be to Him, raises among His creation whom He wills as He wills. He raised among time Ramadan above the other months, and among places He raised the Sacred House and Bayt al-Maqdis. Among the angels He raised them, as in His saying, related on the tongue of the angels: ﴿There is none of us but has a known station﴾ [al-Ṣāffāt: 164].

Among the messengers He raised those of firm resolve (ulū al-ʿazm), as He said: ﴿Those messengers – We preferred some of them over others﴾ [al-Baqarah: 253]. And He raises the common people of creation, as He, glory be to Him, said: ﴿Allah will raise those of you who believe and those who have been given knowledge by degrees﴾ [al-Mujādilah: 11]. And just as Allah, glory be to Him, raised the people of knowledge (ulū al-ʿilm), He likewise raised the people of activity in life, who have not been given knowledge but have a motion that executes this knowledge, applies it, and realises its aim in life. Knowledge in its execution needs a working hand, like the people of crafts, labourers, and artisans. Therefore He, glory be to Him, said: ﴿And it is He who made you successors upon the earth and raised some of you above others in degrees﴾ [al-Anʿām: 165].

So: there is an elevation of time, an elevation of place, an elevation of the angels, an elevation of the prophets, an elevation of the believers, an elevation of the people of knowledge, and finally an elevation of the creatures on earth. Consider the divine justice in the elevation of the successors over one another.

The Truth, glory be to Him, did not tell us which part is raised and over which part it is raised, to show us that every part is raised in something and raised above in something else. So the rich is not raised over the poor, nor the beautiful over the ugly, nor the clever over the dull; rather each is raised according to his deeds, as stated in His saying: ﴿O mankind, indeed We have created you from male and female and made you peoples and tribes that you may know one another. Indeed, the most noble of you in the sight of Allah is the most righteous of you. Indeed, Allah is Knowing and Acquainted﴾ [al-Ḥujurāt: 13].

Thus every creature, other than those already mentioned whom Allah has raised, is raised in something and raised above in something else. The carpenter who makes me a desk is raised above me in this work and is preferred over me in it, because he knows this craft and masters it, and I do not know it.

If this worker then asks me about a matter in which I am raised above him, because I know it and he does not, then we have said that the Truth, glory be to Him, willed that the movement of life among creatures be built on need, not on favour. Each of us needs the other, and the movement of his life is not complete except by the other.

Had the movement of life been based on favour, most interests would have stopped and life would not have been upright. Imagine that we all graduated from university and became scholars: who would perform the other works? Who would sweep the street? Who would work in the sewers? Who would sell in the markets? And so on. This is what the poet meant when he said:

The people, to the people, whether nomadic or settled, are some servants to others, even if they do not know it.

So none of us is merely a servant; rather each of us is made to serve in something and is served in something else. Therefore He, exalted be He, when teaching us this lesson, says: ﴿O you who have believed, let not a people ridicule another people; perhaps they may be better than them, nor let women ridicule other women; perhaps they may be better than them﴾ [al-Ḥujurāt: 11].

Therefore do not look at one work as superior to another work; rather there is a worker better than another worker, and the better is the one who perfects his work more. The worker who perfects his work in a lowly matter is better than the worker who does not perfect his work in a lofty one.

Hence Imam ʿAlī, may Allah honour his face, said: "The worth of every person is what he does well." Whoever wishes to attain superiority in elevation should perfect his work, whatever this work may be, however humble it seems in the eyes of some of us. There is no lowly work in Islam; rather there is a lowly worker, who is the negligent one who does not excel, does not perfect what is in his hand, and is not sincere in it...

As for His saying: ﴿Lord of the Throne [dhū al-ʿarsh]﴾ [Ghāfir: 15], it means: the one who possesses a dominion that is settled for Him without any strife against Him, the one established in the perfection of His power and divinity. A king is not granted to sit and settle upon his throne except after his affair is firmly established for him, with the difference between His sitting and settling upon His throne, glory be to Him, and the sitting of the kings of this world upon their thrones. We believe in this sitting without modality (takyīf) or likening (tashbīh). Since His existence is not like our existence, so His sitting is not like our sitting. We have said that we take these matters within the frame of: ﴿There is nothing like Him﴾ [al-Shūrā: 11].

The Truth, glory be to Him and exalted be He, had His affair firmly established over the universe without any rival, as evidenced by His saying: ﴿Then He turned to the heaven while it was smoke, and said to it and to the earth: Come willingly or by compulsion. They said: We come willingly, obedient﴾ [Fuṣṣilat: 11].

And since He, glory be to Him, is Lord of the high degrees and Lord of the Throne, He wished to bestow from His elevation upon those who believe in Him, to raise them above others, and not to leave them unguided and without a method. Therefore He sent down to them a spirit (rūḥ) from Him, glory be to Him: ﴿He sends down the spirit by His command upon whom He wills of His servants﴾.

He, glory be to Him, would not enslave creation and then abandon them; rather He sent down for them the method that governs their movement in life: do this, and do not do that. This is the law of protection that guarantees for mankind righteousness, elevation, and loftiness of station. He made this method a matter of choice: whoever wills, let him believe, and whoever wills, let him disbelieve; whoever wills, let him obey, and whoever wills, let him disobey. So that the believer may see the effect of Allah's elevation of him in the Hereafter, when He admits him to Paradise, the abode of enduring bliss, where there is no loss of blessing and no death of existence.

This method has come to us in the Book of Allah and in the Sunnah of His Messenger ﷺ, organising the movement of our life so that movements complete one another and do not collide. When you see the law of Allah restricting your movement in something, know that it has restricted the movements of millions for your sake. When it forbids you theft, for example, it restricts your movement as an individual and prevents your hand from reaching what you do not own; and in return it restricts millions of hands so that they do not reach what is yours. When it commands you to lower your gaze and guard what is forbidden, it commands all creatures to lower their gaze from what is forbidden to you... and so on. So reflect: who is the beneficiary of applying this method?

As for His saying: ﴿yulqī al-rūḥ [He sends down the spirit]﴾, the word "rūḥ" has several meanings. What first comes to mind is the spirit that moves in matter and grants it life and movement; this is the spirit that the Creator, glory be to Him, breathed into Adam, so that he moved, and all the limbs performed their functions after having been clay.

Then He, glory be to Him, wished to guard the movement of matter so that it does not speak in its appetites, and so He sent down another spirit from Him, glory be to Him, which is the value-based method in the Noble Qur'an. Therefore He, glory be to Him, said: ﴿O you who have believed, respond to Allah and to the Messenger when He calls you to that which gives you life﴾ [al-Anfāl: 24].

How does He give them life when they are living and addressed by these words? Yes, they are alive with the life of matter, by the spirit that moved in their bodies, so they moved by it. But what is meant here is a life higher than the life of matter: the life of values, which elevates the movement of man and always keeps it in good for himself and for those around him. Just as the life of matter has a spirit, so the life of values has a spirit.

Therefore He called the Qur'an a spirit, and He called the one who descended with it from the angels a spirit. He, glory be to Him, said: ﴿And thus We revealed to you a spirit from Our command﴾ [al-Shūrā: 52].

And He said: ﴿The Trustworthy Spirit has descended with it﴾ [al-Shuʿarā': 193].

These are the life of values and sublime ideals, the life that qualifies you for another enduring life that does not perish. You may weigh a life that qualifies you for the transient world against a life that qualifies you for the enduring Hereafter; you will surely find the second spirit greater and better than the first.

It suffices to distinguish between them that the first spirit, the spirit of matter, flows through both the believer and the disbeliever, and by this spirit comes the disbelief of the disbeliever and the sin of the sinner. But the spirit of the method and values is found only in the believer, and it moves him only toward good, a sound movement that makes him happy and makes those around him happy in this world before the Hereafter.

Therefore He, glory be to Him, said: ﴿And indeed, the Home of the Hereafter – that is the [true] life, if they only knew﴾ [al-ʿAnkabūt: 64]. The meaning of "al-Ḥayawān" is: the real, lasting, enduring life whose bliss does not end and which no extinction can reach. Although the bliss of mankind in this world is according to the measure of their movement and capabilities, their bliss in the Hereafter is according to the measure of the Bestower, glory be to Him.

Then you live in this world exposed to death, which threatens you at every moment, and may strike you suddenly. It has no fixed time or age, and no cause that it is tied to. Some of us die after a year, some after a hundred years, and some die while still in their mother's womb. Death does not distinguish between the old and the young, or between the sick and the healthy. Therefore Allah left it undetermined. Why? So that we may remain constantly mindful of it, awaiting its onslaught. Thus the vagueness here is itself the clearest explanation.

Therefore the Truth, glory be to Him, alerts us to this matter in His saying: ﴿Blessed is He in whose hand is dominion, and He is over all things competent. He who created death and life to test you as to which of you is best in deed﴾ [al-Mulk: 1-2].

Reflect on ﴿He created death and life﴾ [al-Mulk: 2]: He began with death and placed it before life, as if He, glory be to Him, were saying to us: do not face life except with death in your minds. Why? Because remembering death prevents delusion with the world and inclination toward it, and it disciplines human conduct, so that he moves only toward good, for he always takes into account the consequences awaiting him.

As for His saying, glory be to Him: ﴿upon whom He wills of His servants﴾, it means: upon whom He chooses and purifies for this station. This is like His saying: ﴿Allah chooses messengers from the angels and from mankind﴾ [al-Ḥajj: 75].

And His saying: ﴿Allah knows best where to place His message﴾ [al-Anʿām: 124].

Then the Truth, glory be to Him, clarifies the reason for His saying: ﴿He sends down the spirit by His command upon whom He wills of His servants﴾. Why? ﴿That he may warn of the Day of Meeting﴾. That is: beware lest you understand that the matter ends with the end of worldly life, and that the people of sins escape with their sins, and the people of injustice with their injustice. No! Rather there is a return and a retreat to this God whom you disbelieved in or whose prohibitions you disobeyed and dared to violate. Remember this truth, however far you turn away from Him through disbelief, or however your side deviates from the side of your Lord. You are returned to Him against your will, standing before Him, with no escape from Him ever, and no refuge.

We have said that warning means frightening someone about an evil before its time, so that he may prepare for it by avoiding the causes of what frightens him, in order to be safe from it. There is no sense in a warning at the moment the event occurs; it must be some time before the occurrence, sufficient to enable me to take precautions and reckon with the matter.

As for His saying, "the Day of Meeting" (yawm al-talāq), that is: the meeting (al-talāq), and a meeting arises only from a separation that existed between two things. So between which things will this meeting occur? They said: the meeting here, with the intended meaning of the Day of Resurrection, will be in several forms. In the Hereafter you will see the angels in whom you believed in the world with unseen faith, and you will meet them in direct witness.

In the Hereafter you will see your kin and your extended family, from your father Adam to the last child born to him in the world; you will meet them all. You will see the womb (raḥim) that you severed in the world; this great tree with intertwined branches and overlapping boughs will take shape before you, and then you will say: how did I sever this womb, and how did I neglect these near relations, for a cause or without a cause? Therefore the Prophet ﷺ said: "You are all from Adam, and Adam is from dust..."

Among the meetings that will occur in the Hereafter is that the wronged meets his wrongdoer, and the adversary meets his opponent. Yes, on the day of Allah adversaries are gathered, and the intelligent person must reckon a thousand reckonings for this meeting, and whoever reflects on consequences is saved.

Among the meetings in the Hereafter is that a person meets the record of his deeds, which has counted every small and great thing: ﴿Allah has enumerated it while they have forgotten it﴾ [al-Mujādilah: 6].

﴿The Day every soul will find what it has done of good present, and what it has done of evil, it will wish there were between it and that a great distance﴾ [Āl ʿImrān: 30].

On the day when your Lord says to you: ﴿Read your record. Sufficient is yourself against you this day as a reckoner﴾ [al-Isrā': 14].

Then the meeting rises to its peak, as the believers meet their Lord, Mighty and Majestic, when He manifests Himself to them and they see Him. This is the greatest of blessings, by the grace and generosity of Allah. Read: ﴿Faces that Day will be radiant, looking at their Lord﴾ [al-Qiyāmah: 22-23]; ﴿And faces that Day will be overcast, expecting that something of calamity will be done to them﴾ [al-Qiyāmah: 24-25].

And if seeing the Truth, glory be to Him, is the greatest blessing for the believers, it is the most severe torment for the disbelievers, because they will be deprived of it: ﴿No! Indeed, they, from their Lord that Day, will be veiled﴾ [al-Muṭaffifīn: 15]. On that day their regret and grief will intensify: ﴿And those who disbelieved, their deeds are like a mirage in a bare plain, which the thirsty one thinks is water; until when he comes to it, he finds it to be nothing, and finds Allah with him, and He will pay him in full his account. And Allah is swift in account﴾ [al-Nūr: 39].

He found Allah, whom he had disbelieved in during the world, and he found the outcome of which we had repeatedly warned him and reminded him.

Commentary of al-Sha'rawi (Tafsir al-Sha'rawi, surahs 1-53, fragments of 54-66) on surah 40, verse 16 (part 1 of 2):

The word (رَفيع) (rafi') is on the pattern (فعيل) (fa'il) from the verb rafa'a (to raise). This pattern can carry the meaning of the active agent, as in (رحيم) (rahim), an intensive form of (راحم) (rahim/merciful, from rahim). It can also carry the meaning of the passive, as in (قتيل) (qatil), meaning (مقتول) (maqtul, slain). Likewise, the word (رفيع) (rafi') may be understood as (بمعنى رافع) (meaning raise/raising). That is, He, glory be to Him, raises others, just as He, glory be to Him, raises some of creation above others.

It is also valid for (رفيع) (rafi') to carry the passive sense, that is, exalted in His essence. One who raises others can only do so if he is exalted in himself. So here (رفيع) (rafi') means exalted above everything, just as we say: Allah is the Greatest, Allah is the Highest and the Most Majestic.

So Allah, may He be exalted, is exalted in His existence, because His existence is eternal and not from non-existence. As for our existence, it is from non-existence. His existence, glory be to Him, is everlasting, while our existence is heading toward annihilation. He, glory be to Him, exists by His own essence, while our existence is by Him, glory be to Him. Therefore, He, glory be to Him, is the most exalted in existence, yes.

Allah, glory be to Him, is exalted in His self-subsistence (qayyumiyyah). We work, we tire, and we sleep in order to rest. But He, glory be to Him, is not followed by work, nor does He sleep to rest. Therefore He, glory be to Him, said: ﴿Allah, there is no god but Him, the Living, the Self-Subsisting. Neither drowsiness nor sleep overtakes Him﴾ [al-Baqarah: 255]. It is as if the Truth, glory be to Him, is saying to us: Sleep, you, to your heart's content, for I am not overtaken by drowsiness or sleep. He wants us to be at ease while we are in His care, glory be to Him.

By this self-subsistence, Allah raises whom He wills, and by the absoluteness of His power, glory be to Him, He keeps whom He wills in elevation and brings down whom He wills to lowliness. ﴿Say: O Allah, Owner of sovereignty, You give sovereignty to whom You will, and You take sovereignty from whom You will, and You honor whom You will, and You humble whom You will﴾ [Al 'Imran: 26].

His saying: ﴿Exalted in degrees﴾ [Ghafir: 15]. Because raising implies a higher rank than another rank, and these are the degrees (darajat), that is, what lies between each rank and another. Degrees exist only in height, whereas descent downward has its stages called (دركات) (darakat, levels of descent).

The Truth, glory be to Him, raises from His creation whom He wills, in the manner He wills. He raised among time Ramadan above other months, and among places He raised the Sacred House (al-Bayt al-Haram) and Bayt al-Maqdis (Jerusalem). He raised among the angels, as in His saying on the tongue of the angels: ﴿And there is none of us but has a known station﴾ [al-Saffat: 164].

He raised among the messengers those of firm resolve (Ulu al-'Azm) from among them, as He said: ﴿Those messengers — We preferred some of them over others﴾ [al-Baqarah: 253]. And He raises among the general creation, as He, glory be to Him, said: ﴿Allah will raise those of you who believe and those who have been given knowledge by degrees﴾ [al-Mujadilah: 11]. And just as Allah, glory be to Him, raised the people of knowledge (Ulu al-'Ilm), He also raised the people of action in life, who have not been given knowledge but have a drive that carries out this knowledge, applies it, and realizes its aim in life. Knowledge in its implementation needs a working hand, like craftsmen, laborers, and artisans. Therefore He, glory be to Him, said: ﴿And it is He who made you successors upon the earth and raised some of you above others by degrees﴾ [al-An'am: 165].

So, we have an elevation of time, an elevation of place, an elevation of the angels, an elevation of the prophets, an elevation of the believers, an elevation of the people of knowledge, and finally an elevation of the creatures on earth. Consider the divine justice in the elevation of the successors over one another.

The Truth, glory be to Him, did not tell us which part is raised and over which part it is raised, in order to show us that every part is raised in one thing and raised over others in another thing. Therefore the rich is not raised over the poor, nor the beautiful over the ugly, nor the intelligent over the dull. Rather, each is raised according to his deeds, as stated in His saying: ﴿O mankind, indeed We have created you from male and female and made you peoples and tribes that you may know one another. Indeed, the most noble of you in the sight of Allah is the most righteous of you. Indeed, Allah is Knowing and Acquainted﴾ [al-Hujurat: 13].

So all creation, apart from what has been mentioned, whom Allah has raised, is raised in one thing and raised over others in another thing. The carpenter who makes me a desk is raised above me in this work and is more excellent than me in it, because he knows this craft and masters it, and I do not know it. When this worker comes and asks me about a matter in which I am raised above him, because I know it and he does not, we have said: the Truth, glory be to Him, wanted the movement of life among creatures to be built on need, not on favor. Each of us needs the other, and the movement of his life is not complete except through the other.

If the movement of life were based on favor, most interests would be halted and life would not be set right. Imagine that we all graduated from university and became scholars: who would then perform the other works? Who would sweep the street? Who would work in the sewers? Who would sell in the markets? Etc. This is the intended meaning of the poet who said:

People, through nomads and settled folk, serve one another, even if they do not know it.

So none of us is only a servant. Rather, each of us is a servant in one thing and served in another. Therefore He says, while teaching us this lesson: ﴿O you who have believed, let not a people ridicule [another] people; perhaps they may be better than them. And let not women ridicule [other] women; perhaps they may be better than them﴾ [al-Hujurat: 11].

So do not regard one work as better than another work. Rather, there is a better worker than another worker, and the better one is the one who perfects his work more. A worker who perfects his work in a lowly task is better than a worker who does not perfect his work in a higher task.

Therefore Imam 'Ali, may Allah honor his face, said: (The value of every person is what he does well). So whoever seeks excellence in height, let him perfect his work, whatever that work may be, however base it may seem in the eyes of some of us. There is no base work in Islam; rather, there is a base worker, namely the negligent one who does not do well or perfect what is in his hand and is not sincere in it.

We had earlier given an example from France and from the debates of the French National Assembly, where they presented us with some decisive positions from these debates. Among them: the labor union head was very demanding on behalf of workers and would exaggerate in that, but the minister responsible for implementing these demands was governed by budgets, figures, and calculations.

Time passed, and this labor union head became Minister of Labour. The new labor union head stood before him saying: I only ask of you what you used to ask of your predecessor. He said: But I am governed by budgets and calculations. So he (the union head) wanted to stir his sentiment toward the workers, or wanted to embarrass him, and said to him: Do not forget that at one time you were a shoe-shiner. The minister received it with an open heart and a sporting spirit, and replied: Yes, yes, but I used to do it well. So: greatness is not in the work itself, but in doing it well.

Therefore we say: If the worker who is sincere in his work and perfects it knew what he accomplishes for the experiences of faith in Allah (in that he perfects and does well his work for Allah, from the unseen of the employer), he would take pride in this work over the scholars. They said: How is that? And what does the worker contribute to the experiences of faith? We say: Because everyone who sees his perfected work says: Allah! So the perfected work spreads the word of beauty in the universe and leads to the remembrance of Allah, and in this there is reward that is hidden from no one.

His saying, the Exalted: ﴿Lord of the Throne﴾ [Ghafir: 15] means: the One who possesses a universe that is settled for Him without disorder against Him, and who is established in complete power and divinity. A king is not permitted to sit and be seated on his throne until his affair is firmly settled for him, with the difference between His sitting and seating upon His throne, glory be to Him, and the sitting of the kings of this world on their thrones. We believe in this sitting without modality (takyif) or likening (tashbih). Since His existence, may He be exalted, is not like our existence, so His sitting is not like our sitting. We have said that we take these matters within the framework of ﴿There is nothing like unto Him﴾ [al-Shura: 11].

The Truth, glory be to Him and exalted, has His affair firmly settled in the universe without any rival, as evidenced by His saying, glory be to Him: ﴿Then He turned to the heaven while it was smoke and said to it and to the earth: Come, willingly or by compulsion. They said: We come willingly, obedient﴾ [Fussilat: 11].

And because He, glory be to Him, is Exalted in Degrees and He, glory be to Him, is Lord of the Throne, He wills to bestow some of His elevation upon those who believe in Him, to raise them above others, and not to leave them neglected and unguided without a method. Therefore He sent down to them a spirit (ruh) from Him, glory be to Him:

﴿He casts the Spirit of His command upon whom He wills of His servants﴾ [Ghafir: 15].

He, glory be to Him, would not enslave creatures and then abandon them. Rather, He sent down for them the method that governs their movement in life: do this, and do not do that. This is the law of protection that guarantees for humans righteousness, elevation, and loftiness of rank. He made this method a matter of choice: whoever wills, let him believe, and whoever wills, let him disbelieve; whoever wills, let him obey, and whoever wills, let him disobey. So that the believer may see the effect of Allah's elevation of him in the Hereafter, when He admits him into Paradise, the abode of lasting bliss, where there is no loss of blessing and no death of existence.

This method has come to us in the Book of Allah and in the Sunnah of His Messenger, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, organizing the movement of our lives so that movements are complete and do not collide. When you see the Shari'ah of Allah restricting your movement in something, know that it restricts the movements of millions for your sake. For example, when it forbids you from theft, it restricts your movement as an individual and prevents your hand from reaching for what you do not own. In return, it restricts millions of hands so that they do not reach for your property. When it commands you to lower your gaze and guard what is forbidden, it commands all people to lower their gazes from what is forbidden to you, etc. So reflect: who is the beneficiary of applying this method?

His saying: ﴿He casts the Spirit﴾ [Ghafir: 15]. The word "spirit" (ruh) has several meanings. What first comes to mind is that it is the spirit that animates matter and gives it life and movement. This is the spirit that the Creator, glory be to Him, breathed into Adam, so he moved, and all the limbs performed their functions after having been clay.

Then He, glory be to Him, wanted to guard the movement of matter so that it would not give way to its desires, so He sent down another spirit from Him, glory be to Him, which is the value-based method in the Noble Qur'an. Therefore He, glory be to Him, said: ﴿O you who have believed, respond to Allah and to the Messenger when He calls you to that which gives you life﴾ [al-Anfal: 24].

How does it give them life when they are living and being addressed with these words? Yes, they are alive with the life of matter, by the spirit that animated their bodies so that they moved by it. But what is meant here is a life higher than the life of matter: the life of values, which elevates human movement and keeps it always in goodness for himself and for those around him. Just as the life of matter has a spirit, so the life of values has a spirit.

Therefore He named the Qur'an a spirit, and He named the angel who brought it down a spirit. He, glory be to Him, said: ﴿And thus We have revealed to you a spirit of Our command﴾ [al-Shura: 52].

And He said: ﴿The Trustworthy Spirit has brought it down﴾ [al-Shu'ara': 193].

This is the life of values and lofty ideals, the life that qualifies you for another life that remains and does not perish. You may compare between a life that qualifies you for the transient world and a life that qualifies you for the enduring Hereafter. You will surely find the second spirit greater and better than the first.

It suffices to distinguish between them that the first spirit, the spirit of matter, flows in both the believer and the disbeliever, and by this spirit comes the disbelief of the disbeliever and the disobedience of the disobedient. But the spirit of the method and values exists only in the believer, and it moves him only toward good, a sound movement that makes him and those around him happy in this world before the next.

Therefore He, glory be to Him, said: ﴿And indeed, the Last Abode — that is the [true] Life, if they only knew﴾ [al-'Ankabut: 64]. The meaning of (الحيوان) (al-hayawan, the [true] life) is: the real, lasting, enduring life whose bliss does not end and which is not reached by annihilation. Although the bliss of humans in this world is according to the extent of their movement and capabilities, their bliss in the Hereafter is according to the extent of the One who bestows it, glory be to Him.

Then you live in this world exposed to death, which threatens you at every moment. It may strike you suddenly, having no fixed time or age, and no specific cause linked to it. Some of us die after a year, some after a hundred years, and some die while in their mother's womb. Death does not distinguish between old and young, nor between sick and healthy. Therefore Allah kept it vague. Why? So that we remain constantly remembering Him, awaiting its attack. Thus the vagueness here is itself the clarification.

Therefore the Truth, glory be to Him, alerts us to this matter in His saying: ﴿Blessed is He in whose hand is dominion, and He is over all things competent. He who created death and life to test you as to which of you is best in deed﴾ [al-Mulk: 1-2].

Reflect on ﴿He created death and life﴾ [al-Mulk: 2]. He began with death and placed it before life, as if He, glory be to Him, is saying to us: Do not face life except with death in your minds. Why? Because remembering death prevents delusion by the world and reliance upon it, and it governs human conduct, so he moves only toward good, because he always takes into account the consequences awaiting him.

His saying, glory be to Him: ﴿upon whom He wills of His servants﴾ [Ghafir: 15]. It means: upon whom He chooses and purifies for this rank. This is like His saying: ﴿Allah chooses messengers from among the angels and from among mankind﴾ [al-Hajj: 75].

And His saying, the Exalted: ﴿Allah knows best where to place His message﴾ [al-An'am: 124].

Then the Truth, glory be to Him, clarifies the reason for His saying: ﴿He casts the Spirit of His command upon whom He wills of His servants﴾ [Ghafir: 15]. Why? ﴿That he may warn of the Day of Meeting﴾ [Ghafir: 15]. Beware of understanding that the matter ends with the end of worldly life, and that those who commit sins escape with their sins, and those who do wrong escape with their wrongdoing. No. Rather, there is a return and a coming back to this God whom you disbelieved in or whom you disobeyed and dared to violate His sanctities. Remember this truth, however much you turn away from Him by disbelief or turn your side away from the side of your Lord. You are returned to Him against your will, stationed before Him, and there is no escape for you from Him ever, nor any refuge.

We have said that warning (al-indhar) means alarming someone about an evil before its time so that he may prepare for it by avoiding the causes of what alarms him, in order to be safe from them. There is no sense in warning at the moment the event occurs. It must be some sufficient time before the occurrence, enabling me to remedy the matter and take my precautions.

His saying: ﴿the Day of Meeting﴾ [Ghafir: 15], that is, the day of meeting (al-talaqi). Meeting arises only from a separation that existed between two things. So between which things is this meeting? They said: The meeting here, meaning the Day of Resurrection, will be in several forms. In the Hereafter you will see the angels in whom you believed in the world with unseen faith, and you will meet them in plain sight.

And in the Hereafter you will see your kin and your extended family from your father Adam down to the last child he has in the world. You will meet them all. You will see this kinship that you severed in the world. This great tree with intertwined branches and interlocked boughs will appear to you, and then you will say: How did I sever this kinship? And how did I neglect these close relations, for a reason or without a reason? Therefore the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, said: [...]. And the Truth, glory be to Him, says in the Sacred Hadith: [...].

And our master Mu'awiya ibn Abi Sufyan, may Allah be pleased with him, one day had his chamberlain enter upon him and say: O Commander of the Faithful, a man is at the door who says he is your brother. He said to him: Do you not know my brothers? He said: That is what the man says. He said: Let him in. When he entered upon Mu'awiya, he said to him: Which of my brothers are you? He said: I am your brother from Adam. Mu'awiya laughed and said: A severed kinship! By Allah, I will surely be the first to join it. Then he drew him near and gave him what he wanted.

Among the encounters that will take place in the Hereafter is that the oppressed will meet his oppressor, and the adversary will meet the one he disputed with. Indeed, the disputants will be gathered before God. The intelligent person should take this meeting into account a thousand times over, for whoever reflects on the consequences is saved.

Another encounter in the Hereafter is that a person meets the record of his deeds, which has counted against him every small and great thing: ﴿God has counted it, and they have forgotten it﴾ [al-Mujadila: 6]. ﴿On the Day when every soul will find what it has done of good brought forward, and what it has done of evil, it will wish that between it and that there were a great distance﴾ [Ali 'Imran: 30].

On the Day when your Lord says to you: ﴿Read your record. Sufficient is your soul against you this Day as a reckoner﴾ [al-Isra': 14].

Then the encounter rises to its peak, when the believers meet their Lord, Mighty and Majestic, when He manifests Himself to them and they see Him. This is the greatest of blessings, by God's bounty and generosity. Recite: ﴿Faces that Day will be radiant, looking toward their Lord﴾ [al-Qiyamah: 22-23], ﴿and faces that Day will be gloomy, thinking that a calamity is about to befall them﴾ [al-Qiyamah: 24-25].

If seeing the Truth, glorified is He, is the greatest blessing for the believers, it is also the most severe of torments for the disbelievers, because they will be deprived of it: ﴿Nay, indeed they will be, on that Day, veiled from their Lord﴾ [al-Mutaffifin: 15]. On that day their regret and grief will intensify: ﴿And those who disbelieved, their deeds are like a mirage in a level plain, which the thirsty one thinks is water, until, when he comes to it, he finds it to be nothing, and finds God with him, and He pays him his account in full. And God is swift in reckoning﴾ [al-Nur: 39].

He found God, whom he disbelieved in during the world, and he found the consequence which we had repeatedly warned him of and reminded him of.

And His saying, exalted is He: ﴿The Day they will come forth, nothing of them will be hidden from God﴾ [Ghafir: 16]. That is: on this Day of Encounter they will come forth openly, after having been concealed by their misdeeds in the world. On this Day their affair will be exposed and their cover removed. ﴿Nothing of them will be hidden from God﴾ [Ghafir: 16]. All are in one arena: the kings and the common people, the masters and the slaves, the leaders and the led, all in the station of servitude.

Therefore, the Truth, glorified is He, will call out: ﴿Whose is the dominion this Day?﴾ [Ghafir: 16]. The Truth, glorified is He, says this because He used to give some of us dominion in the world, but in the Hereafter there is no dominion except for God alone. Therefore, to this question the believer and the disbeliever both respond, all saying ﴿To God, the One, the Subduer﴾ [Ghafir: 16]. Yes, because there is no god besides Him and no sovereign other than Him.

The meaning of ﴿Whose is the dominion this Day?﴾ [Ghafir: 16] is that dominion belongs to God today and before today. This is the truth which the disbelievers denied in the world, and which the believers, who were content with God as Lord, acknowledged: He gives dominion to whom He wills, takes dominion away from whom He wills, honors whom He wills, and humiliates whom He wills.

The word ﴿this Day﴾ is here directed at the disbelievers who denied this truth in their worldly life, but they acknowledged it in the Hereafter and affirmed ﴿To God, the One, the Subduer﴾ [Ghafir: 16].

**Commentary of al-Sha'rawi (Tafsir al-Sha'rawi, surahs 1-53, fragments of 54-66) on surah 40, verse 17:**

﴿Today﴾ means the Day of Resurrection. ﴿Every soul will be recompensed﴾, meaning held to account, ﴿for what it has earned﴾ [Ghafir: 17]. We have said that *kasaba* (to earn) is used for good and *iktasaba* (to acquire) for evil. The linguists say that every increase in the structure of a word must correspond to an increase in its meaning, so *kasaba* differs from *iktasaba*. *Kasaba* follows the pattern *fa'ala*, meaning the action comes from you naturally, without effort. *Iktasaba* means *if'talaba*, which carries the sense of *ifti'al* (exertion) and attempt.

Good requires no effort from you, unlike evil, which requires toil, hardship and stealth. He, may He be exalted, says: ﴿For it is what it has earned, and against it is what it has acquired﴾ [Al-Baqarah: 286]. We have clarified this matter with the example of a man who sits among his family, where there are beautiful women: his wife, his daughters, his maternal and paternal aunts, and so on. He looks at this beauty without strain or embarrassment. But with women who are not within his mahram (those he may never marry), he steals a glance, is stirred by it, and tries to make sure no one sees him.

We also notice this matter in a woman who carries a child from lawful union and another who carries one from unlawful union. The first boasts of her pregnancy and takes pride in it, while the other strives hard to hide it and rid herself of it. The joy of the first and the grief of the second is the difference between the lawful and the unlawful.

Likewise, when a person takes something from his own house, he takes it openly, without strain and without planning. But if he wants to steal from the houses of others, he schemes for it and plans it. So we say: the lawful does not exhaust its owner, but the unlawful exhausts the whole world.

As for His saying: ﴿Yes, whoever earns an evil deed...﴾ [Al-Baqarah: 81], here *kasaba* is used for evil. Why? They said: this is when the evil deed becomes familiar and habitual to its doer, who does it without strain or hardship to himself, as though it were a good deed. Once he has become accustomed to it, it becomes for him *kasb* (earning) rather than *iktisab* (acquiring). This is what we call *al-Faqid* (the one who has lost his sense of restraint): the one who has grown bold in what is forbidden and has become so familiar with sin that it has become a habit for him.

Similar to this is the matter of the gaze, in His saying: ﴿He knows the treachery of the eyes﴾ [Ghafir: 19]. So there is a treacherous eye and a trustworthy eye: the trustworthy eye is the one that looks at what is lawful, and the treacherous eye is the one that looks at what is forbidden.

Even in the economic domain, which governs peoples and by which the progress and advancement of nations is measured, we say: the lawful does not burden, but it is the unlawful that burdens. This is from the economic perspective, because the basic principle regarding the lawful is ﴿Eat and drink, but do not be excessive﴾ [Al-A'raf: 31]. In the noble hadith: "If we lived by these principles, little would suffice us." You may test yourself: do not eat except when hungry, and then you will find the morsel delicious even if it is only with salt. Your steadfastness upon the religion of God thus brings you comfort and covers you, and does not exhaust you in the movement of life, nor require of you more work or more wealth.

Likewise, when we eat, we are not satisfied, and you see the one who eats until he suffers indigestion and needs a digestive remedy. He has burdened himself with food and with the disposal of food.

Then He, glorified be He, says: ﴿No injustice today﴾ [Ghafir: 17]. Yes, because the judge on this day is God, the absolute Just. It is as though the Truth, glorified be He, is saying: injustice is your concern, O humans. We granted you respite in the world, where you rule through injustice: the strong oppresses the weak, the rich oppresses the poor, and the ruler oppresses the ruled. But today ﴿there is no injustice﴾ [Ghafir: 17], for when injustice reached its utmost limit in the world, it was because you associated partners with God.

Therefore He, glorified be He, said: ﴿Indeed, associating partners with God is a great injustice﴾ [Luqman: 13]. Yes, it is a clear and manifest injustice, because injustice means taking for yourself the right of another, or taking a right from its owner and giving it to someone other than its owner. This is what you did when you associated partners with God: you took from Him, glorified be He, divinity and gave it to idols.

Injustice comes in several forms. Among injustice is doing good and not being repaid for it with good. Among injustice is doing a good deed for which you deserve ten, yet being given five. Among injustice is doing an evil deed and not being held accountable for it. And among injustice is not doing an evil deed yet being held accountable for it.

So every disruption of the balance of ownership and benefit from labour is considered injustice. For this reason He, the Exalted, said in the Hadith Qudsi: "This was in the world." As for the Hereafter, you will stand before the just Judge, in the sphere of absolute justice that shows no partiality to one at the expense of another. He has no son and no consort, so He does not deviate from the truth for their sake.

Therefore we have said: the jinn were more truthful in their reception than we were, when they said: ﴿And that He, exalted is the majesty of our Lord, He has taken neither a consort nor a son﴾ [Al-Jinn: 3]. This is because most corruption comes from these two: the consort and the son.

His saying, glorified be He: ﴿Indeed, God is swift in reckoning﴾ [Ghafir: 17] points to the perfection of His power in judging between people and recompensing them for their deeds. It is as though He is saying to us: beware of thinking that the standing for reckoning is difficult for Us, or that it will take a long time. No, We have other reckonings. We have no session that drags on, nor a session that is postponed.

﴿Indeed, God is swift in reckoning﴾ [Ghafir: 17], because God, exalted is He, does His act with "Be" (*kun*), not with treatment as you do. The evidence for this is that in the world of people there are thousands and millions of judges who judge between people with truth, across thousands and millions of lands, at the same time, in different countries and different courts. The truth by which they judge is not a truth passed from one judge to another. Rather, it is a gift that has dissolved into all their souls, and a colouring that has coloured all their judgments.

If the creature, by God's grace, is able to take hold of the souls of judges across the various lands at one time, then the One who created this truth is more worthy of judging among all creatures at one time.

For this reason, when Imam Ali, may God be pleased with him, was asked this question: "How will people be held to account at one time despite their multitude?" He said: "As He provides for them all at one time."

Al-Sha'rawi said: We say: al-Inqadh (warning) is informing and cautioning about evil before it occurs. Al-Azifah comes from azifa al-shay', meaning it drew near and came close. The intended "Day of al-Azifah" is death, because it comes suddenly and no one knows its appointed time; or it is the Day of Resurrection, which is also near, because Allah the Exalted says about it: ﴿The command of Allah has come, so do not seek to hasten it...﴾ [al-Nahl: 1]. So He used the past tense (atā, "has come") to indicate the certainty and nearness of its occurrence, since everything that is coming is near.

On this Day of al-Azifah, ﴿when the hearts will be at the throats, choking with grief...﴾ [Ghafir: 18]. Imagine that the heart has come loose from its place in the chest and left its position until it reaches the throats, stifling the breath from the intensity of the terror, the distress, the misery and the constriction. As He, glorified is He, said in another place: ﴿And when the eyes will be dazed, and the hearts will reach the throats, and you will think about Allah various thoughts﴾ [al-Ahzab: 10].

The meaning of ﴿kāzimīn﴾ [Ghafir: 18] is al-kazm (suppressing): that you try to hold something inside you so that it does not come out. From it comes kazm al-qirba (tying off a waterskin) when it is torn, so that water does not leak out, by binding the place of the tear and securing its tie. From it also comes kazm al-ghayz (suppressing anger): you control your anger, hold it within yourself, and do not carry it out, as Allah the Exalted said: ﴿And those who suppress anger and pardon people...﴾ [Al 'Imran: 134]. This is an ascent through the ranks of righteous deeds: the first of them is suppressing anger; better than that is dispelling anger through pardon; and better than that is ﴿And Allah loves the doers of good﴾ [Al 'Imran: 134].

As for His saying: ﴿The wrongdoers will have no close friend (hamim) nor any intercessor who will be obeyed﴾ [Ghafir: 18], this is the hour when Allah gathers the wrongdoers together in Hell, may Allah protect us. These people gathered in the world upon disobedience to Allah and walked in it according to their desires, and now in the Hereafter some of them flee from others, and the followed one runs away from his follower, as He, glorified is He, said: ﴿On the Day a man will flee from his brother, and his mother and his father, and his companion and his children. For every man among them, that Day, there will be a matter that preoccupies him﴾ [Abasa: 34-37].

Likewise, they will find no intercessor who will intercede for them or defend them. Allah, the Truth, has made clear that these intercessors, the leaders of the people and the imams of disbelief, will precede their followers into Hell; when they enter they will find that the followers have preceded them into it. That is more severing of their hope for salvation and more intense for their regret. Therefore He said about Pharaoh: ﴿He will lead his people on the Day of Resurrection and bring them to the Fire, and wretched is the watering-place to which they are brought﴾ [Hud: 98].

The meaning of (al-hamim) is the intimate friend, the one who is sincere to you, who protects you when harm is intended against you and stands by your side in time of hardship. The wrongdoer in the Hereafter finds neither this friend nor anyone who will intercede for him; their friends have fled from them, because they gathered in the world upon sin.

And Allah says: ﴿The intimate friends on that Day will be enemies to one another, except the righteous﴾ [al-Zukhruf: 67]; that is, on the Day of Resurrection each of them disowns his companion, blames him, and hates him. ﴿Nor any intercessor who will be obeyed﴾ [Ghafir: 18]: even if an intercessor stands for the wrongdoer to intercede for him, he will not be obeyed, because intercession in the Hereafter has conditions: that Allah permits the intercessor to intercede, and that Allah is pleased with the one for whom intercession is made; and Allah does not permit intercession for a wrongdoer nor is He pleased with him.

Therefore such intercession is not accepted, and its performer is not obeyed, because he asks of Allah, who holds the punishment, to obey him and to pardon the one for whom he intercedes. How could the Truth, glorified is He, become obedient to His servant?

Commentary of al-Sha'rawi (Tafsir al-Sha'rawi, surahs 1-53, fragments of 54-66) on surah 40, verse 19:

Meaning: Know that Allah's knowledge encompasses everything, and nothing is hidden from Him, however subtle it may be. If you blind people in this world to what is in the sight of Allah's creation and steal glances at what is not lawful for you, then know that you are not hidden from Allah. Had the believer been certain of the comprehensiveness of Allah's knowledge and of His watching over him, the stealing of glances (khā'innat al-a'yun) would never have been part of him.

Thus we have seen a judge, when judging between people and seeking justice in his ruling, sense through the faculty of truth within him that the witnesses are giving false testimony. But what can he do, when they all agree in their statements, however much he questions them, turns the circumstances over to them, and tries to expose their falsehood and deceit, and they all speak with one tongue? This is because a lawyer, for example, had taught them the answer. So what does he do? He becomes angry and stirred for the truth by which he judges, and says a word that shakes all the witnesses and makes them speak the truth. He says to them: "By Allah, if you blind yourselves to the judgment of the earth, you will not blind yourselves to the judgment of heaven." It is a word that Allah caused him to utter, and it restored their right judgment to them and shook them from their depths, so they returned to the truth.

And His saying: ﴿And what the breasts conceal﴾ [Ghafir: 19] means: He, glorified is He, knows the hidden things of the breasts and their inmost secrets, and no one knows these except Allah.

Meaning of ﴿He judges (yaqdi)﴾ [Ghafir: 20]: that is, He rules with truth. ﴿And those whom they invoke besides Him﴾ [Ghafir: 20]: that is, the idols and others that they worshipped besides Allah. ﴿Do not judge anything﴾ [Ghafir: 20]: they do not rule over anything. They have no standing in judgment whatsoever, not even in injustice; they have no capacity to judge. ﴿Indeed, Allah is the All-Hearing, the All-Seeing﴾ [Ghafir: 20]. He hears every utterance that departs from His way, knows every deed that departs from His way, and witnesses everything.

So the Truth, glory be to Him, is the Witness, the Judge, the Ruler and the Executor. If authorities are many in your worldly life, then authority in the Hereafter belongs to Allah alone, with no partner.

After that He, glory be to Him, says: What is the matter with these disbelievers who oppose the call and confront the Messenger whom Allah sent to them as a mercy? Have they not looked into the history of their predecessors among the nations that denied, and what befell them of punishment, and the destruction that came upon them, the traces of which they themselves see?

The Truth, glory be to Him, has recorded this upon Himself, saying: ﴿And certainly Our word has preceded for Our servants, the messengers. Indeed, they would be the ones given victory﴾ [As-Saffat: 171-172].

We know that a person memorises the promise that is in his favour and does not memorise the one that is against him, but as for the Truth, glory be to Him, He preserved and recorded this promise as binding upon Himself: ﴿Indeed, We sent down the Reminder, and indeed, We will be its guardian﴾ [Al-Hijr: 9]. So the Truth, glory be to Him, guaranteed His messengers victory and support, and He, glory be to Him and exalted, would not utter a word and then have the reality of life contradict it. Therefore, the victory of the messengers is one of Allah's laws (sunan) in His creation. He, glory be to Him, says:

﴿Have they not travelled through the earth and observed how was the end of those before them?...﴾.

...the Exalted One wills from our travel through the earth two things: travel through the earth for contemplation and taking admonition, and travel for benefit and investment. So, travelling and journeying through the earth is a sought-after matter of faith. Therefore, He, the Exalted, said regarding travel for contemplation: ﴿Have they not travelled through the earth and seen how was the end of those before them?﴾ And He said regarding travel for investment: ﴿Say: Travel through the earth and observe how He began creation...﴾ [al-'Ankabut: 20].

And He said: ﴿Indeed, those whom the angels take in death while they are wronging themselves, [the angels] will say: "In what condition were you?" They will say: "We were oppressed in the land." [The angels] will say: "Was not the earth of Allah spacious enough for you to emigrate therein?"...﴾ [al-Nisa': 97].

So there is no obstacle to combining, in your journeying through the earth of Allah, travel for contemplation with travel for investment and benefit. Do not deprive yourself of the reflection of contemplation upon the new creation of Allah before you, and do not let trade and investment distract you from contemplation.

Here there is a notable point in His words: ﴿fi al-ardh﴾ ("in the earth"). We have taken this observation only recently from modern science. The scholars used to interpret ﴿fi al-ardh﴾ as "upon the earth," meaning the land and soil on which we walk, until we came to know recently that the earth includes its atmospheric envelope. This air above the earth is the essential and necessary element for the continuation of life upon it; without it there would be no life on the earth, for a human being cannot dispense with it for the length of an inhalation or exhalation. Accordingly, we walk "in the earth" just as the text of the Qur'an, which preceded modern science to this truth, has stated.

When you travel through the earth of Allah for contemplation of Allah's creatures, you see various colours you had not seen before, of people, places, plants, and countless blessings, and you know that the Creator, the Exalted, gives each place what suits it, and to each environment what is fit for it of sustenance...

Commentary of al-Sha'rawi (Tafsir al-Sha'rawi, surahs 1-53, fragments of 54-66) on surah 40, verse 22:

﴿with the clear signs..﴾ [Ghafir: 22] with the manifest signs and the dazzling miracles that testify to the truthfulness of the Messenger, and the signs which they were unable to match, even though eloquence was the very thing in which they excelled. These signs were sufficient for them to believe in Allah and in the Messenger of Allah sent to them, who came to guide them, but they disbelieved. ﴿So Allah seized them..﴾ [Ghafir: 22] The word (akhadhahum, "seized them") denotes taking hold with force. ﴿Indeed, He is Mighty, Severe in punishment﴾ [Ghafir: 22].

There is no doubt that seizing is proportionate to the strength of the one who seizes. The seizing of a child is not the seizing of a youth, and the seizing of a youth is not the seizing of a grown man. How much more so when the One who seizes is Allah, the Mighty, Severe in punishment. When Allah, glory be to Him, is the One who seizes, the one seized has no strength to resist through obstinacy or refusal.

For this reason He said elsewhere: ﴿the seizing of One Mighty, Omnipotent﴾ [al-Qamar: 42]. This is the supreme power: the Mighty (al-'Aziz) is the One who overcomes and is not overcome, and the Omnipotent (al-Muqtadir) is the One capable of everything, whom nothing can incapacitate.

Then the Truth, glory be to Him, relates some of the stories of the messengers who were denied and harmed. Here He recounts to us a portion of the story of our master Musa, peace be upon him:

﴿And We certainly sent Musa with Our signs...﴾.

The Exalted Lord here mentions the story of our master Musa, peace be upon him, because it is distinguished from the stories of the messengers before him. In that they came to cure people of certain doctrinal ailments, to bring them out of the ignorance of "do this and do not do that," and to return them to the right path. As for our master Musa, he came to confront a man who claimed divinity, grew arrogant and became tyrannical, so his mission was more difficult. For this reason he is the messenger with the most stories in the noble Qur'an.

The Most High mentions here the story of Prophet Musa (peace be upon him), because it is distinguished from the stories of the earlier messengers. They came to cure people of certain doctrinal ailments, to bring them out of the ignorance of "do this and don't do that," and to restore them to the right path. Musa, however, came to confront a man who claimed divinity, grew arrogant and became tyrannical, so his mission was harder. For this reason, his is the most frequently narrated story in the Noble Qur'an.

As for the words of the Exalted: ﴿with Our signs﴾ [Ghafir: 23], this refers to the nine clear signs given to Musa (peace be upon him), as confirmation of him and proof of the truth of his message. The first of them was the staff. The staff has a history and a set of events in the story of Musa. With it he struck the sea, and every separated part became like a huge mountain. With it the sea was split and the water was made to stand firm. With the same staff he struck the stone, and twelve springs gushed forth from it. So the matter is not about the water and the mountain; rather, it is the miracle of the One who created the water and created the mountain, who says to a thing, "Be," and it is.

For this reason, the orientalists stopped at the story of Musa. They saw that it takes the largest share among the procession of the messages, and that the Qur'an details it in a way they considered repetitive, especially regarding the staff, which is mentioned in three situations. In reality these are not repetitions; they are different snapshots of one gathered event. The first time God gave Musa the staff as a miracle, He asked him about it: ﴿And what is that in your right hand, O Musa? He said, "It is my staff; I lean upon it, and I beat down leaves with it for my sheep, and I have other uses for it."﴾ [Ta-Ha: 17-18].

We have said that Musa did not answer according to the measure of the question, because the one being asked is his Lord. He wished to prolong his conversation with his Lord, Mighty and Majestic. So he did not say "a staff" or "my staff," and when he sensed that he had gone on at length, he concluded and said: ﴿and I have other uses for it﴾ [Ta-Ha: 18].

The second situation in which the staff is mentioned is when the Most High wanted to train Musa in using it and to test it himself, so that he would be prepared and practiced when he faced Pharaoh, the claimant to divinity. He said to him: ﴿He said, "Throw it down, O Musa." So he threw it, and behold, it was a snake, moving swiftly. He said, "Take hold of it and fear not; We will return it to its former state."﴾ [Ta-Ha: 19-21].

This is the purpose of carrying out this trial before Musa: that he should be afraid of it and see it as it truly is, alive. Had it remained a staff in its condition, Musa would not have been afraid of it, and his Lord would not have said to him: ﴿and fear not﴾ [Ta-Ha: 21].

Then came the final situation of the staff, when Musa met the sorcerers of Pharaoh in Pharaoh's presence, and confronted their sorcery with his staff, which he threw so that it swallowed up what they had made. About this situation the Exalted said: ﴿They said, "O Musa, either you throw, or we will be the first to throw." He said, "Rather, you throw." And behold, their ropes and their staffs appeared to him, by their sorcery, to be moving. So Musa felt a fear within himself. We said, "Fear not; indeed, you are the superior."﴾ [Ta-Ha: 65-68].

So there is no repetition in the mention of Musa's staff; rather, these are different situations and several states of one and the same thing.

As for His words ﴿and a clear authority﴾ [Ghafir: 23]: "sultan" means clear proof, and it also means power. It is either the power of argument and proof, or the power of domination and overpowering force, as occurs in the dialogue of Satan on the Day of Resurrection: ﴿And Satan will say when the matter has been decided, "Indeed, Allah promised you a true promise, and I promised you, but I failed you. I had no authority over you except that I called you, and you responded to me..."﴾ [Ibrahim: 22].

That is, I had no authority of proof that could convince you, nor any authority of force and power that could terrify you and compel you into disobedience. Rather, you were at a mere (tashwira), a simple signal: as soon as I called you, you responded. ﴿So do not blame me, but blame yourselves. I cannot help you, nor can you help me...﴾ [Ibrahim: 22]. We say: "So-and-so cried out, and I answered his cry," meaning: I removed the causes of his crying out.

As for His words: ﴿to Pharaoh, Haman, and Qarun...﴾ [Ghafir: 24]: Pharaoh was indeed the head of the trial and the claimant to divinity, but Haman is mentioned with him because he was his minister and assistant, and Qarun because he was in charge of his treasury. So the three were partners, and therefore they also shared in accusing Musa: ﴿they said, "A sorcerer, a liar."﴾ [Ghafir: 24].

﴿So when he brought them the truth from Us...﴾ [Ghafir: 25], meaning: the signs. ﴿they said, "Kill the sons of those who believe with him..."﴾ [Ghafir: 25]. The matter of killing the sons came from Pharaoh twice. The first was in the days when Musa was a child. Pharaoh learned from the astrologers that his rule would end at the hands of one of the sons of the Children of Israel, so he began killing the young boys, out of fear of this child who would be born and at whose hands his kingdom would fall.

What is remarkable here is the stupidity and heedlessness of Pharaoh in killing the sons of the Children of Israel, and his eagerness that not one of them should escape, to the point that his men would enter the houses searching them for young children.

This situation revealed his stupidity in two respects. First: he kills the young sons, although the prophecy says that the end of his rule would come at the hands of one of them. Then a boy comes to him in this suspicious manner: a chest in the sea, with a young boy inside, arriving at the door of his house. He feels reassured by him, takes him, raises him under his own eye, and remains heedless of what is intended for him.

This situation is clarified by His words: ﴿And know that Allah comes between a person and his heart...﴾ [Al-Anfal: 24]. Indeed, the hearts are between two fingers of the All-Merciful; He turns them however He wills.

As for His words ﴿and spare their women...﴾ [Ghafir: 25], meaning: kill the male sons, because they are the source of fear, from them comes rebellion, and from them will come the one at whose hands Pharaoh's kingdom will fall. As for the women, leave them alive for service and for humiliation.

This explains to us why the Arabs, when they went out to war, took their women with them, so that they would share one fate with them: if they were victorious, they would return safe, and if they were killed, they would all be killed together, so that no women would remain after them to be taken captive, enslaved, and humiliated.

﴿And the scheming of the disbelievers is nothing but in error﴾ [Ghafir: 25]. Indeed, this was a scheme from Pharaoh and his helpers. But did his scheme succeed against the Children of Israel? No; rather, Allah turned his scheme back upon him, and he returned with error and loss.
