The word ﴿fasbir﴾ [Ghafir: 55] (so be patient) is evidence that the Prophet (ﷺ) was addressed with it in times of severe hardship. Concerning these times, God says: ﴿And they were shaken until the Messenger and those who believed with him said, "When is the help of God?" Unquestionably, the help of God is near.﴾ [al-Baqarah: 214]

And His saying: ﴿Indeed, the promise of God is true﴾ [Ghafir: 55]. The wa'd (promise) is the announcement of good before its time, and the promise of God is true, meaning it is certain to be fulfilled. A promise is when you pledge to a person and give him good tidings of benefit, bliss and happiness. Can you then guarantee that you will keep your promise? No, for you may die before its time comes, or your power to act may weaken so that you are unable. But when the promise comes from the Self-Subsisting, the All-Powerful, who cannot be opposed, and He, glory be to Him, is everlasting and does not cease, then it is a promise that is true and must be fulfilled.

Therefore, the Truth, glory be to Him, teaches us not to be certain of a promise, nor to state it definitively, because you are among the contingent beings (al-aghyar). He, exalted, says: ﴿And never say of anything, "Indeed, I will do that tomorrow," * Except [when adding], "If God wills."﴾ [al-Kahf: 23-24]

So making fulfillment conditional on God's will relieves you of the accusation of lying if you do not act. If you say, "I will do such and such tomorrow," do you possess the means of fulfilling it? Do you possess time, or guarantee the effective power? Certainly not; you cannot guarantee the continuation of any of these means. So say, "If God wills," and clear yourself of lying if you do not do it.

And His saying: ﴿And seek forgiveness for your sin﴾ [Ghafir: 55] means: ask for forgiveness. Does the word ﴿for your sin﴾ [Ghafir: 55] mean that the Messenger committed a sin? They said: The Messenger of God (ﷺ) is a human being to whom revelation is sent, and he has an opinion in his humanity in matters on which no ruling from God has come. Even if his opinion was correct, the judgment of the Truth, glory be to Him, is more correct.

Therefore his Lord corrects him: ﴿And seek forgiveness for your sin﴾ [Ghafir: 55]. So for what does the Messenger of God seek forgiveness? He seeks forgiveness of God for being slow to seek victory, in His saying, exalted: ﴿until the Messenger and those who believed with him said, "When is the help of God?"﴾ [al-Baqarah: 214]. Yet the victory is coming, so why would he be slow to seek it?

Therefore, verses have come in the Qur'an establishing that the Messenger (ﷺ) did something for which he was rebuked, and the Truth, glory be to Him, corrected him and set right his action. But how did this rebuke come? Consider His saying, exalted: ﴿May God pardon you. Why did you grant them permission?﴾ [al-Tawbah: 43]. Before rebuking him, He first pardoned him.

But why did the Messenger grant permission to these people? They said: What occupied the Messenger of God in this matter is that he said to himself: whoever asks my permission not to fight is either truthful in his excuse, so there is no harm in granting him permission, or he is lying in his excuse, and there is no good in him; his absence is better than his presence among the ranks, as God, exalted, says: ﴿Had they gone out with you, they would not have increased you except in confusion, and they would have hurried between your ranks, seeking [to cause] you fitnah﴾ [al-Tawbah: 47].

Then, this rebuke to the Messenger of God (ﷺ), ﴿Why did you grant them permission?﴾ [al-Tawbah: 43], we would not have known it except from the Messenger of God himself. Had he not informed us of it, we would not have known it. He (ﷺ) does not disdain that his Lord should rebuke him or correct his choice.

We have clarified this point in the matter of adoption (tabanni, the practice of adopting a child as one's own son) which took place between our master, the Messenger of God (ﷺ), and Zayd ibn Harithah. When the Truth, glory be to Him, wished to abolish the custom of adoption, He made His Prophet Muhammad (ﷺ) and Zayd ibn Harithah an example of this new ruling.

Zayd had been a slave of Khadijah, and she gave him to the Messenger of God. When his family learned of his presence in Makkah with the Messenger of God, they came and asked the Messenger of God for him. The Messenger of God gave him the choice between staying with him or going with his family. Zayd chose to remain with the Messenger of God. The Messenger (ﷺ) wished to honour Zayd for his stance and his love of remaining in his company, so he adopted him and attributed him to himself. From that day Zayd was known as Zayd ibn Muhammad.

But the Truth, glory be to Him, willed to nullify this custom and forbid adoption, so He sent down: ﴿Call them by [the names of] their fathers; it is more just in the sight of God. But if you do not know their fathers, then they are your brothers in religion and your clients﴾ [al-Ahzab: 5].

The meaning of ﴿more just in the sight of God﴾ [al-Ahzab: 5] is that what the Messenger of God did was just and equitable, but the ruling of God is more just and more equitable. Would this correction anger the Messenger of God? Certainly not, as evidence by the fact that he (ﷺ) himself informed us of it; had the Messenger of God concealed it, we would not have known it.

Likewise, in His saying about the captives of Badr: ﴿It is not for a prophet to have captives until he has inflicted a massacre upon the land﴾ [al-Anfal: 67]. When they disagreed about taking ransom from the captives, God rebuked His Messenger with this verse. But did the ruling change after that? No, it remained as it was, and He said: ﴿Were it not for a decree from God that preceded, you would have been touched for what you took by a great punishment﴾ [al-Anfal: 68].

It is as if it were permissible for the Messenger of God (ﷺ) to deny this matter, especially since the ruling remained as it was. Therefore: we did not know of God's rebuke of His Messenger except from the Messenger himself. The one who reflects on the Truth's rebuke of His Messenger finds that it is either a rebuke for his own benefit (ﷺ), or a rebuke because the side of correctness was the one the Truth, glory be to Him, ruled on, as in the matter we have mentioned.

As for the rebuke for his own benefit (ﷺ), it is like His saying, exalted: ﴿O Prophet, why do you prohibit what God has made lawful for you, seeking the approval of your wives?﴾ [al-Tahrim: 1]. This is like when you rebuke your son for staying up too late studying and exhausting himself. Likewise, the Truth, glory be to Him, rebukes His Messenger for constricting himself and making things hard on himself, seeking the approval of his wives.

Likewise He rebuked him in the matter of the blind man, saying: ﴿He frowned and turned away, * Because there came to him the blind man. * And what would make you know? Perhaps he would purify himself, * Or be reminded, and the reminder would benefit him. * As for one who thinks himself self-sufficient, * You give him attention, * And you are not responsible if he does not purify himself. * But as for he who came to you running, * While fearing [God], * From him you are distracted﴾ [Abasa: 1-10].

The rebuke here is because he (ﷺ) was hard on himself when he left this blind man and turned away from him, though he was a believer, and went to the chiefs of disbelief to call them, seeing that they were more deserving of the call than him.

Some scholars took from His saying ﴿And seek forgiveness for your sin﴾ [Ghafir: 55] evidence that the prophets are not infallible (ma'sum). Others said: the good deeds of the righteous are the misdeeds of those brought near [to God]. It has been narrated that he (ﷺ) said in his supplication: ...

Another party had a different observation on the verse. He said: ﴿And seek forgiveness for your sin﴾ [Ghafir: 55] does not indicate that the sin had actually occurred from him. The meaning is: if you commit a sin, then seek forgiveness, in the future. Like His saying, exalted: ﴿O Prophet, fear God﴾ [al-Ahzab: 1]. Does this mean that he (ﷺ) did not fear God? No, it is an initial command to piety.

It does not mean that he (ﷺ) opposed his method, so God commanded him to be pious, just as we now see someone opposing the method of God and we say to him: "O so-and-so, fear God," meaning: keep to His method, abandon opposition, and place between you and God a shield.

Therefore he said: The command in ﴿And seek forgiveness for your sin﴾ [Ghafir: 55] is a command of worship (ta'abbudi), as in His glorified saying: ﴿Our Lord, grant us what You promised us through Your messengers﴾ [Ali 'Imran: 194]. The command here is a command of worship, because we say "grant us," and He, glory be to Him, has promised this to His messengers, so it is a command that is fulfilled and realized.

Then we say to those who claim that the messengers committed sins: Did God remove them from prophethood because they committed the sin? Or did He leave them as messengers? Rather, He left them and kept their messages. So what is your view if what the Messenger did does not contradict his messengership, and he is well-pleasing to the one who disagreed with him and sinned against him?

And His saying: ﴿And exalt your Lord with praise in the evening and the morning﴾ [Ghafir: 55]. Al-'ashiy (the evening) is the time from after the midday prayer until the end of the day, and al-ibkar (the morning) is from dawn until forenoon. So the meaning is: be constantly glorifying your Lord with praise.

And if the command here is to the Messenger (ﷺ) and to those believers with him who shared with him in the evening and the morning, then from another perspective it is a command to all people, in every time and every place, because his message (ﷺ) is universal.

Thus: the evening and the morning here are pervasive in all time and all place, for each has an evening and a morning suited to its time and place. This means that the glorification of God should remain pervasive in time and place, continuous and never ceasing. This is if we look at the differences in times from one place to another.

Therefore we have said: linking the obligations and acts of worship to the lunar cycle is intended to sustain the continuity of worship of God, exalted. If they were tied to the sun, the times would coincide for people. But by the reckoning of the moon, you see that one person is praying the dawn prayer at the same time that another is praying the end of the midday prayer, and the end of the afternoon prayer, and the end of the sunset prayer, and so on. So the Truth, glory be to Him, is worshipped at every time, with every time.

The meaning of ﴿And exalt your Lord with praise﴾ [Ghafir: 55] is: glorification joined with praise, because glorification is declaring God free of imperfection. Since the Truth is exalted above all deficiencies, the fruit of this declaration returns to you. You are the one who benefits from your Lord, whom you have believed in, being One and exalted above all deficiencies.

Jidal (disputation) means contention, argument and rebuttal. It is derived from jadl al-habl wa fatlih (the twisting of a rope), and twisting is a process in which threads grip one another and intertwine after having been loose and scattered. Thus jadal carries the sense of strengthening, the strengthening of one opinion by another.

Disputation is of two kinds: constructive disputation, which aims to reach the truth, and contentious disputation (mira'), which has no benefit. The disputation of truth is "with authority" (bi-sultan), meaning with proof and evidence, while the contentious disputation is in falsehood, meaning without authority or proof. Authority is of two kinds: the authority of compulsion, which carries you, forces you and overpowers you into doing something, and the authority of proof and persuasion. The authority of compulsion makes you act while you are unwilling and coerced, while the authority of proof and persuasion makes you act while you are content and convinced...

As for the meaning of "in the signs of Allah" (fi ayat Allah), we have said that they are of three categories:

The first are cosmic signs (ayat kawniyyah) that establish the Supreme Existence, His power and the wondrous perfection of His making. Among these cosmic signs are the sun, the moon, the stars, the earth, the air and the water, etc.

The second are the miracles (mu'jizat) which Allah gives to the messengers to establish the truthfulness of the Messenger in conveying from Allah.

The third are the verses of the Noble Qur'an which carry the rulings (ahkam) of Allah to people and carry the method of Allah: do and do not.

So in which of these categories do they dispute? They say: they dispute concerning the miracles and the verses of rulings. As for the cosmic signs, they are not a field of disputation.

As for His saying: "without any authority having come to them" — does this mean that there is disputation in the signs of Allah with authority? They say: rather the meaning is that it is impossible, i.e., there is no disputation in the signs of Allah. The matter is: "There is naught in their breasts but greatness (kibr)." This is the cause, and the source of disputation concerning the signs of Allah is a greatness in their breasts that prevents them from accepting the truth, and prevents them from submitting to a man from among them, whom they may have thought themselves superior to.

Therefore, in some verses Allah, glorified is He, makes clear that they believe in the Qur'an, but their objection is to the Messenger of Allah as a person who came with the message, being one of the common people, neither the greatest of them nor the wealthiest. He, exalted is He, says, relating on the tongue of the disbelievers: "And they said, 'Why was this Qur'an not revealed to a man of importance from the two cities?'" [Az-Zukhruf: 31].

In another place they deny everything and say: "O Allah, if this is the truth from You, then rain down on us stones from the sky or bring us a painful punishment" [Al-Anfal: 32]. The logical thing would have been for them to say: "Guide us to it."

This statement of theirs is evidence that they are averse to the religion entirely, because their hearts are occupied with a contrary matter, namely their polytheism and their worship of idols, this worship in which they were raised and which they inherited. When a person is preoccupied with falsehood, he cannot be guided to the truth unless the false matter is first removed from his heart; then the truth is permitted to enter.

Therefore Allah, glorified is He, makes clear to us that matters of belief are not to be discussed in the crowd of people; rather you contemplate them between yourself and yourself. And if participation is necessary, let it be with one person only. Why? Because when you sit alone or with one person, the discussion bears fruit and the circle of disagreement does not widen, so it is more conducive to reaching what is correct. And if one of you two is defeated, he will not be defeated before the crowd, and then he will not be obstinate or stubborn, and he will return to the truth and come back to it without embarrassment.

Therefore He, glorified is He, says: "I admonish you with one thing: that you stand up for Allah in pairs and singly, then reflect: there is no madness in your companion" [Saba': 46], meaning: do not investigate matters of belief in the mass manner, for the masses have no restraint, and their collective thinking leads to confusion and mob mentality. So be alone, lest desire enter you and you incline with it.

As for the greatness in His saying, "There is naught in their breasts but greatness" — "in" here means "what is in their breasts is nothing but greatness." That is: haughtiness toward the truth that the Messenger brings. This greatness or arrogance is what prevented them from listening to the Messenger and made them look down on him, because they were lords in their society, and listening to the Messenger of Allah and obeying him would make them subordinate to those whom they listen to and obey.

It is well known that Quraysh had supremacy over all the Arabs. This supremacy enabled them to be secure in their trading journeys in winter and summer, moving freely without anyone molesting them. Why?

Because all the tribes of the Arabs came to Quraysh in Makkah during the season of Hajj, and they were under Quraysh's hospitality and protection and within its sphere. The Sacred House and its pilgrimage are what gave Quraysh this status and this awe. Therefore He, glorified is He, says: "For the security of Quraysh, their security during the caravan of winter and summer. So let them worship the Lord of this House, who has fed them against hunger and made them safe from fear" [Quraysh: 1-4].

And He, glorified is He, says: "Have they not seen that We made a sanctuary secure while people are being snatched away from around them?" [Al-'Ankabut: 67].

The proof of this is that when they saw in the idols gods that have no commands and no obligations, they were content with them and worshipped them besides Allah. Yet when they wanted a place in which to honour these gods, they found nothing but the Ka'bah, and they placed their idols around it. So the Ka'bah has a sanctity in their eyes despite their disbelief in Allah.

This is the greatness that prevented them from accepting the truth, and Allah described this greatness by His saying: "They will not attain it" [Ghafir: 56], meaning: they do not have the grounds for greatness. It is a false greatness, because one who is proud should be proud of something intrinsic to himself, not of something accidental that may be taken from him. It is a false greatness, like one who is proud of his strength, his health, his wealth or his authority.

As for His saying, exalted is He: "So seek refuge in Allah," because seeking refuge in Allah means that something has come beyond your material means, so do not stand before it with folded hands. Rather turn to your Lord who sent you and say to Him: "This matter has overwhelmed me and exceeded my capacity, so bear it for me." Therefore He, glorified is He, said: "Who answers the distressed one when he calls upon Him?" [An-Naml: 62].

So when means are scarce, turn to the Causer (al-musabbib). "Indeed, He is the All-Hearing, the All-Seeing." These two are among the attributes of absolute perfection of Allah, the Exalted: hearing and seeing. For every movement of a person's limbs is an action: the tongue has an action, the hand has an action, and the foot has an action.

This action is divided into two parts: either speech or deed. Speech alone takes up half of the action, which is the action of the tongue, and the actions of the other limbs are called (fi'l, deed).

Therefore the Exalted said: "O you who believe, why do you say what you do not do?" [As-Saff: 2], mentioning speech and deed, and all of it is called action. So hearing is for what is said, and seeing is for what is done. The Exalted explains to His Messenger, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, the status of seeking refuge: "So seek refuge in Allah," because He is All-Hearing of everything that is said and All-Seeing of everything that is done.

The lam in (لَخَلْقُ) indicates an oath, as if the Truthful, Glorified One is saying: "By My might and My majesty, the creation of the heavens and the earth is greater than the creation of mankind." How so? They said: because people in this world have varying lifespans: one person's life is a moment, another's is an hour, and another's is a hundred years, up to the lifespan of Nuh (peace be upon him). So where is my lifespan compared with the lifespan of the sun, even though it was created to serve me? Could the servant be longer-lived than the one served?

Therefore: there must be another lifespan for you that remains after the sun and the other creatures that serve you have passed away, and this can only be in the Hereafter. They said: a lifespan has a length that none knows but Allah, and it has a breadth that may exceed its length. Likewise He made for it a volume and a depth. So Allah, who has set the lifespan as a span of time, it is possible that a person takes his lifespan in length, but he can increase its breadth, so that breadth becomes the longer dimension, meaning that he widens the circle of his activity so that he benefits himself and benefits his community, and he leaves a good remembrance after his death. Thus, by his activity, he has added lifespans to his lifespan.

Accordingly, we say: people's homelands are determined according to the measure of their aspirations. One whose homeland is himself wants everything for himself while belonging to no one; this is the selfish person. One whose homeland is his family, another whose homeland is his tribe, another whose homeland is his town, and one whose homeland is the whole world. Whenever aspiration increases, the circle of the homeland widens and its expanse grows.

When we say that the sun has a longer lifespan than I do, we note that you, O human, are a living being who eats and drinks, whereas the sun is inanimate, neither eating nor drinking. You have a law of maintenance, and sickness and other things afflict you, because you are a son of accidents. As for the sun, it has none of this; it has no law of maintenance, and what afflicts you does not afflict it. Since Allah created it, it has been working without stopping, without malfunction, and without maintenance. A machine with this description points to the power of its Creator and the greatness of its Originator.

Therefore we say: if we look at the creation of the heavens and the earth, we find it is indeed greater than the creation of mankind. ﴿But most people do not know﴾. But what is the meaning of (لاَ يَعْلَمُونَ)? The universe falls under our senses, and we see it with our eyes. When we see this universe with its creative wonder, we should have reflected on it, on the greatness of its creation, the precision of its order, and how perfectly regulated and unfailing it is.

Are we not now, through knowledge, able to determine the time of an eclipse, for example, to the minute and the second? It is as if the Truthful, Glorified One has enlisted even non-Muslims to demonstrate the truth of His cosmic signs and how they are regulated with a precision that no one can corrupt. Therefore we have said: if you see a disorder or corruption in the universe, know that the hand of chosen man has intervened in it, whereas what we leave in its natural state cannot be seen to have any disorder or corruption.

Yes, those who neglect the signs of God and do not reflect upon them are not equal to those who contemplate them, draw lessons from them, and are guided by them. The one who does not reflect upon these signs is like the blind man, for he is not alert to the signs in the cosmos, which are greater than the creation of people. And if these cosmic signs are greater in creation and more magnificent than the creation of people, how can you neglect them? From them you can take the proof of the existence of the Necessary Existent, the Most High, glory be to Him, and of the absoluteness of His power and the perfection of His craftsmanship.

Just as the blind man and the seeing man are not equal, so too are those who believe and do righteous deeds not equal in the sight of God to the evildoer. This is one of the manifestations of His justice, glory be to Him: ﴿Little do you remember﴾. That is, few among you remember this.

Almighty God reminds us of this truth, which is often absent from minds, and you should not have been heedless of it, because the matter is not merely knowledge of something; rather, the matter goes further than that. It is a precaution for what will happen and for what will come to you.

﴿Indeed, the Hour is surely coming﴾ [Ghafir: 59], i.e., the Resurrection, ﴿there is no doubt in it﴾ [Ghafir: 59], no uncertainty. Since the Hour is coming and there is no doubt about it, we must prepare for it. For if you had been created and left like this, cut off from God, you would have been free to do as you wished. But what of it, when you have a return to your Lord and a going back to your Creator, and a standing for reckoning and recompense? So there is no escape for you from protecting your Hereafter, which is the supreme goal beyond which there is no other.

As for His saying: ﴿But most of the people do not believe﴾ [Ghafir: 59], i.e., they do not know these realities or they are heedless of them, even though pure reason must guide one to believe in the existence of the Hour, reckoning and recompense. Why? Because when you look at the universe, you find that whoever is bound by a method of "do" and "do not do," and proceeds according to this method, you find him well-mannered toward the universe around him, no corruption or transgression coming from him. And you find the one who is loose, who has slipped out of this method, a source of disturbance and corruption to the universe around him. Are the two equal in reason, in mere reason?

Are the reformer and the corrupter equal? Him who ran riot in the universe, harmed God's creatures and wearied the whole world, and him who reformed the universe, made people happy and helped them? Then, in the process of education, do we not give students end-of-year examinations and say: this one has passed, and this one has failed? Do we not set in our worldly life rules of reward and punishment that require rewarding the good-doer and punishing the wrongdoer?

So why do you deny the reckoning on the Day of Resurrection, the Day when each is recompensed for what they did? Even people who do not believe in the Hereafter believe in the principle of reward and punishment; they have penalties for crimes against society to discipline those who step outside the law. If in your worldly life you made penalties, criminalized certain acts and punished for them so that the movement of your worldly life would be upright, then why do you deny this principle with God in the Hereafter?

Is it conceivable that the movement of all people in this world, from its beginning to its end, is left like this without reckoning, without reward for the good-doer and punishment for the wrongdoer?

By God, if the matter were as they claim and deny, then the deviant criminals would have triumphed, and the violators who step outside the law and religion would have profited, since they did what they did, wronged whom they wronged, and escaped with their crimes. And in this bargain only the believers and the upright, who bound themselves to a method for no benefit, would have lost.

And His Exalted saying: ﴿But most of the people do not believe﴾ [Ghafir: 59].

He means: the matter is not founded upon reason but upon faith. Had it been left to reason alone, we would have said what we have just said. But the matter of the Hour rests upon faith and creed. Whoever wants not to be bound by faith and to slip out of its restraints wants not to restrict his movement in existence by a method of "do" and "do not do"; he wants to be free, moving through life according to his desire.

Therefore we said: those who worshipped trees and stones worshipped them because they are gods with no method and no obligations, and this worship is false in its meaning, because worship means the worshipper's obedience to the command of the one worshipped. So these gods you claim: what have they commanded you? And from what have they forbidden you? What have they prepared for whoever worships them? And what have they prepared for whoever disbelieves in them?

So you have only accepted these gods in order to move through life without restraints, without obligations, without a method, and without a controlling check upon your desires.

Commentary of al-Sha'rawi (Tafsir al-Sha'rawi, surahs 1–53, fragments of 54–66) on surah 40, verse 60:

The meaning of "Rabbukum" (your Lord) is the One who has taken charge of your nurture (tarbiyah). Tarbiyah here means bringing into existence from nothing and providing sustenance from non-existence. Since He is my Lord, I am under His responsibility: He guarantees my provision and my livelihood in this world. And before that, He gave me the limbs that work and the organs by which I live. He is my Lord and my Creator, who summoned me into the universe and provided for me in it the means of life.

Therefore, when He, glory be to Him, wished to make a model in the universe, He made it such that the universe sympathizes with its own self and completes itself. So He made this one strong and that one weak, this one healthy and that one sick.

The strong one's movement in life is complete and powerful, exceeding his need, and He says to him: "What exceeds your need, make it for the weak one who cannot move." The Creator, glory be to Him, is able to make all people strong, but He willed that creation be linked in the movement of life by the link of need, not the link of favour (tafaddul). For linkage does not come through the law of favour, since favour has no obligation in it, and one who bestows a thing is free: he may act or not act.

As for His saying: "Call upon Me, I will answer you" (ud'ūnī astajib lakum), it means: in matters where you are unable to attain their causes and cannot achieve them, and you find no help from your surroundings, there is nothing for you but to turn to Me and call upon Me, and I will respond: "Or who answers the distressed one when he calls upon Him and removes the evil?" (An-Naml: 62). I am your Lord and your Creator; I summoned you into existence, granted you the means and the limbs, and made you vicegerents on earth. So you have no refuge other than Me to resort to if the causes become difficult for you.

But if the causes are made available to you, and every responsible person performs his role, then do not abandon the causes and say: "O Lord!" Rather, first take up the causes that are in your hands; strive in them, and if they are too narrow for you, then go to the Causer (al-musabbib).

Yet we notice in this matter that God, exalted is He, has commanded us to supplicate and promised us an answer, and yet among us is one who calls upon Him and is not answered. Why? They said: because you call while you are not in a state of necessity (idtirar); had you been in a state of necessity, you would have been answered. You live in a respectable dwelling and ask God to give you a villa or a palace; if He gives you the palace, you say: "I want a building to pay for the palace's upkeep." This is a supplication out of luxury, not out of necessity, and the answer here is conditioned upon the one in necessity.

And the Truth, glory be to Him, does not exempt a servant from the responsibility of extending benefit to the servants. They said: because the one who has means spends, and the one who lacks means advises the one who has. If you advise without result, your obligation is still not discharged even after that.

If you read the Qur'an you will find His saying: "There is no blame upon the weak, nor upon the sick, nor upon those who find nothing to spend, when they are sincere to God and His Messenger. There is no cause for blame against the good-doers. And God is Forgiving and Merciful" (At-Tawbah: 91).

When is this? They said: when you have no wealth, you must advise: "when they are sincere to God and His Messenger, there is no way against the good-doers" (At-Tawbah: 91). You advised and it was not answered. They said: "Be dutiful to yourself"; how? 

"Nor upon those who, when they came to you to be provided with mounts, you said, 'I cannot find anything to mount you on'; they turned away, their eyes overflowing with tears of grief that they could not find anything to spend" (At-Tawbah: 92). So has He exempted anyone? No, rather He urged everyone to act: either by spending wealth or by spending speech. If you cannot do this nor that, then you must grieve because you did not take part, and mere emotional pain is not sufficient here; rather it must be accompanied by an emotional reaction that produces weeping: you weep that you found nothing to spend in the way of God.

So: the matter is one of beneficial extension through the universe, and this extension leaves none of us in need.

Then we say to him: are you a poor person who is incapable, or one who is poor by choice (ihtiraf)? If he is poor by choice, he is not counted nor regarded; but if he is poor by incapacity, he may sit in his house honoured and respected, and the wealthy one is the one who goes to him and gives him his due. So the capable one becomes in the service of the one who is not capable.

As for His saying: "Indeed, those who are too proud to worship Me will enter Hell, humbled" (Ghafir: 60). The meaning of "they are too proud to worship Me" is: they are too proud to supplicate to Me, to abase themselves before Me, and to show their need of Me. Therefore the people of knowledge said: let not your share of supplication be that you are answered; rather let your share of supplication be the humility of one in need before one who possesses good. Is this the meaning of worship here?

Therefore you will find your Lord, mighty and majestic, always correcting your error in supplication: "And man prays for evil as he prays for good, and man is ever hasty" (Al-Isra': 11).

For you may pray for yourself for an evil you think is good, and by the mercy of God toward you He does not answer you. Therefore we say in praise of God, exalted is He: "Glory be to You, O You who correct the error of the supplicants by not answering them, and by this You protect us from harm; how often does a person pray for evil as he prays for good..."

As for why "they will enter Hell humbled" (dakhirīn), meaning: abased, humiliated, lowly. They said: because you do not call upon anyone unless you are obedient to him, since supplication and worship are equivalent. Therefore the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: "Every matter not begun with the name of God is cut off (abtar)," meaning: it has no blessing.

And we were taught to say: "In the name of God, the Most Merciful, the Most Compassionate" (Bismillah al-Rahman al-Rahim), meaning: I begin my work with the name of God so that the hand of God may be with me in the action. So what is the meaning of "al-Rahman al-Rahim" here?

They said: perhaps you are a disobedient servant, so He mentions to you the attribute of mercy, for He, glory be to Him, does not abandon His servant even if he is disobedient. Those people will enter the Fire humbled, abased, because they disdained to call upon God and were too proud to worship Him; the Fire is the recompense of arrogance.

Commentary of al-Sha'rawi (Tafsir al-Sha'rawi (surahs 1-53, fragments of 54-66)) on surah 40, verse 61:

Allah, glory be to Him, mentions here two of His cosmic signs: the sign of the night and the sign of the day. The night, which we know, is from the setting of the sun until its rising, and the day, which we know, is from the rising of the sun until its setting. This is a period of time, and time is the vessel of events. Since time is the vessel of events, every event has a time in which it occurs.

An event that requires effort has a time for it. When you work during the day, your limbs become tired and need a time of rest. The Creator, glory be to Him, has therefore made the night for you to rest in and the day for you to work in. You rest at night to regain your strength and vigour for work the following day, and so on.

If circumstances arise that prevent you from resting at night, how will you be during the day? You will be exhausted, with no strength left with which to deal with anything. It is as though God, exalted is He, wants to teach us that among His creation are opposites, and it is the folly of humanity to have made them enemies, when in reality they are complementary.

If you wish, read His words, exalted is He: ﴿By the night when it covers, and by the day when it appears, and by Him who created the male and the female, indeed your effort is diverse﴾ [al-Layl: 1-4].

This means that the night has a function, the day has a function, the male has a function, and the female has a function. So do not think there is enmity between the night and the day, or between the male and the female. Each of them completes the other, and between them is mutual support, not opposition, as some imagine.

Therefore He, exalted is He, says in another verse: ﴿Say: Have you considered, if Allah made the night perpetual over you until the Day of Resurrection, what god other than Allah could bring you light? Will you not then listen? Say: Have you considered, if Allah made the day perpetual over you until the Day of Resurrection, what god other than Allah could bring you a night in which you rest? Will you not then see?﴾ [al-Qasas: 71-72].

Consider the closing phrase of the verse in both places. In the case of the night He said ﴿Will you not then listen?﴾ [al-Qasas: 71], because in the night the sense of sight is disabled, while the ear remains hearing, and hearing is the instrument of summoning at night. In the case of the day He said ﴿Will you not then see?﴾ [al-Qasas: 72], because sight belongs to the day.

As for the word sarmad (perpetual): some exegetes hold that the night is not perpetual, nor the day, in the sense that neither is continuous and unbroken. But if we consider the movement of the earth and the succession of night and day, we find in them perpetuity, because when the night leaves us, it goes to others, rather than being everlasting and then ending.

Thus both are perpetual and everlasting. However, the perpetuity that is relevant to us is the perpetuity with respect to a single place, so that they have perpetuity in themselves and perpetuity in every place, while the perpetuity of a single place ends so as to begin in another place.

Therefore He, exalted is He, says: ﴿And it is He who made the night and the day alternating for whoever wishes to remember or wishes to be grateful﴾ [al-Furqan: 62]. Khilfah (alternation): each of them succeeds the other; the night succeeds the day and the day succeeds the night. This is now clear to us as a cosmic sign. But what of the beginning of creation: which of them was first, and the other succeeded it?

They said: at the beginning Allah created them together at one time, because the sun was created facing the earth. So what faced the sun from the earth was day, and what was screened from it on the other side was night. Then the earth turned in its orbit, and the night and day alternated. This is evidence that the earth is spherical; had it been flat, this would not have been possible.

As for the phrase in His words ﴿and the day as something that gives sight﴾ [Ghafir: 61], meaning: giving sight within it. In former times they believed that the ray of vision went out from the eye to the seen object, until the Muslim scholar al-Hasan ibn al-Haytham came and proved the opposite, and showed that the ray comes from the seen object to the eye, so that you see it. The proof is that you do not see what is in darkness, but you see what is in light, even if you yourself are in darkness, because the ray is reflected from the seen object so that you see it.

Accordingly, the day itself is (giving sight): ﴿Indeed, Allah is full of bounty toward mankind﴾ [Ghafir: 61]. Yes, Allah is the possessor of bounty and of favour upon all people, because He, glory be to Him, gave them without any right that they had over Him. He is bountiful in bringing into existence from non-existence, bountiful in sustaining from lack, and bountiful in imposing obligations. Yes, even in imposing obligations He is bountiful. How?

They said: because when He imposes an obligation upon you, He imposes something whose benefit returns to you, and He gains nothing from it at all. Then afterwards He rewards you for it and gives you a recompense. Thus it is as though He, glory be to Him, has shown you favour in the imposition twice.

And His words ﴿But most people do not give thanks﴾ [Ghafir: 61] mean that the few are the grateful, and gratitude is recognised by the increase of blessings. Gratitude and the increase of blessing go together, and Allah, glory be to Him, has promised: ﴿And when your Lord proclaimed: If you give thanks, I will surely increase you﴾ [Ibrahim: 7].

The Almighty's saying, ﴿That is⦅ Allah⦆ your Lord﴾ [Ghafir: 62], is a reference to Him, glorified is He. That is, the One who did for you such-and-such and bestowed His favour upon you is Allah, your Lord. ﴿The Creator of all things﴾ [Ghafir: 62]. This is a matter that no one has denied, and no one has claimed for himself. ﴿There is no god but He﴾ [Ghafir: 62]. Thus the Truth, glorified is He, pronounced for Himself that there is no god but He.

So, you believe in Allah, and Allah, glorified is He, is certain of His own essence, and bore witness to this for Himself. He bore witness for Himself that there is no god but He before anyone bore witness to it. Therefore He, glorified is He, says "Be" (kun), and He knows that it takes effect, because it is His word and has no opponent, and there is no other god who could reject it, alter it, or object to it.

The Almighty says: ﴿Allah bears witness that there is no god but He, and so do the angels and those endowed with knowledge, upholding justice. There is no god but He, the Mighty, the Wise﴾ [Al 'Imran: 18]. They said: Allah bore witness for Himself with the witness of essence to essence; the angels bore witness with the witness of presence (mashhad); and those endowed with knowledge bore witness with the witness of inference (istidlal).

When the Truth, glorified is He, says ﴿The Creator of all things﴾ [Ghafir: 62], He states it in this way as a general proposition in its absolute sense. We say: either it is a true proposition or otherwise—and far be it from Allah—so if it is true, the proof has been established; and if it is not so, then where is the Creator of all things?

Where is the creator of this universe if it was not Allah who created it? Who is he? And why did he remain silent and not declare himself? If he did not know of the existence of Allah, then he is a sleeping, heedless god who is unfit for divinity; and if he knew of the existence of Allah, who made this announcement and did not contradict it, then he is powerless, and a god is never powerless.

Therefore, the One, glorified is He, said, affirming the soundness of this proposition: ﴿Say: Had there been other gods with Him, as they say, they would surely have sought a way to the Lord of the Throne﴾ [al-Isra': 42]. That is: they would have gone to the true God to dispute with Him: how did He take creation from them, and how did He claim it for Himself? But this has not happened.

And His saying: ﴿How then are you turned away?﴾ [Ghafir: 62]. That is: you are diverted from the Truth which reason affirms and which proofs, evidences and reality establish. The truth in this proposition is clear. This proposition has been stated and announced, and no opponent has stood against it, and no one has claimed it for himself. It is well known that a proposition is established for its holder as long as it has no opponent.

We had already clarified this matter and said: Suppose a group of people sat in a place, and when they left, the owner of the place found a wallet. He said to his servant: "Look for the owner of this wallet." The servant began to call them one by one, but none of them said, "It is mine." Then one of them knocked on the door and said: "By God, I forgot my wallet here. To whom, then, does it belong?" It belongs to whoever claims it, until another claimant appears.

His saying: ﴿Thus are turned away those who used to deny the signs of Allah﴾ [Ghafir: 63]. That is: they are diverted from this clear and manifest truth. The meaning of "deny" (yajhadun) the signs: they reject them out of arrogance and haughtiness. They do not deny them or reject them on account of any proof they hold or any logic they rely upon; rather they deny them because they are the signs of Allah, and they do not want Allah, nor do they want the way (manhaj) of Allah.

They fear this way which disciplines their movement in life and restrains their desires. They want to set out in life with the ferocity of power and the oppression of people, and with the ferocity of desires that have no restraint. So denial of the signs is the cause of turning away from the Truth; it is as though it were an unnatural matter for them.

For this reason we see the disbelievers of Quraysh became arrogant in accepting the Truth, opposed the Messenger of God, and never uttered "There is no god but Allah," not even merely uttering it as a word. Why? Because they knew its meaning completely and knew what it requires. Had they known that it was merely a word to be said, they would have said it. But they, being Arabs, the people of this language, know that the meaning of "There is no god but Allah" is: there is no object of worship but Allah, no sovereignty, no authority of opinion, no judgement and no submission except to Allah. Al-mu'tafikah are the towns which Allah overturned upside down. Likewise, falsehood reverses realities: it denies what exists and affirms what does not exist.

Commentary of al-Sha'rawi (Tafsir al-Sha'rawi (surahs 1-53, fragments of 54-66)) on surah 40, verse 64:

His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿Allah is the One Who made for you the earth as a resting place﴾ [Ghafir: 64]. That is, a place of settlement for you, on which you live. The word (lakum) means: for all the servants. This is explained by His saying in Surat al-Rahman: ﴿And the earth He laid out for all creatures﴾ [al-Rahman: 10]. Thus, in general terms: what earth, and what creatures? He did not specify.

So, the earth, all of it, is for the creatures, all of them. But is this principle the reality of our lives? No. Corruption has not befallen the world, nor have people fallen into crises and constriction of livelihood, except because this principle has not been applied.

Now there is earth without people in the world, and in other regions there are people without earth. The cause of this is those barriers that humans have set up, which stand between the servants of God and His earth.

You may read the saying of God Most High: ﴿Indeed, those whom the angels take in death while they are wronging themselves, the angels will say, "In what condition were you?" They will say, "We were oppressed in the earth." The angels will say, "Was not the earth of Allah spacious that you could have emigrated therein?"﴾ [al-Nisa': 97].

But, my Lord, how can we emigrate when they have placed at the gates barriers, walls and borders, and laws for entry, for which God has sent down no authority? So look at the map and consider the borders of the different states: you will find them overlapping and unorganized, and in some regions you find the borders unclear or disputed, and in some countries you find the borders to be foci of dispute and conflict between states.

If this indicates anything, it indicates that the earth is one earth for all. When humans came upon it, they divided it and placed borders upon it. God created it one, open and wide, so that when affairs become constricted for you in one patch of it, go to another and set out in the earth of God. If this divine principle is not applied, our problems will not be solved, and crises will continue to grind the people.

Settlement in the earth is of two kinds: settlement for life and movement, and settlement for rest and calm. Each of us has a house in which he lives and to which he returns; it is his dwelling place, his place of rest and lodging, and for this reason we call it a house (bayt).

And he has a land in which he strives and seeks sustenance and movement; for this reason our master Ibrahim said: ﴿Our Lord, I have settled some of my offspring in an uncultivated valley near Your Sacred House﴾ [Ibrahim: 37], and he said: ﴿My Lord, make this a secure city﴾ [al-Baqarah: 126]. The former is a settlement for lodging and rest, and the latter a settlement for movement and striving.

You notice that the settlement for lodging and rest is specific to you, whereas the settlement for movement is shared with others. And the earth is not a settlement for you in your worldly life alone; rather, it is a settlement for you even after your death: ﴿From it We created you, and into it We will return you﴾ [Ta-Ha: 55].

His saying: ﴿And the sky as a structure﴾ [Ghafir: 64]. That is, a structure firmly built, with no defect in it. A building, as is known, stands on pillars that bear it; for this reason He said: ﴿without pillars that you can see﴾ [al-Ra'd: 2]. Either there are no pillars at all, or there are pillars bearing it but you do not see them; the pillars exist, but your senses do not perceive them.

So the sky is held up by the power of God, glory be to Him. And why not, when the earth on which we live is only a sphere suspended in the air? Why does it not fall despite its weight?

Read: ﴿Indeed, Allah holds the heavens and the earth lest they cease; and if they should cease, no one could hold them after Him﴾ [Fatir: 41]. That is: no one holds them after Allah.

Then the Truth, glory be to Him, gives us a sensory example that brings us close to God's power in bearing up the heavens and the earth. He says: take from the sensory things that you perceive as evidence for what is hidden from you: ﴿Have they not considered the birds above them, spreading their wings and folding them in? None holds them up except the Most Merciful﴾ [al-Mulk: 19].

Yes, we see birds in the air of the sky standing still in the atmosphere without movement, and yet they do not fall. Who holds them? Their Lord, Mighty and Majestic, holds them by His power; likewise He holds the heavens and the earth by His power.

His saying: ﴿and He shaped you and perfected your shapes﴾ [Ghafir: 64]. After He spoke, glory be to Him, of cosmic things external to us, such as night and day, sky and earth, He speaks here of something within ourselves, for He, glory be to Him, said: ﴿We will show them Our signs in the horizons and within themselves until it becomes clear to them that it is the truth﴾ [Fussilat: 53].

His saying: ﴿and He shaped you﴾ [Ghafir: 64]: that is, He gave you a distinctive form by which you are distinguished, then He gave you special marks by which individuals are identified, so that no one commits an act and hides it from another.

Thus the distinguishing of individuals here is important, so that the act may be attributed to its doer. ﴿And perfected your shapes﴾ [Ghafir: 64]: that is, He made them the best form among creatures. He was capable of shaping the human being in any form, such as walking on four legs like the animals, but He honoured him, perfected his form, and made him walk upright, with his stature raised.

He, Exalted, says: ﴿O mankind, what has deceived you concerning your Lord, the Generous? Who created you and proportioned you and balanced you? In whatever form He willed, He assembled you﴾ [al-Infitar: 6-8]. That is: in the best form and the most beautiful shape and the most balanced.

After that: ﴿and provided you with good things﴾ [Ghafir: 64], which is for sustaining life with food. But He did not mention here marriage, by which the species is preserved; He gave us a glimpse here and left the other for another place, so that no place in His Book is devoid of a miracle in His creation.

﴿So blessed is Allah, the Lord of the worlds﴾ [Ghafir: 64]: that is, He is exalted and sanctified, and blessing comes from Him, and bounty comes from Him, and provision comes from Him.

The word (tabaraka) has taken its share in the Book of God. We find it for material, sensory matters, and we find it for spiritual matters and for the method that God has laid down for the proper movement of life. God has given you the physical body, and He has given you the soul by which this body lives.

Commentary of al-Sha'rawi (Tafsir al-Sha'rawi, surahs 1–53, fragments of 54–66) on surah 40, verse 65:

His saying, the Exalted: ﴿He is the Living﴾. It is as if all the attributes of perfection, in their origin, exist through life, so that power cannot exist except through life, nor hearing except through life, nor sight except through life. The word (al-Hayy, the Living) means that Allah, the Exalted, is not among the things that are subject to change (al-aghyar), for you have a existence and a life bound to that existence, whereas the Truth, glory be to Him, is living through His own essence. Al-Hayy is an attribute of His essence, and al-Muhyi (the Giver of Life) is an attribute of His act. Since al-Hayy is an attribute of the essence, what belongs to the essence does not fail; so He is living, that is, He does not die. But the attribute al-Muhyi has its opposite, al-Mumit (the Causer of Death); so He gives life to this one and causes that one to die.

Therefore they said: the name that has an opposite is an attribute of act, and the name that has no opposite is an attribute of essence. In praising Him, glory be to Him, they say: "O Living," an attribute of His essence, and "O Giver of Life," an attribute of His act; what belongs to the essence does not perish, and what belongs to the act lives and dies.

And since He, glory be to Him, is Living, and there is no god but Him, ﴿so call upon Him, sincere to Him in religion﴾. That means: when you call upon Him, let nothing else be in your mind; if nothing else is in your mind when you call upon Him, He is with you and responds to you.

Yes, ﴿so call upon Him﴾, because He is al-Qayyum (the Self-Subsisting Sustainer). He says to you: sleep and rest, for your Lord is al-Qayyum who does not slumber: ﴿Neither drowsiness nor sleep seizes Him﴾ [al-Baqarah: 255]. It is as if He, glory be to Him, is showing tenderness to whoever believes in Him: ﴿so call upon Him, sincere to Him in religion﴾. So beware of saying: "I have relied upon Allah and upon you," or "I have relied upon Allah and then upon you." All of this is false; seek sufficiency in Allah, and Allah is sufficient as a Guardian (wakil).

When you call upon Him, sincere to Him in religion, you have placed your affair in the hand of One who alone has the power to act, not in the hand of one who cannot. Then notice in the matter of supplication that your Lord gave you and responded to you before you called, indeed before you knew the supplication, indeed He gave you before you even existed. So all that He wants from you is to show the humility of servitude before the might of Lordship.

﴿Praise be to Allah, Lord of the worlds﴾. That means: praise Allah, who has graced you with all these blessings from the beginning: He brought you into existence from non-existence and sustained you from nothingness, until your journey ends in Paradise, God willing. Therefore, when we enter Paradise we say what He, glory be to Him, said: ﴿And the last of their call will be: Praise be to Allah, Lord of the worlds﴾ [Yunus: 10].

(قل) The address is to our master, the Messenger of God (ﷺ): "Say..." 
﴿Say: "I have been forbidden to worship those whom you call upon besides God."﴾ That is: the matter is not from me; it is rather a prohibition from God that came to me in clear, manifest verses. ﴿And I have been commanded to submit to the Lord of the worlds.﴾ That is: I submit my leadership and my affair to the Lord of the worlds, glory be to Him.

Yes, because a person among us, even in the worldly affairs of people, when he does not know how to do something and his means fail him, turns to someone who can fulfil his need and is capable of it, just as we go, for example, to the lawyer to file a case, or to the doctor for treatment, and so on. This is because you cannot defend yourself before the judge, and you cannot treat your illness yourself. So when you go to one of these people, there is no doubt that you hand over to him the reins of your affair and entrust him to do what he sees as good, without debating with him or objecting to him.

Thus, the meaning of ﴿I have been commanded to submit to the Lord of the worlds﴾ is: handing over the reins from one who is incapable of something to one who is capable of that thing. So when your Lord commands you a command, take the command from the standpoint of your faith in Him. How? He said: like my situation with the doctor when he prescribes for me the medicine suited to my condition: I do not debate with him about it, and I do not say to him, "Why did you prescribe this and leave that?" Even when I am asked about the medicine, I say: "By God, the doctor prescribed it for me," and I place the responsibility and accountability upon him.

If you hand over your affair and your reins to the doctor, who is a human being like you who errs and is right, because you see in him a wisdom above your wisdom and a knowledge that you do not have, how do you do this with him and not do it with God, the Mighty and Wise, the All-Powerful?

So: what your Lord commands you, comply with the command and carry it out without debate, objection, or resentment at what He has decreed for you. The Truth, glory be to Him, teaches us the lesson of submission to Him in the story of our master Abraham, peace be upon him, and how he submitted his face and handed over the reins of his affair to his Lord, may He be exalted, when He commanded him to slaughter his son Isma'il, who was granted to him only in old age and after despair. Therefore he said: ﴿Praise be to God, who has granted me, in old age, Isma'il and Isaac﴾ [Ibrahim: 39]...

As for His saying ﴿I have been forbidden to worship those whom you call upon besides God﴾, it is a prohibition because He loves him (the Messenger). So He said to him: direct your worship to the One who is able to act for you. This advice comes only from one who loves, just as you advise your friend and point him to good; and had you not loved him, you would not have advised him.

As for His saying ﴿And I have been commanded to submit to the Lord of the worlds﴾: I submit my leadership and the reins of my movement in life to my Lord; I do what He commands me to do, and I refrain from what He forbids me. As for a matter about which He was silent and did not tell me "do" or "do not," I place it in the category of the permissible, even if it were a matter that ordinary souls recoil from.

And even if He judges you with a judgment in which you see an apparent hardship upon yourself, know that He wants good for you from where you do not know, as we said in the story of our master Abraham, peace be upon him...

So: in submitting to God you do not take the act for its own sake, but together with the one who commands it, the Commander.

The Exalted turns us back once more to the matter of the first creation: ﴿It is He who created you from dust..﴾ [Ghafir: 67]. It is known that we have two creations: a creation from dust, when Allah created Adam and Hawwa' (Eve), and a creation from the offspring that proceeded from them.

Notice that Allah said ﴿from dust..﴾ [Ghafir: 67], and said ﴿from clay..﴾ [al-An'am: 2], and ﴿from black mud molded (ḥama' masnun)﴾ [al-Hijr: 26], and said ﴿from clay like pottery (ṣalṣāl)﴾ [al-Rahman: 14]. These are all stages of one thing. Dust, when we put water on it, becomes clay (ṭīn). If we leave it for a period, it rots and its smell changes, and this is the ḥama' masnun (molded black mud). If we leave it to dry, it becomes ṣalṣāl (dried clay that rings like pottery).

The saying of the Exalted, ﴿It is He who created you from dust..﴾ [Ghafir: 67], does not mean only our forefather Adam. Rather, all of us are from dust, even those who were created through marriage and procreation. Why? Because the microbe from which the male sperm cell and the female ovum will arise comes from the food we eat, and food is taken either from plants or from animals, and the origin of plants and animals is the dust of the earth.

For this reason, we have seen in the chemical analysis of the elements of the human being that they are the same elements as those of the dust, namely the sixteen known elements. So the fact that man was created from clay has a material proof known to us now. Therefore, we are all from dust, even if we came from a pair. Thus, the Prophet (ﷺ) said: Therefore, when the Exalted spoke of creation, He said: ﴿I did not make them witness the creation of the heavens and the earth, nor the creation of themselves..﴾ [al-Kahf: 51], because the creation of the heavens and the earth precedes the creation of man, and man is a later arrival upon them. When Adam was created, he had no discernment by which he could know how he was created.

Then comes the Exalted with words that show the miraculous nature of the Qur'an and the silencing of the obstinate. He says: ﴿And I would not take the misleaders as helpers.﴾ [al-Kahf: 51]

That is: I did not take them as assistants or as helpers to me in the process of creation. The "misleaders" (al-muḍillūn) are those who lead people astray and present falsehood in the garb of truth. What is meant by the misleaders here are those who mislead in the matter of creation, like those who say to us now that man, in his original creation, was a monkey and evolved, as Darwin said.

But the Exalted cuts off their path to misguidance and says to them: You did not witness the creation so that you could inform people about it. I am the Creator alone, and no one was with Me who knows what happened. So if you want to know how creation occurred, listen to Me, and I will inform you of it. Allah has informed us of it in many verses in His Book.

If you say: this is a matter that Allah has informed us of and we did not witness it, we say: reflect on the reality of life, for it indicates the truthfulness of Allah in what He said. You have not seen creation, but you have seen its opposite, which is death, and the undoing of a thing comes in the reverse of its building. For example, when you build a house of four stories, you begin with the first floor, but if you want to demolish it, you demolish the fourth.

Likewise death: it begins with the departure of the soul, which is the last thing in the creation of man. After the soul departs, the body stiffens, then it decays and changes like a carcass, then the water in it evaporates, then what remains dissolves into dust. Thus death came to confirm what was hidden from you at the beginning of creation.

His saying: ﴿from dust, then from a drop (nuṭfa), then from a clinging clot ('alaqa), then He brings you out as infants (ṭifl), then that you may reach your full strength (ashudd), then that you may become elders..﴾ [Ghafir: 67] These are stages of creation. ﴿Then He brings you out as infants..﴾ [Ghafir: 67]. They said: he is an infant as long as he is in the stages of growth. When he attains his proportion and takes his final form and settles into a complete shape, he has reached the stage of puberty (bulūgh), in which he completes all the faculties of existence, because by puberty he has become able to beget the like of himself.

The Exalted says: ﴿When the children among you reach puberty, let them ask permission as those before them asked..﴾ [al-Nur: 59]. So childhood is the stage of growth, and the stage of puberty is the full strength (ashudd). ﴿Then that you may reach your full strength..﴾ [Ghafir: 67], that is, your power. ﴿Then that you may become elders..﴾ [Ghafir: 67], that is, you descend again from strength to weakness and to old age, which is a stage of frailty and emaciation of the body.

When the stage of growth and increase ends, the stage of weakness and emaciation begins. In the stage of growth, you find that what enters him of food is more than what leaves him of waste, so he increases. But in the stage of old age, the waste becomes more, so he suffers loss and emaciation. His strength begins to decline, his muscles to waste away, until he reaches the last store in the body, which is the bones, and they become brittle and break because of what has been absorbed from them.

For this reason our master Zakariyya said: ﴿My Lord, indeed my bones have weakened and my head has glistened with white hair..﴾ [Maryam: 4]. He mentioned the last of the stages of old age, which is the weakening of the bones. This is on the material, bodily side. As for memory and intangible things, forgetfulness overtakes him, as the Exalted said: ﴿so that he knows nothing after having known..﴾ [al-Hajj: 5]. Forgetfulness reaches him until it is as if he had known nothing in his life. Then you see him crawling and being carried as children are carried: ﴿And whomever We grant long life, We reverse him in creation. Will they not reason?﴾ [Ya-Sin: 68].

His saying: ﴿and among you is he who is taken before..﴾ [Ghafir: 67] means: among you is he whom death hurries, so he does not reach these stages. A person may die in his mother's womb, or after his birth, or in his childhood. ﴿and that you may reach a specified term..﴾ [Ghafir: 67].

So the term differs and is written with Allah. Among us is he whose life is a moment, and he whose life is minutes, and he whose life is hours, and he whose life is days or months. And among creatures is he who does not reach the completion of the stages of creation, so he is taken while still a clot or a lump of flesh and his creation is not completed.

His saying: ﴿so that you may reason.﴾ [Ghafir: 67] means: understand that when Allah gives you full strength and you reach the stage of power, it is not inherent in you; rather, it is a gift given to you, and every blessment you have is a gift, not something inherent. It can be taken from you at any moment. Since you have known that it is a gift and that it may be taken from you at any time, then keep your good manners with the One who has granted you these blessings.

We have learned that a human being, in his creation, passes through several stages, and that his lifespan is uncertain; he may die at any one of these stages. So how are we to understand His saying, exalted is He, ﴿Be, and it is﴾ [Ghafir: 68], in relation to someone whose life is, for example, a single moment, or to someone who dies in his mother's womb?

They said: "Kun" (Be) here is said to what a human being is at that moment, whether a clinging clot (ʿalaqah), a lump of flesh (mudghah), or something else; it is as though He is saying to him: "Be alive." Then life is taken from him according to its law at its appointed times, which none knows but Allah.

Commentary of al-Sha'rawi (Tafsir al-Sha'rawi, surahs 1–53, fragments of 54–66) on surah 40, verses 69–70:

We have said: they dispute concerning the signs of Allah, and these are of three kinds: cosmic signs, such as the sun and the moon; the miraculous signs that accompany the sending of the messengers; and the signs of the Qur'an, which carry the rulings (ahkam). We have seen that they disputed concerning the miracles, saying of them: "Sorcery." And they said: "Trickery (sha'wadhah)." They disputed concerning the verses of rulings and said: "They are not suitable." As for the cosmic signs, they are not a subject of dispute.

His saying: ﴿Whence are they turned away?﴾ [Ghafir: 69], meaning: they are turned away from the truth, which is clear. Where, then, are their thinking minds? ﴿Those who denied the Book and that with which We sent Our messengers; they will come to know﴾ [Ghafir: 70]. He said: ﴿denied﴾ [Ghafir: 70] in the past tense, but in the recompense he said ﴿they will come to know﴾ [Ghafir: 70].

That is, in the future. They said: because the recompense does not necessarily have to occur at the same time, or while they are still existing in the expanse of worldly life; it is valid that the recompense be deferred for them to the Hereafter.

The word "sawfa" (will) indicates the future, whether near in this world or distant in the Hereafter. So if the punishment does not overtake them in this world, it awaits them in the Hereafter, as Allah the Exalted says: ﴿So whether We show you some of what We promise them, or We take you in death, to Us they will be returned﴾ [Ghafir: 77].

Allah, glory be to Him, wishes to connect us to Himself constantly, such that nothing else comes to our minds. This connection makes you, when things come to you, not think that you have obtained them by your own essence; rather, they are bestowed upon you, and the Bestower has the right to take back His gift.

Therefore He warns us, saying: ﴿Nay, indeed man transgresses, when he sees himself self-sufficient﴾ [al-Alaq: 6–7], then He says after it: ﴿Indeed, to your Lord is the return﴾ [al-Alaq: 8], meaning: remember your return to Him and your standing before Him.

His saying "the Book" means: that which Allah sent down, carrying His method. ﴿And that with which We sent Our messengers﴾ [Ghafir: 70], meaning: upon the tongues of His messengers. If you say the Book is what We sent with Our messengers, we say: no, there is a difference. The Book is the method, whereas the Messenger was sent carrying the method, conveying it, and as a model of applying that same method, as Allah the Exalted says: ﴿Indeed, in the Messenger of Allah you have an excellent example﴾ [al-Ahzab: 21].

Al-Sha'rawi on surah 40, verses 71–72:

That is: ﴿They will come to know﴾ [Ghafir: 70] — when? On the Day of Resurrection, ﴿when the shackles are around their necks and the chains; they will be dragged﴾ [Ghafir: 71]. Reflect on the extent of the humiliation they are in ﴿in the scalding water, then in the Fire they will be burned﴾ [Ghafir: 72].

Al-aghlal (shackles) is the plural of ghull, which are restraints placed on the hands and joined to the neck. As-salasil (the chains) are of iron, with which the feet are bound. What greater humiliation is there after this?

The meaning of al-hamim is the water whose heat has reached its extreme, meaning it has reached the utmost degree of heat. Then after that they will be set aflame in the Fire, meaning they will be heated up by means of them, and they will become fuel for it.

Consider this rebuke of the polytheists in this dreadful situation: "Where are your partners whom you associated with Allah? Call upon them, let them ward off this punishment from you! By Allah, if they worshipped beings like themselves, they will see them having preceded them into the Fire; and if they worshipped stones, they will see them before them as fuel for Hell."

So they will say: ﴿They have strayed from us...﴾ [Ghafir: 74], meaning: they did not guide us to them, nor did they know our path. Then they see that the situation is greater than their partners, so they lie, ﴿Nay, we used to call upon nothing before.﴾ [Ghafir: 74]. Glory be to Allah, they lie even in this situation, just as they had previously sworn by Allah that they had not associated anyone: ﴿They said, "By Allah, our Lord, we were not polytheists."﴾ [al-An'am: 23].

Therefore Allah, the Exalted, describes these liars: ﴿And they used to persist in the great violation.﴾ [al-Waqi'ah: 46]. In other words, they had become accustomed to lying, such that the moment of reckoning did not deter them from it, so they say: ﴿We used to call upon nothing before.﴾ [Ghafir: 74], meaning: we did not associate anyone with Allah. It may be that they are truthful in this, because they did not call upon these deities, since they knew that they neither harm nor benefit; they worshipped them only to satisfy their desire for religiosity, with deities that have neither a method nor obligations.

﴿Thus Allah leads astray the disbelievers.﴾ [Ghafir: 74]. Indeed, the Truth does not lead astray any person; rather, He leads astray only the one who disbelieves. How can Allah guide one who has disbelieved? We have previously given an example for this, and to Allah belongs the highest likeness: we said that a traffic policeman, for instance, when you ask him about the way, guides you; but if you object to him and do not obey him, or you mock his opinion and say to him, "You do not know this place," he leaves you and abandons your guidance. But if you submit to his opinion and thank him for his kindness toward you, he says to you, "But by Allah, ahead of you there, at a distance of such-and-such kilometers, is a steep pass or a diversion; I will go with you until you pass through it." So he guided him first by indication, and when he showed gratitude, he became deserving of his assistance.

Likewise, Allah, Glorified and Exalted, says: ﴿And those who are guided, He increases them in guidance and gives them their piety.﴾ [Muhammad: 17]. And here: ﴿Thus Allah leads astray the disbelievers.﴾ [Ghafir: 74], that is, those who do not deserve guidance. Therefore we have said that whoever loves disbelief, inclines toward it, and chooses it for himself, Allah says to him: "I am the Lord; I give you what you desire. Since you have loved disbelief, I will help you in it and seal your heart, so that faith does not enter it and disbelief does not leave it."
