That is (a reference to) what befell them of punishment with the shackles, the chains and the Fire; its cause is: ﴿because you used to exult in the land without right, and because you used to be insolent﴾.

Al-farah (exultation): the expansion of the soul with what delights and makes it happy. But true joy (al-farah al-haqiqi) is to be made happy and delighted by what helps it reach its original purpose. There is joy in anything, perhaps even in sin, and there is joy in what is right, which is to rejoice in what helps you reach your goal. As for the thing that does not help you toward this goal, but rather collides with it, it is a passing pleasure followed by regrets that may exceed many times over the pleasure that was gained from it.

Consider, as an example of true joy, His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿And do not think of those who have been killed in the cause of Allah as dead. Rather, they are alive with their Lord, receiving provision, [Rejoicing in what Allah has given them of His bounty]﴾ [Aal-Imran: 169-170].

Yes, this is joy in truth, and it even extends to others: ﴿and rejoicing in favor from Allah and bounty and that Allah does not allow to be lost the reward of the believers. Those who responded to Allah and the Messenger after injury had struck them﴾... [Aal-Imran: 170]. Then ﴿and they rejoice for those who have not yet joined them from behind them, that there will be no fear concerning them, nor will they grieve﴾ [Aal-Imran: 170]. This is joy that reaches beyond you to others, true joy, because it achieves the original purpose of existence.

Among this also is His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿Say, "In the bounty of Allah and in His mercy—in that let them rejoice; it is better than what they accumulate"﴾ [Yunus: 58]. This is joy in the bounty and mercy of Allah, not in their own deeds, and this is lawful joy.

From lawful joy also: ﴿And those to whom We gave the Scripture rejoice in what has been revealed to you﴾ [al-Ra'd: 36], because it came confirming what is with them and supporting their stance upon the truth. You rejoice in this because it helps you toward the original purpose of existence.

And He, Exalted is He, says: ﴿Alif, Lam, Mim. The Romans have been defeated, in the nearest land. But they, after their defeat, will overcome, within three to nine years. The command is with Allah, before and after. And that Day the believers will rejoice in the victory of Allah﴾... [al-Rum: 1-5]. So how many kinds of lawful joy are there? The joy of the martyrs in the bounty and mercy of Allah, the joy of those given the Scripture in the Messenger of Allah, and the joy of the believers in the victory of the method of heaven over the method of earth.

Apart from lawful joy, there is foolish joy. Among it is His saying, Exalted is He, about the disbelievers: ﴿If good befalls you, it distresses them; but if a misfortune strikes you, they say, "We had already taken our precaution before," and they turn away while they are rejoicing. Say, "Never will we be struck except by what Allah has decreed for us"﴾ [al-Tawbah: 50-51]. That is, what befalls us from Allah is counted for us, not against us.

And He said: ﴿If good touches you, it distresses them; but if an affliction strikes you, they rejoice in it. And if you are patient and mindful of Allah, their plotting will not harm you at all. Indeed, Allah is encompassing of what they do﴾ [Aal-Imran: 120].

And He, Exalted is He, also said about unlawful or foolish joy, as we have said: ﴿So when they forgot what they had been reminded of, We opened to them the doors of all things until, when they rejoiced in what they had been given, We seized them suddenly﴾ [al-An'am: 44].

And He said: ﴿Do not think that those who rejoice in what they have done...﴾ [Aal-Imran: 188], meaning they rejoice that they harmed the believers and mocked them, ﴿and love to be praised for what they have not done—do not think them safe from the punishment, and for them is a painful punishment﴾ [Aal-Imran: 188].

And He said: ﴿And if We let man taste mercy from Us and then We withdraw it from him, indeed, he is despairing and ungrateful. But if We let him taste blessing after adversity has touched him, he will surely say, "The evils have left me," indeed, he is exultant and boastful﴾ [Hud: 9-10].

And He said: ﴿Then they divided their affair among themselves into sects, each faction rejoicing in what it has﴾ [al-Mu'minun: 53].

Since the factions have multiplied, and each rejoices in what it has, this is vain joy that is not lawful.

And He also said: ﴿Indeed, Qarun was of the people of Moses, but he oppressed them. And We had given him treasures whose keys would surely burden a company of strong men. When his people said to him, "Do not exult; indeed, Allah does not love the exultant"﴾ [al-Qasas: 76].

So: there is lawful joy in four places, and in nine places there is joy that is not praiseworthy and not lawful.

Here He, Exalted is He, says: ﴿That is because you used to exult in the land without right﴾ [Ghafir: 75]. This is evidence that there is joy in the truth and joy in what is not the truth, ﴿and because you used to be insolent﴾ [Ghafir: 75]. Al-marah (insolence): excessive exultation, and proceeding with it in arrogance, boastfulness and conceit.

Commentary of al-Sha'rawi (Tafsir al-Sha'rawi, surahs 1-53, fragments of 54-66) on surah 40, verse 76:

﴿مَثْوَى﴾ means place of return and abode. ﴿ٱلْمُتَكَبِّرِينَ﴾ refers to those who were arrogant towards God, who gave them life, and yet did not believe in Him. These are the ones who were arrogant towards God and so did not believe in Him, arrogant towards His messengers and so did not affirm them, and arrogant towards His method and so did not act by it. They chose their own desires and handed over their reins to them, instead of handing them over to God.

After that, He turns to His Messenger ﷺ and says to him: You will face many hardships that require patience from you, because your mission is arduous, and you will be harmed in every kind of way:

﴿So be patient. Indeed, the promise of God is true. And whether We show you some of what We promise them...﴾.

Yes. "Indeed, the promise of Allah is true..." [Ghafir: 77]: that is, His promise to support His messengers is true, because He, may He be exalted, is able to fulfil His promise. We have explained the difference between your promise and the promise of Allah: your promise is not necessarily true, because you do not possess the means to fulfil it and guarantee it. As for the True One, glory be to Him, He has the attributes of perfection, and nothing prevents Him from fulfilling His promise.

And His saying: "So whether We show you part of what We promise them..." [Ghafir: 77], that is, of the punishment in this world. "Or We cause you to die..." [Ghafir: 77], before you see a sign among them. "Then to Us they will be returned" [Ghafir: 77], that is, in the Hereafter, where they cannot escape the punishment. For this reason, He, may He be exalted, said: "And We will surely make them taste a punishment lesser than the greater punishment, that perhaps they will return" [As-Sajdah: 21].

The lesser punishment is what befalls them in this world, and the greater punishment is on the Day of Resurrection; meaning, they have no escape.

Then, glory be to Him, clarifies to His Prophet (ﷺ) the reality of the message. He says to him: Know, O Muhammad, that you are not an innovation among the messengers, and you are not the first to be harmed in the cause of his call. Every one of your brothers who preceded you in the procession of messages was harmed according to the measure of his message. Therefore, you are the most harmed of them, because you are the Prophet of the last age, and your message is general for all people in every time and place, so your trial must necessarily be more severe than those who preceded you.

He, glory be to Him, says:

"And We had certainly sent messengers before you; among them are those whom We have related to you..." [Ghafir: 78].

Yes, the Exalted One mentioned to His Messenger, peace and blessings be upon him, the names of some of the prophets, and their number in the Qur'an is twenty-five. The versifier said:

"Among them, in that proof of ours, are eight, and after ten, seven remain; and they are:
Idris, Hud, Shu'ayb, Salih, Dhu'l-Kifl, Adam, and with the Chosen One they are sealed."

However, the Exalted One says in another place: ﴿And there is not a nation but that a warner has passed among them﴾ [Fatir: 24], and this means that those prophets who were not mentioned are many. ﴿And it was not for a messenger to bring a sign except by permission of Allah...﴾ [al-Ra'd: 38]. What is the relevance of this here? They said: because they used to propose signs to him, as the Exalted One says: ﴿And they say, "We will not believe you until you cause a spring to gush forth for us from the earth, or you have a garden of palms and grapes and cause rivers to burst forth within it in force"﴾ [al-Isra': 90-91], meaning: so that this garden may remain. ﴿Or you cause the sky to fall upon us in fragments as you have claimed, or you bring Allah and the angels before us as a guarantee. Or you have a house of gold, or you ascend into the sky. And we will not believe in your ascension until you bring down to us a book we can read...﴾ [al-Isra': 92-93]. So what was his answer? ﴿Say, "Exalted is my Lord! Was I but a human messenger?"﴾ [al-Isra': 93], meaning: I am only a messenger from Allah, conveying what I was sent with.

The Exalted One has made clear to us, when He does not grant them what they asked for of signs, that they did not content themselves with what they already had and were not satisfied with it. Thus, seeking signs after that is considered a disparagement of the previous verse. This is one point. Also, there are people who asked for signs, Allah granted them, and yet they disbelieved in them. Therefore, my compliance with them in seeking signs is futile and of no benefit. For this reason the Exalted One said: ﴿And nothing prevented Us from sending the signs except that the former peoples denied them...﴾ [al-Isra': 59], meaning: the signs that were demanded.

As for the saying of the Exalted One: ﴿So when the command of Allah comes, it will be judged with truth, and the falsifiers will lose therein﴾ [Ghafir: 78]. The meaning of ﴿it will be judged with truth...﴾ [Ghafir: 78] is: since the judgment is by truth, the believers have succeeded and ﴿the falsifiers will lose therein...﴾ [Ghafir: 78], meaning: in the Hereafter. ﴿Al-mubtilun﴾ [Ghafir: 78] are the disbelievers, the people of falsehood. This is the natural conclusion and the recompense is of the same kind as the deed.

﴿الْأَنْعَامَ﴾ [Ghafir: 79] are: camels, cattle, sheep, and goats, and these have a particular function. ﴿لِتَرْكَبُوا مِنْهَا..﴾ [Ghafir: 79] means: some of them are ridden, namely camels, so we do not ride a lamb, for example. ﴿وَمِنْهَا تَأْكُلُونَ﴾ [Ghafir: 79] means: their meat. ﴿وَلَكُمْ فِيهَا مَنَافِعُ..﴾ [Ghafir: 80] means: other benefits besides riding and eating, such as benefiting from their hides, wool, and fur. They used to make from them clothing, coverings, furnishings, tents, and so on.

Consider here the magnificence of the Qur'anic expression. For riding, He said: ﴿لِتَرْكَبُوا مِنْهَا..﴾ [Ghafir: 79], and for eating, He said: ﴿وَمِنْهَا تَأْكُلُونَ﴾ [Ghafir: 79]. They said: because eating is among the permissible matters, whereas riding is among the necessities.

And His saying: ﴿وَلِتَبْلُغُوا عَلَيْهَا حَاجَةً فِي صُدُورِكُمْ..﴾ [Ghafir: 80] means: they carry you to your need, for example in travel for the Hajj (pilgrimage) or for trade and carrying loads. ﴿وَعَلَيْهَا وَعَلَى الْفُلْكِ تُحْمَلُونَ﴾ [Ghafir: 80] means: upon them (the livestock) and upon the ships you are carried, because we ride them and place loads upon them.

As for ﴿عَلَى الْفُلْكِ..﴾ [Ghafir: 80], it means: the ships. It is well known that we ride in the ship, as the Exalted said concerning the ship of our master Nuh (peace be upon him): ﴿قُلْنَا احْمِلْ فِيهَا..﴾ [Hud: 40], and He did not say "upon it." How so? They said: because the Truth, glorified is He, seems to give us the stages through which shipbuilding passes and how to benefit from them. The ship of Nuh was the first ship, so it was in a simple form, and Allah, glorified is He, wanted to teach us that shipbuilding would develop, and that ships would have different decks, so we ride within them.

For this reason, in San Francisco we asked them about these giant ships: when were they built? They did not know the exact year. One of those present said: consider it to be a century ago, for example. I said: yes, and in the Noble Qur'an there is a report about them and an precise description of them: they are wide at the bottom and narrow with each deck upward, so you see them giant upon the surface of the water like a mountain.

How then does the Truth, glorified is He, say in His Qur'an, while enumerating His blessings upon us, in Surat al-Rahman: ﴿وَلَهُ الْجَوَارِ الْمُنْشَآتُ فِي الْبَحْرِ كَالْأَعْلَامِ﴾ [al-Rahman: 24], meaning: like mountains? It is well known that Muhammad (ﷺ) never sailed the sea and never saw such giant ships. It is evidence of the truthfulness of Muhammad (ﷺ) in conveying from his Lord.

Then tell me: when were these elevators and these modern lifts made? They said: fifty years ago, for example. I said: the Truth, glorified is He, says in the Noble Qur'an: ﴿وَلَوْلَا أَن يَكُونَ النَّاسُ أُمَّةً وَاحِدَةً لَّجَعَلْنَا لِمَن يَكْفُرُ بِالرَّحْمَٰنِ لِبُيُوتِهِمْ سُقُفًا مِّن فِضَّةٍ وَمَعَارِجَ عَلَيْهَا يَظْهَرُونَ﴾ [al-Zukhruf: 33].

Ma'arij means: lifts like those you have fifty years ago; Allah informed us of them more than fourteen centuries ago.

All of these are snapshots from the Book of Allah, which the Truth, glorified is He, mentioned to be evidence of its inimitability: ﴿سَنُرِيهِمْ آيَاتِنَا فِي الْآفَاقِ وَفِي أَنفُسِهِمْ حَتَّىٰ يَتَبَيَّنَ لَهُمْ أَنَّهُ الْحَقُّ..﴾ [Fussilat: 53].

Commentary of al-Sha'rawi (Tafsir al-Sha'rawi, surahs 1-53, fragments of 54-66) on surah 40, verse 81:

He means ﴿His signs﴾ in these creatures, and His signs in the sea when you ride the ships and see other worlds in the sea, signs greater than what you see on land. Now, after the scientific progress that has taken place, we have seen them make windows of glass for ships beneath the surface of the water, and make glass vessels that enable you to see the depths and what they contain of the marvellous creation of God and His signs that point to His power, to the point that you say: Glory be to God, how can the disbeliever disbelieve after seeing these worlds?

Likewise, when you ride camels on land and travel with them across distances, you see many of God's signs in His creation: in the camel you ride, in the desert, and in the mountains you pass by. In everything around you there is a sign. Therefore you find that the Truthful, Exalted One asks us to travel through the earth.

So He, glorified is He, says: ﴿Say: Travel through the earth and see...﴾ [An-Naml: 69].

And He, glorified is He, says in another place: ﴿Say: Travel through the earth, then see...﴾ [Al-An'am: 11].

So travelling through the earth serves two purposes: travelling through the earth for reflection (fa-unzuru, "then see") and travelling through the earth for trade and investment. He said to you: travel through the earth and seek provision and investment, but do not deprive yourselves of the pleasure of reflection and contemplation of the marvellous creation of God. So He said: ﴿Say: Travel through the earth, then see...﴾ [Al-An'am: 11]. It is well known that the fa (فاء) denotes sequence and immediacy, while thumma (ثم) denotes sequence with a delay.

As for His saying: ﴿Which then of the signs of God will you deny?﴾ [Ghafir: 81], it means: these signs that you see, which of them will you deny, and how can you deny them when they are clear in their indication of God's power? As He, glorified is He, said in Surat al-Rahman (the Surah of Blessings): ﴿Then which of the blessings of your Lord will you both deny?﴾ [Ar-Rahman: 13]. The Truthful, Exalted One repeated it after each of the blessings, and the meaning is that these are signs that should not be denied, nor should they be rejected.

Therefore the Prophet (ﷺ) said to his Companions: [the text here is cut off in the source]

He used the form (أي) for the masculine, although (آيات) is feminine and he did not say (آية). They said: because it is a metaphorical feminine that came in the plural form, so the masculine is permissible for it, as in His saying, exalted is He: ﴿So when he saw the sun rising, he said: This is my Lord...﴾ [Al-An'am: 78], where he said "this" although the sun is feminine.

This is a journey, as we have said, for the purpose of taking lessons (i'tibar, drawing a moral lesson). The lesson here is drawn from the nations that came before them. Allah, glory be to Him, shows them that those nations which denied the truth before you were greater in number than you, mightier in strength, and more far-reaching in their traces upon the earth. The "traces" (athar) are what a people leave behind them, like the pyramids in relation to the Pharaohs, which Allah preserves as a witness against them.

There are other traces that we have not seen because they are buried, but Allah has informed us of them, as in His saying: ﴿Have you not considered how your Lord dealt with 'Ad, Iram of the pillars, the like of which had not been created in the lands?﴾ [al-Fajr: 6-8]. These are lasting traces. ﴿And indeed, you pass by them in the morning, and at night. Will you not then reason?﴾ [al-Saffat: 137-138].

So where are you, O Arabs, from these vanished civilizations? You should have learned the lesson from those earlier peoples who denied the messengers and opposed them. Allah seized them while they were stronger than you and mightier, and He granted victory to His messengers and His method. You are far below them, and you will never escape Allah's power; rather, your matter is even easier.

As for His saying: ﴿So what they used to earn did not avail them at all﴾ [Ghafir: 82], it means: these civilizations and this architecture, which is considered a marvel whose secret we have not reached until now, did not benefit their owners.

Let us speak, for example, of their traces in Egypt. We have the monuments of the Pharaohs in the temples and in the pyramids. We have seen the colours on the walls still intact, as if they had been carved in modern times. We have seen some grains that, they say, are still fit to germinate after these thousands of years, and you know the secrets of the construction of the pyramids that we have not yet come to understand.

All this advancement, its people were not able to protect it, nor were they able to preserve this civilization, nor even to leave us anything that explains it. Had it not been for Champollion, who deciphered for us the symbols of the Rosetta Stone, we would not have been able to reach this history or know it.

... His saying: "They rejoiced in what knowledge they had" (فَرِحُواْ بِمَا عِندَهُمْ مِّنَ الْعِلْمِ). This is a kind of the rejoicing we mentioned earlier, and we said that it is not legitimate, a foolish rejoicing. The meaning is: they rejoiced in what knowledge they had, with which they dispute against the Qur'an, like their saying: "There is nothing but our life of this world; we die and we live, and nothing destroys us except time" [al-Jathiyah: 24]. Thus say the secularists (al-'ilmaniyyun), and like their saying: "If God had willed, we would not have associated [anything with Him]" [al-An'am: 148].

So every matter presented to them, they want to oppose it with an opposition in which they are convinced, despite its falsehood, and this is a kind of knowledge they have.

Or the meaning is: they rejoiced in what knowledge they had of the outward aspects of life and the civilizations they built, so they said: "We have no need of the messengers, because what we have of sciences, that is, the material ones, is sufficient." And we say: you looked at the superficialities of matters and at the things with which you justify your thinking, so you said: "If God had willed, we would not have associated [anything with Him]" [al-An'am: 148], meaning: you accuse God, and this is evidence that you want that...

As for the meaning of "they mock" (يَسْتَهْزِئُونَ), it is from the mockery (هُزْء) of falsehood against truth. Why? They said: because falsehood, when it sees truth, must push it away, for it must weaken the arm of whoever believes in it, because if it did not weaken his arm, it would draw him to the truth. That is why we have heard them say: "Do not listen to this Qur'an, and make noise during it, that perhaps you will overcome" [Fussilat: 26].

By God, if they did not know the sweetness of the Qur'an and how it takes hold of whoever hears it, and its dominion over the ears and hearts, and if they did not fear that the Qur'an would take away their leadership, they would not have said this word, nor would they have warned people against listening to them, and if it were ordinary speech they would not have taken this stance toward it. So: they understood that the Qur'an is true, and whoever hears it must be guided by it. And the meaning of "hearing it" here means: with its experiential reality (بمواجيده)...

This verse presents the same situation in which Pharaoh found himself when drowning overtook him: ﴿He said, "I believe that there is no deity except the one in whom the Children of Israel have believed, and I am of the Muslims."﴾ [Yunus: 90] So Allah replied to him: ﴿"Now? And you had disobeyed before and were among the corrupters."﴾ [Yunus: 91]

That is, your faith will not benefit you now. Hence there is a period in which one cannot return from disbelief to faith, and it is the moment when death encompasses a person. Faith is accepted only from one who is still at liberty in his affairs, when he believes while he has the capacity not to believe.

Likewise these people: ﴿So when they saw Our punishment...﴾ [Ghafir: 84], i.e., Our punishment descended upon them in this world, ﴿they said, "We believe in Allah alone, and we disbelieve in that which we used to associate with Him."﴾ [Ghafir: 84] Is this a time when faith from them would be accepted?

The Truth, glory be to Him, affirms: ﴿So their faith was not going to benefit them when they saw Our punishment...﴾ [Ghafir: 85], i.e., it was not proper, by the standard of reason or by the standard of truth, that this faith should benefit them. And how could it, when they no longer had any means of opposing the method of Allah, nor any strength? Now let them believe?

It was never fitting that this faith should benefit them, and this faith is according to their own assumption; otherwise it is false faith, rejected, having no meaning, because it comes at a time other than its time.

And this is ﴿the way of Allah which has already passed...﴾ [Ghafir: 85], i.e., it has gone by, ﴿among His servants...﴾ [Ghafir: 85]. We have seen this way throughout history: just as He seized peoples for their sins and did not accept their faith at the moment of their death-rattle or at the moment the punishment descended upon them, so too will you be treated, and this way will not change, for it is established: ﴿And you will not find any change in the way of Allah﴾ [al-Ahzab: 62], and the way of Allah will continue to operate upon all creation.

﴿And the disbelievers were lost there﴾ [Ghafir: 85]. This is the natural outcome and the end that they deserve.
